### FOMC — The Hawkish Shock That Wasn't Quite Scenario B

**Decision:** Rate held at 3.50%–3.75% (12–0 unanimous vote). **Fourth consecutive hold.**

**Dot Plot — The Shock:**
- **9 of 18 FOMC participants now project at least one 2026 rate hike** — a dramatic shift
  from the March dot plot (which leaned toward extended holds or cuts)
- Median fed funds rate end-2026: **3.8%** (up from 3.4% in March projections)
- 8 participants project no change; 1 projects a cut; 9 project a hike
- Traders now price the first hike could come as early as **October 2026**
- Kevin Warsh notably **did not submit his own dot plot forecast** — he is "data-dependent
  and forward guidance-free" as his communication approach

**Warsh Press Conference — First As Fed Chair:**
- FOMC statement removed all references to "additional rate adjustments"
- Warsh explicitly said "none of the Fed participants felt the need to raise rates today"
- Declined to give any forward guidance: "We're not going to tell you what we're going to do"
- Language tilt: **hawkish on process, neutral on immediate action**
- No explicit acknowledgment of the Iran deal's disinflationary oil price impact
- Announced **task forces to overhaul major Federal Reserve operations** — an unusual
  first-meeting administrative signal (accountability culture at the Fed)

**Market Reaction:**
- S&P 500: **−1.21%** (close near session lows)
- Nasdaq Composite: **−1.34%**
- 2-year Treasury yield: **jumped 16bps to 4.21%** — highest in over one year
- Stocks sold into the last hour after Warsh concluded remarks (2:30pm → 3pm weakness)
- Dow: **−0.8% (−410 points)**

**Portfolio verdict vs. the three pre-market scenarios:**

The June 17 pre-market report forecasted three scenarios. The outcome was a hybrid:
- The dot plot was unmistakably **Scenario B (Hawkish)** — 9 of 18 projecting hike
- BUT the market reaction was **between B and A** — the Nasdaq fell −1.34%, not −3% to −5%
- The difference: Warsh's language was ambiguous (he didn't hike, didn't threaten imminent
  action, and the "task force" announcement shifted some attention to Fed process reform)
- **Result:** Our five systematic sleeves escaped the tech selloff with +1.18%/+1.37%/
  +0.99%/+0.03%/−0.74% returns while SPY fell −1.25% — a clean alpha day despite the
  macro shock being realized exactly as feared.

**Key implication:** The quality filter (ROA) is the dominant protective factor in rate-shock
days. Higher-profitability companies (MU, STX, WDC, VRT, ARWR) rallied even as the broad
market fell because their fundamental earnings stories are not rate-dependent in the near term.

Sources: [CNBC (Fed holds rates June 2026)](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html), [CNN (Fed signals higher rates ahead)](https://www.cnn.com/2026/06/17/business/live-news/federal-reserve-interest-rate-kevin-warsh), [BeinCrypto (Warsh hawkish shock 9 FOMC)](https://beincrypto.com/warsh-hawkish-shock-rate-hike/), [TheStreet (S&P Nasdaq plummet June 17)](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-june-17-2026), [RSM (Fed tilts hawkish Warsh price stability)](https://realeconomy.rsmus.com/fed-tilts-hawkish-as-warsh-promises-price-stability/)

### CBOE — Structural Insight: The Options Market Share Narrative

CBOE's persistent decline (entry $285.24 → $254.69 today = **−10.71%**) surfaces an
important structural insight for the systematic model going forward.

The residual_roa strategy's ROA quality filter was designed to select companies with
high **idiosyncratic returns** weighted by profitability. CBOE was presumably selected
because it has:
1. High ROA (exchange businesses are capital-light)
2. Positive 12-1 momentum (options volumes surged with AI/meme stock activity in 2025)

**But the competitive dynamic has changed:** SpaceX's equity options launch attracted
massive order flow to NYSE, MIAX, and other exchanges simultaneously. Cboe's moat
(being the preferred venue for single-name equity options) is being eroded by:
- Multi-exchange simultaneous launch becoming standard (SpaceX is the highest-profile
  test case yet)
- SEC approval for expanded maker-taker rebates on rival platforms
- Cboe's own operational disruptions (20% RIF, Europe wind-down, office mandates)

**Lesson:** The ROA quality filter is excellent at identifying profitable businesses but
cannot anticipate competitive moat erosion from structural market structure changes (a
new exchange listing protocol). This type of risk is NOT captured by trailing ROA data.

A potential augmentation: add a **market share stability signal** to the quality factor
for exchange/financial infrastructure names (CBOE, ICE, CME, NDAQ). These businesses'
ROA is a function of market share × pricing power — both of which can deteriorate quickly.

performance is the strongest out-of-sample evidence that the quality augmentation of

#### Insight 3: The Warsh Policy Uncertainty Regime and Long-Horizon Alpha

Warsh's explicit removal of forward guidance ("we will not tell you what we're going
to do") creates a new policy uncertainty regime. Historical analysis of high policy
uncertainty periods suggests:

1. **Momentum factors historically OUTPERFORM** in high-uncertainty environments
   — because investors anchor on trend rather than discounted cash flow models
   (which become unreliable when the discount rate is unknown)
2. **Quality factors also outperform** — investors flee to companies with visible
   earnings (reducing DCF sensitivity to the uncertain rate path)
3. **Pure momentum without quality** (mom_v1, mom_v2) historically struggles in
   rate-shock environments because they hold speculative names alongside quality names
   → the quality filter is the differentiation

**Practical implication:** The Warsh uncertainty regime (no guidance, data-dependent,
dot plot signaling hike risk) is likely to persist through at least Q3 2026. This is
a supportive environment for mom_roa_6535 and residual_roa_6535 strategies.

### OVERNIGHT CATALYST #1: Apple-Intel Chip Partnership (+9% INTC Pre-Market)

**This is the largest single overnight catalyst for the portfolio since inception.**

On the evening of June 17, President Trump posted on Truth Social:
> *"Apple has agreed to work with Intel to design and build its Chips in America."*

**What was announced:**
- Apple and Intel have reached (or are near) a manufacturing agreement to produce
  Apple silicon chips on Intel's domestic US foundry nodes
- Intel's 18A-P process (an advancement of 18A) entered risk production on June 16,
  one day before the announcement — providing the technical readiness context
- The Wall Street Journal had earlier reported that Apple held exploratory discussions
  about using Intel to produce main processors in the US

**Pre-market reaction as of 8am ET June 18:**
- INTC: **+9.0% to ~$132.06** (from $121.10 close)
- MU: +4.8%
- AMD: +3.9%
- AVGO (Broadcom): +3.0%
- Nasdaq 100 futures: **+1.44%**
- S&P 500 futures: **+0.81%**

**Critical caveat:** Neither Apple nor Intel has issued an official press release
confirming the deal. The announcement came exclusively from Trump's Truth Social post.
Intel said its 18A-P process "entered risk production" but made no Apple-specific
statement. Markets are pricing on the Trump announcement; deal confirmation adds
further upside.

**Why this matters (if confirmed):** Intel's annual run rate is ~$53B. Winning
Apple's chip manufacturing business would roughly double Intel's foundry revenue and
transform Intel Foundry from a money-losing cost center into a profit-generating
external business. The deal validates Intel's IDM 2.0 strategy and the $13B+ CHIPS
Act investment in US semiconductor fabs.

### OVERNIGHT CATALYST #2: Apple CEO Cook — Memory Costs "Unsustainable" (MU +4.8% Pre-Market)

In an exclusive interview with The Wall Street Journal (published June 17 evening),
Apple outgoing CEO Tim Cook stated:

> *"We're doing our best to mitigate the huge increases that are being passed to us,
> and we've been trying to shield our customers from the increases, but the situation
> has become unsustainable."*

**What Cook said:**
- Price hikes across Apple's entire product lineup are now "unavoidable"
- The root cause: explosive demand for DRAM and NAND from AI data centers (Google,
  Microsoft, Meta, Amazon) is redirecting memory supply away from consumer devices
- Cook said Apple is willing to use its balance sheet to help increase supply but
  ruled out building its own memory factories
- TechInsights estimates: passing on higher costs while preserving margins could add
  **~$270 to the price of the next iPhone 18 Pro**

**Wall Street response — analyst upgrades overnight:**
- **Citi (Atif Malik):** Raised MU price target to **$1,200** (from $840)
- **Deutsche Bank (Melissa Weathers):** Raised MU price target to **$1,500** (from $1,000)
- **Citi memory team:** Projects DRAM prices up **+200%** in 2026; NAND prices +**186%**

**Pre-market reactions (8am ET, June 18):**
- MU: **+4.8% to ~$1,093.25**
- WDC: Expected +2–5% (retail sentiment "extremely bullish" on Stocktwits)
- STX: Expected +1–3% (retail sentiment "bullish")
- SNDK (SanDisk): Expected similar lift

**Why Apple's statement is structurally important:**
This is not an analyst projection — it is a first-person admission from the world's
largest consumer electronics company that memory scarcity is real and worsening.
Apple typically negotiates long-term supply contracts and hedges aggressively. When
Apple's CEO says costs are "unsustainable," it is a signal that:
1. Even locked-in supply contracts are being renegotiated at higher prices
2. The memory pricing floor is durable — consumer electronics cannot absorb more
   at current volumes
3. AI memory demand is NOT decelerating into H2 2026 (contradicting the "AI capex
   pause" bears)

This is the single most bullish independent data point for MU ahead of the June 24
earnings (now 6 days out).

### SATS (EchoStar) — CRITICAL: Grace Period Expires July 1

New information changes the SATS risk profile significantly.

**The AT&T deal timeline revision:**
The EchoStar 10-Q (filed for Q1 2026) reveals that the **final AT&T acquisition closing
is now targeted for November 30, 2027** — not mid-2026 as previously indicated. While
the spectrum transfer to an intermediary trust was completed May 22, 2026 (regulatory
approval received), the actual cash payment of ~$20.25B from AT&T to EchoStar does not
arrive until the 2027 final closing.

**The collision of timelines:**
- **June 1:** $183M interest payment deferred on DISH DBS notes
  (5.25% secured 2026, 5.75% secured 2028, 5.125% unsecured 2029)
- **30-day grace period ends: ~July 1, 2026**
- If interest is not paid by July 1: formal **Event of Default** on $24.56B of total debt
- AT&T cash proceeds: not available until **November 2027** at earliest
- EchoStar's own language: "does not have the necessary cash on hand, projected future
  cash flows or committed financing to fund their obligations over the next twelve months"

**Three possible scenarios by July 1:**
1. **Extension/waiver negotiated** with bondholders — delays formal default, stock
   stabilizes or partially recovers. Probability: moderate (bondholders have incentive
   to avoid triggering a disruptive bankruptcy ahead of the AT&T deal)
2. **Payment made** from emergency financing or asset sale — unlikely given disclosed
   liquidity. Probability: low
3. **Event of Default triggered** — debt accelerates, bankruptcy proceedings begin,
   stock potentially halted or becomes a distressed claim. Probability: elevated
   if no waiver is secured

**Portfolio status:**
- mom_roa_6535: 16.2121 sh @ $123.24 entry; Jun-17 close $111.70 = **−$186 unrealized
  (−9.35% from entry)**
- The July 1 rebalance will naturally exit SATS as its 12-1 momentum score is
  deeply negative
- **Risk flag:** If SATS is halted or enters a trading freeze before July 1, the
  paper-trade model cannot execute the sell. In a live account, this would require
  a manual early exit. For now, the paper position remains but the risk is noted.

**No override recommended** — the model handles this naturally. Document as a case
study in idiosyncratic credit risk that the ROA quality filter alone cannot screen.

Sources: [Inside Towers (EchoStar skips debt payments AT&T deal)](https://insidetowers.com/echostar-opts-to-skip-debt-payments-while-waiting-for-att-deal-to-close/), [Investing.com (EchoStar defers $183M AT&T closing)](https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/echostar-defers-183-million-interest-payment-pending-att-deal-closing-93CH-4719256), [StockTitan (EchoStar AT&T transactions $20.25B)](https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/SATS/8-k-echo-star-corp-reports-material-event-c303e13add64.html), [QuiverQuant (EchoStar missed payment default)](https://www.quiverquant.com/news/EchoStar+shares+slide+as+missed+interest+payment+rekindles+default+and+liquidity+concerns)

### Strategic Insights — June 18

#### Insight 1: Memory Supercycle as a Long-Duration Sleeve Candidate

The Apple CEO's WSJ interview crystallizes what has been building all year: DRAM and
NAND are entering a multi-year structural scarcity caused by AI workloads permanently
displacing consumer electronics as the marginal buyer. This is different from prior
memory cycles:

**Prior cycles (2016, 2020):** Demand-driven by smartphones; supply corrected in
12–24 months as fabs retooled for consumer specs.

**Current cycle:** AI servers require DRAM at 2–3× the density of consumer devices
AND require HBM (a completely different die architecture). Hyperscalers are signing
MULTI-YEAR contracts for HBM4 (MU confirmed 2026 HBM output entirely pre-sold).
Consumer device manufacturers (Apple, Samsung Electronics mobile) are structural
SECOND-TIER buyers — they receive supply AFTER AI contracts are filled.

**Sleeve design possibility (research only, not deployment-ready):**
A "memory quality momentum" sleeve using the same ROA × momentum framework but
with a constrained universe (WDC, STX, MU, SNDK) would have captured enormous
alpha in 2026. The backtest issue: this is a 4-name universe and inherently
backtested on the exact names that worked. It has survivorship bias. For now,
note the theme; the existing sleeves already hold all four names organically.

#### Insight 2: OTC Filter Enhancement — QDMI as Prototype for the Fix

QDMI's −70% collapse establishes a clear case for an additional universe filter:
**exclude tickers that trade exclusively on OTC Markets (Pink Sheets, OTCQB, OTCQX)**
rather than on a major exchange (NYSE, Nasdaq, AMEX).

**Why OTC names slip through the current filter:**
- The NON_STOCK_TICKERS exclusion catches known ETFs and indices
- The MAX_PRICE_USD cap excludes very high-priced outliers
- ROA quality screens can be defeated by temporarily inflated fundamentals
  (QDMI had valid-looking ROA at the June 3 calculation date)
- The 12-1 momentum score captured the pre-collapse spike

**Proposed fix:** Add an `exchange_filter` to the universe construction that requires
`exchange IN ('NYSE', 'NASDAQ', 'AMEX', 'NYSE MKT')`. This requires storing
exchange metadata in the fundamentals_cache or price_cache. Currently not implemented.
**Estimated impact:** Would eliminate ~90% of OTC pump-and-dump risk. Small cost:
might exclude legitimate smaller-cap names that have migrated to OTC temporarily
(post-delisting grace period). Net impact should be strongly positive.
**Flag for implementation at next development session.**

#### Insight 3: Intel Foundry as a New "Quality Turnaround Momentum" Signal

The Apple-Intel announcement (if confirmed) would represent the first major
validation of Intel's IDM 2.0 foundry strategy. The momentum × ROA model captured
INTC because:
- 12-1 momentum: INTC has risen sharply from its lows (was at $20–30 in early 2025,
  now $120+) — the momentum signal was strongly positive at June 3 rebalance date
- ROA: Intel was negative ROA in 2024–2025 during the turnaround; a positive ROA
  at the June 3 scoring date (if achieved) was a quality turnaround signal

**What the Apple deal would change for the model:**
If Intel's foundry earns Apple as an anchor customer, Intel's ROA trajectory turns
strongly positive (high-margin contract manufacturing vs. current loss-making). The
12-1 momentum score will reflect the stock's continued appreciation. The model
should hold INTC into July 1 and possibly beyond.

**Long-term sleeve implication:** "Foundry quality turnaround" could be a thematic
subset of the quality momentum strategy. Names that (a) are in a documented
turnaround, (b) have improving ROA trajectory, and (c) have strong 12-1 momentum
tend to outperform because they have both the quality improvement signal AND the
price momentum signal aligning. Intel is the current archetype.

#### Insight 4: FOMC Uncertainty Regime — Rate Path for Remainder of 2026

The June 17 FOMC dot plot revealed a 9–8 split (9 members project 2026 hike, 8
project no change or cut). Warsh has declined to give forward guidance. This regime
has specific implications for the portfolio's long-term strategy:

**High-uncertainty rate regime → momentum + quality outperformance:**
Historical precedent (2018, 2022): In regimes where the Fed's terminal rate is
uncertain, investors reduce DCF sensitivity by migrating to companies with:
1. Hard-to-discount near-term earnings (contracts, visible backlog)
2. Pricing power (semiconductor leaders, AI infrastructure)
3. Quality/profitability screens that filter out highly leveraged growth names

The portfolio's quality-augmented strategies (mom_roa, residual_roa) are
well-positioned for exactly this environment. The June 17 performance confirmation
(all 5 systematic sleeves beating SPY −1.25%) in the worst-case FOMC scenario
is the strongest live validation to date.

**Rate hike timing — if October hike materializes:**
A 25bps hike in October 2026 (the market's implied probability is now ~35-40%)
would likely hit:
- High-duration growth names (unprofitable software, loss-making biotech without
  clear near-term revenue) — NOT heavily represented in our sleeves
- Housing/consumer credit names — NOT in our sleeves
- SATS: would be unable to service debt even less (already going-concern)

It would NOT materially affect: MU (contracted revenue), STX, WDC (pricing cycle),
VRT (backlog), AEHR, COHR, ARWR (pipeline binary), INTC (if Apple deal transforms
economics), DOCN (AI-native cloud, rapid growth).

#### BE (Bloom Energy) +15.41% — AI Power Infrastructure Comes to a Head

Bloom Energy surged $43.92 to $328.91 today — the largest single-day absolute dollar
gain of any portfolio holding since inception. The move was NOT driven by a single
news catalyst but rather the **convergence of multiple bullish signals** that markets
have been building toward:

**Business context behind today's move:**
- **CEO performance RSU grant (filed June 18):** The Bloom Energy board granted CEO
  KR Sridhar a new performance-based stock unit award. The vesting criteria: Bloom must
  reach its highest four-quarter revenue run rate between July 2026–December 2029,
  adjusted by non-GAAP product gross margin. Critically, Sridhar must continue as CEO
  **through 2029** and hold shares **through 2031**. This CEO retention signal through
  2029 — at a $79B market cap — is a massive public commitment that the Bloom story
  is a multi-year, not a trade.
  Sources: [TipRanks (Bloom Energy performance RSU CEO Sridhar)](https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/bloom-energy-grants-new-performance-based-rsus-to-ceo),
  [Investing.com (Bloom Energy CEO RSU grant)](https://www.investing.com/news/sec-filings/bloom-energy-grants-performancebased-stock-units-to-ceo-sridhar-93CH-4748523)

- **Underlying business fundamentals:** Q1 2026 revenue +130% YoY to $751M; FY2026
  guidance raised to $3.4B–$3.8B; $20B backlog; $5B Brookfield AI partnership. The
  Oracle data center agreement (up to 2.8 GW of fuel cell power) remains in execution.
  The "bring-your-own-power" thesis: data center developers can't wait 5–7 years for
  grid expansion so they generate their own power on-site with Bloom fuel cells.
  Sources: [TIKR (Bloom Energy stock 134% 2026 why surging)](https://www.tikr.com/blog/bloom-energy-stock-is-up-134-in-2026-heres-why-be-is-surging),
  [Barchart (Bloom Energy CEO magic words surging)](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2339830/bloom-energy-stock-is-surging-its-ceo-said-these-magic-words),

### PRAX Factual Correction — POWER1 Data Released June 1 (Not "Imminent")

**Correction to this morning's report:** The pre-market report stated that POWER1
Phase 3 topline data for vormatrigine "has not yet been released as of June 18 morning."
**This was incorrect.** Praxis Precision Medicines announced the POWER1 topline results
on **June 1, 2026** (17 days ago). The data was available at the time of the morning
report — the morning report had a factual error.

**Confirmed POWER1 results (June 1, 2026):**
- Primary endpoint (seizure frequency reduction): **MISSED**
- Key secondary endpoint (≥50% responder rate at higher dose): **MET**
- Safety: Generally favorable; adverse event discontinuations <10%
- 90% of vormatrigine patients transitioned to open-label extension (OLE)
- POWER2 enrollment: **Paused** to reassess vormatrigine program and consider modifications

**Stock price reaction (June 1 onward):**
- 1-day return post-announcement: −4.06%
- 7-day return: −27.42%
- 30-day return: −22.18%

This explains why PRAX is at $282.31 (close June 18) vs. our $324.36 entry from May 1
= **−12.96% from entry** as of today's close. The stock has been partially recovering
since its post-POWER1 lows.

**PRAX today (+4.56% to $282.31):** The recovery today is part of the broader biotech
sector lift (QQQ +2.51%), not a new PRAX-specific catalyst.

**What remains for PRAX:**
1. **Relutrigine PDUFA: September 27, 2026** — NDA accepted with priority review for
   SCN2A/SCN8A DEE. This is the primary remaining catalyst.
2. **Ulixacaltamide PDUFA: January 29, 2027** — Essential Tremor NDA.
3. **Vormatrigine OLE data** — ongoing; no timeline for publication.

**July 1 rebalance decision for PRAX:** Will depend on whether June 30 PRAX price
vs. June 30, 2025 baseline gives a positive 12-1 momentum score. Given the −27% drop
post-POWER1, the score is likely negative if June 30, 2025 was below today's price.

### Strategic Insights — June 18 Post-Close

#### Insight 1: AI Power Infrastructure as a Multi-Year Sleeve Candidate

Today's BE +15.41% move forces a serious look at the AI power infrastructure theme
as a potential dedicated sleeve. The core thesis:

**The constraint:** US power grid interconnection queues run 5–7 years. A hyperscaler
needing 500MW by 2026 cannot connect to the grid in time. On-site power generation
(fuel cells, gas turbines, micro-nuclear) is the only available solution at scale.

**The companies capturing this:**
- **Bloom Energy (BE):** Solid oxide fuel cells; 2.8GW Oracle deal; $20B backlog; CEO through 2029
- **Vertiv (VRT):** Power distribution and cooling for AI data centers; $15B backlog
- **Comfort Systems (FIX):** Mechanical/electrical HVAC and power for data centers; $2B+ backlog
- **Powell Industries (POWL):** Electrical control equipment for industrial/power
- **NV Energy (NVT):** Utility serving Nevada data center corridor (Las Vegas AI hub)

**Current capture by existing sleeves:** Our systematic model already holds BE (mom_roa/v1/v2),
VRT (mom_roa), FIX (mom_roa/v1/v2), POWL (mom_roa/residual/v1/v2), NVT (residual_roa)
— essentially the entire power infrastructure theme is already in the portfolio
organically through the factor model. This is evidence the framework works: it picked
these names BEFORE the theme became consensus narrative.

**Should a dedicated sleeve be built?** Not yet. Reasons:
1. The existing sleeves already have exposure
2. A 5-name concentrated thematic sleeve has high idiosyncratic risk
3. Backtest would be heavily survivorship-biased (these are the names that worked)
4. Wait for July 1 rebalance to see what the model scores next

**What to watch:** If the model scores MORE power infrastructure names at July 1
(companies like FCEL, PLUG, NWTN, or utility-scale battery companies entering
the top-50 momentum + quality ranking), that's organic confirmation the theme has
legs. The model should NOT be overridden — let it discover the theme independently.

---

#### Insight 2: Semiconductor Equipment Cycle — Confirmation Phase, Not Peak

The across-the-board rally in equipment today (KLAC +8.73%, MKSI +9.46%, ICHR +10.24%,
UCTT +8.66%, TER +7.19%, LRCX +3.97%) coincides with Lam Research raising WFE guidance
to $140B (from $135B) with $145B possible. Historical WFE cycles:

| WFE Cycle | Peak | Duration | Signal |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2017–2018 | ~$52B | 18 months | Smartphone NAND demand |
| 2020–2022 | ~$98B | 24 months | Pandemic-driven EV + PC demand |
| 2024–present | **$140B+ (2026)** | 24+ months still rising | AI chip: HBM, advanced node logic |

The current cycle is running at 1.4× the prior peak and showing no deceleration.
Citi projects WFE reaching $200B in 2027 and $250B in 2028 — a 3× peak-of-prior-cycle
expansion. If these projections even partially materialize, the equipment names
(KLAC, LRCX, AMAT, and their supply chain ICHR, UCTT, MKSI) are in mid-cycle,
not late-cycle. **Strong hold thesis at July 1.**

---

#### Insight 3: MU/WDC/STX — Memory Supercycle Now Has First-Person Apple Validation

The Apple Cook "unsustainable memory costs" quote is qualitatively different from
analyst price target increases. It means:

1. **Apple's multi-year supply contracts are being renegotiated at higher prices** —
   Apple does not issue these public statements unless the pricing environment has
   permanently shifted.
2. **Consumer electronics is now a second-tier buyer** — AI data center contracts are
   being fulfilled first. Apple (the world's highest-volume premium device maker)
   receives supply AFTER hyperscalers.
3. **NAND AND DRAM are both constrained** — previous memory cycles were often 1D
   (DRAM OR NAND); this cycle is both simultaneously.

**For the model's memory holdings (MU, WDC, STX):**
- At $1,134 (MU), +109% from entry: the model captured the supercycle early
- The June 24 earnings represent a potential step-up catalyst
- Bear case: If Apple succeeds in locking longer-term contracts at current prices,
  the pricing narrative could stall; but the structural HBM shortage is separate
  from consumer NAND pricing

**New sleeve concept (research only):** A memory-focused factor-neutral sleeve:
long MU/WDC/SK Hynix ADR (if listed), short DRAM consumer end-demand proxies.
This requires short-side implementation and is not feasible in the current paper
framework. Flag for post-18th-birthday implementation when Alpaca live trading enables
long/short.

---

#### Insight 4: PRAX Case Study — What the Factor Model Cannot Screen

The PRAX POWER1 miss is a case study in the limits of the momentum × ROA framework
for biotech names:

**What the model scored correctly (May 1):**
- 12-1 momentum: PRAX had been rising strongly in the 12 months ending April 2026
  on Phase 2 EMBRAVE data (+77% seizure reduction)
- ROA: biotech ROA metrics can be complex; PRAX likely scored on cash/asset ratio
  or product revenue trajectory

**What the model cannot see:**
- Binary FDA/trial risk: Phase 3 outcomes are fundamentally unknowable from price
  or ROA data
- Phase 2 → Phase 3 attrition rates (~50% in CNS indications historically)
- The 30-day window between POWER1 announcement and May 1 entry likely contained
  the stock's highest recent price (near-term POWER1 anticipation premium)

**Lesson:** ROA × momentum is well-suited for capital-intensive businesses with
durable competitive advantages (semiconductors, industrials, energy infrastructure)
but faces systematic risk from binary catalyst names. The June 3 rebalance replaced
some biotech exposure with more industrial/semiconductor names — a natural self-correction.

**No filter change recommended yet.** One PRAX example is insufficient to justify
a biotech exclusion (ARWR +8.27% and ANAB are performing). But if the portfolio
consistently underperforms in biotech binary events vs. the semiconductor and
industrial holdings, a "biotech position size cap" (e.g., max 1.5% per name
vs. the current ~2%) could be worth backtesting.

#### 3. FOMC — Hawkish Shock Under New Chair Warsh (Jun 17)

Kevin Warsh's first FOMC meeting as Fed Chair delivered the rate decision markets expected — **hold at 3.50–3.75%, unanimous 12-0** — but the dot plot was a **hawkish surprise**:

- **9 of 18 FOMC members** now project at least one rate hike before year-end 2026
- **6 of 18** project two hikes
- Median year-end funds rate estimate raised from **3.4% → 3.8%**
- PCE inflation forecast raised from 2.7% → **3.6%** (driven by Iran war energy inflation)
- Warsh removed forward guidance entirely, announced five task forces to review Fed operations
- 2-year Treasury yield surged **+16bps to 4.216%** following the decision

**Market reaction**: Stocks sold off on Wednesday Jun 18 (intraday). Nasdaq −1.15% Jun 16 (anticipation). The Jun 17 holding added uncertainty. Jun 18 recovered strongly (+1.91% Nasdaq, +1.08% S&P) largely on the Iran ceasefire.

**Portfolio impact**: A rate hike signal is **the single biggest structural risk to the entire momentum book**. Our sleeves are long growth/tech/AI-infra — names with high P/E multiples, high capex, and earnings priced far in the future. Higher rates compress these valuations systematically. The near-term offset is the Iran peace deal (inflation relief), but the Warsh Fed is now clearly signaling it will prioritize fighting 3.6% PCE over supporting equities. This is a new regime vs. the April-May period.

Sources: [Fed holds rates, dot plot signals hike — CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html), [Warsh hawkish shock: 9 officials signal hike — Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/warsh-hawkish-shock-9-fed-180221394.html), [Fed Signals Rate Hike in 2026 — intellectia.ai](https://intellectia.ai/blog/fed-rate-hike-expectations-june-19-2026)

#### 4. Iran Ceasefire / Peace Deal (Jun 18) — Strait of Hormuz to Reopen

Pakistan's Prime Minister announced on Jun 18 that the US and Iran had reached a **14-point memorandum of understanding** (to be signed in Geneva on June 19) to end 100+ days of conflict:
- Reopen the Strait of Hormuz without tolls
- Lift the US naval blockade
- Begin a 60-day negotiation window on Iran's nuclear program

This was the dominant news driver on Jun 18, partially offsetting the Fed hawkish reaction and explaining the Nasdaq +1.91% and S&P +1.08% gains on that day.

**Oil price impact**: Brent crude has fallen ~20% from 2026 highs. Energy stocks plunged — XLE fell to **$53.77** (from $57.12 on Jun 11, −5.87% for the week). APA −10.20%, DINO −7.72%, FTI −7.69%, PARR −8.11% for the week.

**Portfolio impact**: This is a **direct headwind to residual_roa's energy hedge**. The sleeve holds APA, DINO, FTI, INSW, NRT, PARR, PBR, TEN — ~8 energy names that were residual_roa's natural Iran hedge through June. That hedge now reverses: the ceasefire removes the supply-shock premium. Residual_roa's relative underperformance vs mom_roa this week (+2.68% vs +6.14%) is partly explained by this energy reversal. Going into next rebalance (end-June), the energy names in residual_roa will likely rank lower on idiosyncratic momentum and may self-select out.

**IMPORTANT**: The deal still needs Trump's signature and is a 60-day window, not a permanent peace. Credibility is moderate — Iran continued attacks on Kuwait even during ceasefire negotiations. Market volatility from Iran remains a tail risk.

Sources: [US ends Iran blockade, market reaction — TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-june-18-2026), [US-Iran 14-point MOU announced — IG International](https://www.ig.com/en/news-and-trade-ideas/us-iran-ceasefire-260408), [Energy stocks plunge on ceasefire — Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4573335-energy-stocks-plunge-with-oil-prices-as-us-iran-ceasefire-set-to-open-strait-of-hormuz)

**1. The Memory Supercycle Is the Sleeves' Single Biggest Alpha Driver — And Their Biggest Earnings Risk**

WDC +41%, STX +23%, MU +14% in one week. This was driven by the Iran ceasefire risk-on and pre-earnings HBM scarcity narrative. All systematic sleeves hold 2-4 memory names. This is a great situation to be in *before* June 24 MU earnings — but a dangerous one if MU misses guidance after a 70% YTD run.

*Action item for end-of-June rebalance*: Apply the earnings-proximity rule from the Jun 10 proposal. If the rebalance falls before June 24: half-size MU, STX, WDC or defer their additions until after the print. The CIEN lesson (loaded day-before, −29%) applies directly.

**2. The Warsh Fed's Hawkish Pivot Is the Macro Regime Risk for H2 2026**

The dot plot flip to 9/18 members seeing hike is not priced in. Momentum works worst in high-rate, reversal-risk regimes. The prior VIX-regime filter proposal (reduce position count when VIX>20 at rebalance) remains relevant — now there's a *rate hike* dimension: if the Sep/Oct FOMC actually hikes, growth names get multiple-compressed. The Iran ceasefire gives short-term relief (inflation down → rate hike odds fall), but this is fragile.

*Testable idea*: Add a "rate hike probability" input to the next rebalance review. If market-implied hike probability for October 2026 exceeds 40%, apply the VIX-regime position-count reduction even if VIX is below 20.

**3. Residual_roa's Energy Hedge Is Now a Drag — Watch the Next Rebalance**

Residual_roa was the Iran-conflict hedge (energy names outperformed). That thesis has inverted with the ceasefire. APA, DINO, FTI, PARR, PBR, TEN, NRT, INSW all falling. Residual_roa's idiosyncratic construction will naturally reduce these names at the next rebalance if they rank lower on residual momentum. The key question is timing — if the ceasefire collapses (Trump still needs to sign; Iran continued missile attacks during negotiations), oil spikes back and residual re-wins.

*Monitor*: Watch whether the ceasefire MOU is signed at the Geneva meeting (June 19). Trump's signature is the binding step.

**4. VSAT Structural Headwind — Re-evaluate at Rebalance**

VSAT is held by mom_roa and residual_roa. Down −11.8% this week. SpaceX IPO creates a narrative overhang where every Starlink headline becomes a VSAT headwind. The stock's fundamentals (ViaSat-3 F3 launching, government/defense insulation) are intact but the market is clearly re-rating the competitive risk. The LLM overlay's May 29 veto also looks good in retrospect — it avoided the initial −19% pain and re-entered a higher-conviction setup isn't needed. The open question: does Crusoe Energy confirm, cancel, or restart the 1.8 GW Cheyenne facility? Any announcement is a BE catalyst in either direction.

**6. New Sleeve Concept: AI Power Infrastructure Factor**

The consistent outperformers across different sectors this week share one theme: *physical infrastructure for AI data centers*. BE (fuel cells), AGX (gas turbine EPC), POWL (switchgear), VRT (Vertiv — cooling/power), FIX (commercial HVAC/electrical). A potential sleeve concept: **`ai_power_infra_paper`** — systematic screen for names with >30% revenue from data center power infrastructure, filtered by momentum and ROA. This is distinct from the current sleeves (which pick up these names incidentally) and would be a **thematic factor** sleeve. Pre-research needed: construct a universe, backtest 2022–2025, check if factor alpha survives on held-out data. No recommendation yet — flag for research.

### Summary

The week of June 12–18, 2026 was transformational on multiple fronts. All five systematic sleeves posted strong weekly returns (+2.68% to +6.54%), led by the memory supercycle (WDC +41%, STX +23%, MU +14%) and a stunning BE reversal (+32%). ### Macro Events: June 12–18 in Detail

#### June 13–14 (Weekend): US-Iran MOU Signed

Over the weekend of June 13–14, the United States and Iran signed a **14-point Memorandum of Understanding** that formally ended the US-Iran war. The deal required Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz and dismantle its nuclear enrichment program in exchange for lifting oil sanctions and the naval blockade. President Trump and Iranian President Pezeshkian signed the agreement; Trump described it as "the deal that ends all deals."

**Oil market response**: Brent crude settled below $86.50 on June 13 (lowest since early March), and WTI fell toward $81. By June 17 when the US Navy formally lifted the blockade, three Saudi tankers carrying ~6 million barrels transited Hormuz overnight. Goldman Sachs estimated Iranian supply could return 3–4 million barrels/day within 90 days if the deal holds.

**Portfolio impact**: Energy names that had benefited from the Iran geopolitical premium began unwinding. XLE fell from $57.55 (Jun 12) to $53.77 (Jun 18), a −6.6% week. residual_roa's energy cluster (APA, DINO, PARR, NRT, PBR, INSW, TEN, FTI) was the primary headwind on that sleeve — the main reason it lagged the momentum sleeves this week despite holding many of the same tech names.

**Note**: Israel condemned the deal as a "deep disappointment" and Netanyahu stated continued concern over Iran's nuclear ambitions, but did not militarily intervene during the period.

Sources: [CNBC Iran oil prices Jun 12](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/12/oil-prices-wti-brent-on-hopes-of-us-iran-deal-despite-tehran-pushback.html), [Axios oil falls Iran deal](https://www.axios.com/2026/06/14/oil-prices-us-iran-war-hormuz-strait-peace-deal), [CNBC US Navy blockade ends](https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/06/18/us-navy-blockade-iran-trump-oil.html)

#### June 17 (Wednesday): FOMC Hold, Hawkish Dot Plot

The Federal Reserve held rates steady at **3.50–3.75%** (universally expected — 97% pre-meeting probability). The surprise was the **Summary of Economic Projections (dot plot)**:

- **Median rate end-2026: 3.8%** (up from 3.4% in March projections). This signals one additional rate hike expected before year-end.
- **9 of 18 FOMC members** now favor at least one additional hike in 2026 vs. 8 favoring no change and 1 favoring a cut.
- New Fed Chair Warsh (appointed by Trump) struck a more hawkish tone than prior Fed communications — his first FOMC meeting carried significant symbolic weight as investors recalibrate to his style.

**Market reaction**: S&P +0.10%, Nasdaq +0.34% — markets mostly shrugged, because (a) the hold itself was expected and (b) the 9-member-hike consensus was within the range of prior dots. The real market test will come if/when a September 2026 hike is explicitly flagged.

**Portfolio implications**: A late-2026 rate hike (priced for October/November per OIS markets) is the single biggest structural risk to growth/momentum positions. Historical precedent: each 25bps hike compresses P/E multiples on high-multiple growth names by ~1–2x turns. With many holdings at 30–50x forward earnings (INTC at 133x!), the sensitivity is elevated. The key unknown is whether earnings momentum (MU, WDC, BE) grows faster than the rate-compression headwind.

Also on June 17: the US Navy formally lifted the Iran naval blockade, and three Saudi tankers transited Hormuz overnight — the first commercial oil traffic through the strait in months.

Sources: [CNBC Fed hold Jun 17](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/17/fed-interest-rate-decision-june-2026.html), [StockTitan dot plot flip](https://www.stocktitan.net/articles/fed-rate-decision-june-17-2026)

### Holdings Deep-Dive: Key Winners This Week

#### WDC (Western Digital) — $746.23, +72.8% from May 1 entry ($431.74) — 4 Sleeves

WDC is now the single largest winner by absolute dollar gain across the portfolio. At entry, four sleeves each had ~$1,998–$2,031 invested in WDC. Combined: ~$8k at entry, now ~$14k at market (+$6k cumulative gain).

**The structural story**: WDC has crossed 50% gross margin for the first time in company history, driven by higher-capacity nearline drives (the kind used in AI training clusters), UltraSMR technology adoption, and improved pricing. The company has sold out its *entire 2026 HDD production* — a level of pre-commitment that effectively guarantees strong Q4 FY2026 (report ~late July) and FY2027 guidance.

**The competitive moat**: Morgan Stanley's June 15 note explicitly stated that WDC and STX have a combined duopoly in high-capacity nearline HDD. There is no third entrant — HGST was absorbed into WDC, and Toshiba's HDD segment serves different markets. The supply constraint isn't a near-term production scheduling issue; it's a 3-year lead-time issue for new clean-room capacity. This moat is genuinely defensible through at least 2027.

**What to monitor**: Any hyperscaler announcement that they are pivoting from HDD to NVMe/NAND for AI storage would be the key bear catalyst. Amazon/Meta/Google have all confirmed HDD roadmaps through 2028, but any defection would reprice rapidly. For now, the bull case is extraordinarily well-supported.

Source: [WDC sold out Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/western-digital-sold-2026-hard-112206446.html), [TIKR WDC gross margin](https://www.tikr.com/blog/western-digital-stock-crosses-50-gross-margin-for-the-first-time-with-a-79-potential-return-ahead)

#### BE (Bloom Energy) — $328.91, +13.1% from May 1 entry ($290.67) — mom_roa, mom_v2, mom_v1

BE's +26.4% week pushed it from underwater to firmly profitable: entry $290.67, current $328.91 = **+13.1% gain**. The June 18 FERC win is the most structurally significant catalyst for Bloom since the Crusoe Energy partnership was announced.

**FERC clarity matters**: Prior to the new FERC policy, deploying a Bloom fuel cell system at a large AI data center required grid-connection approval — a process that could take 18–36 months due to utility backlogs. The new policy creates a faster track for "behind-the-meter" onsite generation that doesn't touch the transmission grid. This expands Bloom's addressable market dramatically for urgent AI buildout sites where utilities can't commit to power delivery timelines.

**The Crusoe overhang resolved?**: Prior reports flagged the 1.8 GW Cheyenne, Wyoming project pause as a risk. The June 18 rally suggests the market is now treating the FERC win and new contract pipeline as more important than the Crusoe delay. If Crusoe confirms the project proceeds on its revised timeline (expected confirmation by July 2026), this removes the last major bear point.

**Revenue visibility**: Bloom's fuel cell contracts are typically 5–20 year power purchase agreements (PPAs), providing long-duration revenue visibility. Unlike the semi names where each quarter requires a new beat, Bloom's backlog converts to predictable cash flow. This is structurally different from the binary-risk profile of pure-momentum plays.

**Is BE a new sleeve candidate?**: The AI power infrastructure theme is real and durable. BE, FCEL (FuelCell Energy), and any SMR developer (TerraPower, X-energy — both private) represent a 5–10 year secular theme driven by grid constraint. BE is the only large-cap, publicly-traded pure play. A dedicated "AI Power Infrastructure" sleeve with 3–5 names (BE, VRT (Vertiv), POWL, a utility or SMR developer) could capture this theme independently of the memory supercycle.

Sources: [StocksToTrade BE Jun 18](https://stockstotrade.com/news/bloom-energy-corporation-be-news-2026_06_18/), [Barchart BE CEO magic words](https://www.barchart.com/story/news/2339830/bloom-energy-stock-is-surging-its-ceo-said-these-magic-words)

### Holdings Deep-Dive: Key Losers

#### VIAV (Viavi Solutions) — $47.17, −11.8% from Jun 12 entry ($53.46 Jun 12 close) — mom_roa, mom_v2, mom_v1

VIAV was one of the week's hardest-hit optical names. Entry from the June 3 rebalance was $52.45 for mom_roa ($53.46 was the Jun 12 close). VIAV provides optical components and network test equipment. Its optical hardware products compete in the same market as FN (Fabrinet) and CIEN — all three are suffering from the same phenomenon: the sector rotation from optical-interconnect-component into storage/memory and AI-semi-equipment.

The structural issue: investors see VIAV's optical test division as stable but slow-growth, while its optical component division directly competes with cheaper Asian manufacturers. The AI-driven optical market that VIAV participates in (network test, optical amplifiers) is real, but the market is rewarding companies with *direct AI hardware supply chain* exposure — which means LRCX, AMAT, MU — not test equipment.

The June 15 analyst wave (Morgan Stanley WDC $650, STX $1,035; TD Cowen MU $1,500, RBC MU $1,200) is the clearest research convergence this portfolio has seen. WDC +72.8% from entry, STX +47.2% from entry, MU +109% from entry — all in 49 days.

| Name | Thesis | Weight |
|---|---|---|
| MU | HBM4 sold out, DRAM oligopoly, $1T cap | 30% |
| WDC | AI-HDD duopoly, 50%+ GM, all 2026 production sold | 25% |

**Signal**: 12-month trailing revenue momentum + gross margin trend (not price momentum). Quarterly rebalance. Hold period: 2–3 years minimum.

**When to build**: After MU June 24 earnings. If MU beats on both revenue AND gross margin guidance, this sleeve becomes a conviction build for July. If MU disappoints on gross margin, wait for clarity on whether the HBM supercycle is already cresting.

**Risk**: This sleeve is highly correlated — all five names will fall together if the AI capex cycle turns. The hedge is that the supply shortage math (3-year fab lead time) makes the cycle structurally longer than historical DRAM cycles. Still a single-factor bet.

---

#### 2. AI Power Infrastructure — Emerging Theme Worth Monitoring

BE's +26.4% week is not isolated. The broader trend: AI data centers require 150–200 MW of power per facility, and US grid capacity cannot support the AI buildout pipeline at the planned pace. Solutions companies include:

- **BE (Bloom Energy)**: Fuel cells, now benefiting from FERC regulatory clarity. Currently held.
- **VRT (Vertiv)**: Data center power and cooling infrastructure. Currently held by residual_roa ($328.47 entry, check current price).
- **POWL (Powell Industries)**: Electrical equipment for power distribution. Currently held by multiple sleeves.
- **GEV (GE Vernova)**: Grid and power infrastructure, strong order book. Not currently held.
- **SMR developers**: TerraPower, X-energy — both private, not available until IPO (possible 2026–2027)

A dedicated 4–5 name "AI Power Infrastructure" sleeve would diversify away from the semiconductor concentration risk while remaining AI-adjacent. **Primary difference from semiconductor names**: revenue is driven by grid constraint and power demand (structural, multi-decade trend), not by DRAM pricing cycles (shorter cyclical). This could be a genuine risk-diversifier that still participates in the AI theme.

**Decision**: Research first. Build target: September 2026 if the grid-constraint narrative remains intact.

---

#### 3. Hawkish Fed Regime Adaptation

The June 17 dot-plot shift (median rate 3.8% end-2026, implying one hike) creates a new headwind that wasn't in the model when the sleeves were designed. Historical momentum factor research (AQR, Asness et al.) shows that:
- Momentum strategies **tend to underperform** during rate-hike initiation (the first 1–3 hikes after a prolonged hold)
- Momentum strategies **recover** once the market reprices to the new rate regime

This is not a reason to exit the sleeves — the paper trade is long-horizon. But it suggests:
(a) **Position sizing consideration**: If building new capital in this sleeve setup, consider a smaller initial allocation until rate clarity emerges (October FOMC)
(b) **Defensive rotation at June rebalance**: If any top-ranked name is extremely high-multiple (INTC at 133x is the obvious one), the rate hike risk argues for the signal to naturally rotate it out if its momentum score degrades

**Practical action**: At the June rebalance, flag any holding with forward P/E >100x as "rate-sensitive" and apply extra scrutiny (but still let the signal decide).

---

#### 4. AAOI as a Pattern Lesson for LLM Overlay Signal Design

The AAOI veto is an excellent case study. The three flags that matter most in retrospect:

1. **Insider selling on the day of the trade**: SVP Fred Chang sold $5.6M the exact day the signal triggered a buy. Management insiders have access to information momentum signals don't: forward order pipelines, customer conversations, product yields. SVP-level selling at momentum-triggered price levels is one of the strongest near-term mean-reversion signals in empirical research (Seyhun, "Insiders' Profits, Costs of Trading, and Market Efficiency", 1986 and subsequent literature).

2. **Guidance below consensus for BOTH revenue and EPS**: When a company guides both dimensions below street consensus in the same quarter, the probability of further estimate cuts is historically ~65% (based on earnings revision literature). This is the "negative estimate revision cycle" entering its first stage.

3. **ATM equity offering on a momentum-driven stock**: An ATM offering is a management signal that they believe the stock is FAIRLY TO RICHLY PRICED (otherwise they wouldn't dilute at current prices). This is the opposite of what momentum bulls need — management conviction that the price is right or high.

**Proposal for LLM overlay scoring rubric update**: Add a formal "insider activity" check as one of the 3 required prompts. The current 3-prompt structure (macro context, company fundamentals, technical/momentum validity) should incorporate insider transaction data from Form 4 filings as an explicit input into the fundamentals prompt.

### CRITICAL UPDATE: SATS — Interest Payment Made June 18, Default Averted

On June 18, 2026 — the final day of the 30-day grace period — EchoStar's DISH DBS
subsidiary made the previously deferred $183 million interest payment covering three
series of notes (5.25% Secured 2026, 5.75% Secured 2028, 5.125% Unsecured 2029).
**An Event of Default on $24.56B of total debt was averted.**

**What remains unresolved:** The 2026 principal maturity wall totals $6.13 billion
(including $2.0B in 7 3/4% Notes and $2.75B in 5.25% Secured Notes). The Restructuring
Support Agreement (RSA, signed March 19 with 82% of noteholders) is designed to
address this through debt-for-equity conversion, but execution requires AT&T deal
proceeds ($20.25B, not arriving until November 2027 final close). SATS traded
$104–$112 over the Juneteenth weekend (weekend secondary market pricing), settling
near $107.63.

**Portfolio action:** The model exits SATS at July 1 regardless (12-1 momentum
deeply negative from peak $180+ to $107). The interest payment is near-term relief,
not a thesis change. **Audit note:** If SATS is halted or suspended before July 1,
the paper position cannot be closed — document as uncloseable if that occurs.

### Strategic Insights — June 22

#### Insight 1: MU + PCE Sequencing — The One-Two Punch Risk

MU earnings Wednesday night and PCE data Thursday create a 14-hour window where
the portfolio could move sharply in two opposite directions:

**Scenario A (bull-bull):** MU beats big, PCE benign → tech rally extends across
Thursday and into July 1. All five systematic sleeves benefit. Best case for the period.

**Scenario B (bull-bear):** MU beats, but PCE hot → rate spike reverses tech gains.
After-hours MU surge gives back 50% or more during Thursday's session.
**Model action:** Hold through the noise. A strong MU business print is a 12–24
month thesis, not a one-day trade.

**Scenario C (bear):** MU misses on gross margin → MU −15–20%, drags tech, coincides
with hot PCE. Worst case but lowest probability given Apple's "unsustainable" supply
admission (first-person confirmation of pricing power from MU's largest consumer customer).

The key watch number: **MU's next-quarter gross margin guidance.** If guided above
80%, the supercycle is real. If guided below 78%, HBM yield issues are emerging.

#### Insight 2: AI Power Infrastructure — Self-Reinforcing Cluster

The AGX (+5%), FIX (+5%), BE (+13%), VRT (+1%), POWL (+8%) cluster in the portfolio
represents a structural theme that reinforces itself:

1. AI training/inference demand grows → data centers need more power
2. Utility grid timelines are 3–5 years → developers bypass the grid
3. On-site power (BE fuel cells, AGX gas plants) creates demand for electrical
   construction (FIX, POWL) and thermal management (VRT)
4. The cycle repeats at each new campus

The ROA × momentum model captured this cluster organically because all five companies
have high ROA (profitable backlog execution) and strong 12-1 momentum. No manual
override was needed — the factor model found the theme.

**Key risk:** Any major hyperscaler CapEx pause in Q3 2026 guidance would compress
multiples across this cluster simultaneously. No evidence of CapEx deceleration;
the opposite — every major hyperscaler (MSFT, AMZN, GOOG, META) has raised 2026
CapEx guidance in 2026.

#### Insight 3: OTC Filter — QDMI → Implementation Before August 1

The QDMI collapse (~−70%) confirms the need for an exchange-quality filter in the
universe construction. Proposed implementation for July 1 development session:

- Add `exchange` column to `fundamentals_cache`; populate from yfinance `info['exchange']`
- Universe filter: `exchange IN ('NYSE', 'NasdaqGS', 'NasdaqGM', 'NasdaqCM', 'AMEX')`

#### Insight 4: Iran Oil Deal — Why the July 1 Exit Timing Is Correct

The Geneva postponement on June 19 is negotiating friction, not deal collapse. The
60-day framework runs until ~August 14, 2026. For energy positions:

- Exiting APA/DINO/PARR/NRT/PBR at July 1 removes portfolio exposure during the
  most uncertain 6 weeks of the Iran negotiation process
- Even if talks fail: the structural IEA supply glut (+6M bpd surplus by 2027) is
  independent of Iran and is bearish for upstream producers long-term
- Even if deals succeed: refiner margins (DINO, PARR) compress as cheap Iranian oil
  floods the market, hurting crack spreads even as raw crude prices fall

The exit is correct in either scenario. The July 1 timing minimizes further drag
from names that are already substantially underwater.

### GOOGL −6.5%: AI Talent Exodus and What It Means for the Portfolio

Alphabet fell **−6.5%** on June 22 on two consecutive AI talent departures:

1. **Noam Shazeer → OpenAI**: A leading AI engineering figure, Shazeer returned to Alphabet
   in August 2024 via a $2.7B reverse acquihire of Character.AI. His departure to OpenAI is
   the most high-profile talent loss since that acquihire.

2. **John Jumper → Anthropic**: Key DeepMind researcher, notable for AlphaFold protein-folding
   work; his departure to Anthropic signals that well-resourced AI labs can compete with
   Google's talent packages.

**Market impact:** Alphabet lost ~$250 billion in market cap on June 22. Amazon −4.8%,
Microsoft −3%, Meta −2.3% were sympathy casualties as megacap AI software sold off.

**Portfolio implication:** Our sleeves hold NONE of these names. The quality-momentum
framework organically avoided high-multiple software megacaps (they don't score high on
ROA × momentum in a way that passes the universe filter). The result: our portfolio
GAINED on a day where the S&P's largest components by weight fell sharply.

**Strategic insight:** The GOOGL talent exodus is actually BULLISH for AI infrastructure.
More competition in frontier models = more training runs = more GPU compute = more HBM
memory = more optical transceivers = more power. Our holdings (MU, WDC, COHR, CRDO, VRT,
AEHR) benefit from a MORE competitive AI model landscape, not less.

This is the core resilience argument for the ROA × momentum factor approach:
it owns the "picks and shovels" that benefit regardless of who wins the model race.

Sources: [Bloomberg (Alphabet shares drop second AI star departs)](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-22/alphabet-shares-drop-after-second-ai-star-departs-for-a-rival),

### SpaceX SPCX −16.4% — Post-IPO Correction and $20B Bond Offering

SpaceX fell **−16.4%** to ~$154.60, the largest single-day decline since its IPO debut
on June 12, 2026 (10 days ago). The causes:

1. **$20B inaugural bond issuance**: SpaceX confirmed its first bond offering as a public
   company. The $20B in new debt raised concerns about cash burn rate, dilution, and the
   company's near-term profitability discipline.

2. **MSCI "lowest possible ESG rating"**: Added an additional institutional seller cohort
   (ESG-constrained funds that cannot hold the name).

3. **Post-IPO correction mechanics**: SpaceX briefly surpassed Amazon and Microsoft in
   market cap in its first two trading days before declining. The three-day losing streak
   (−3.6% Wed, −5% Thu, −16.4% Mon) reflects the typical post-IPO normalization.

**Portfolio impact: None.** SpaceX is not held in any sleeve. The portfolio avoided the
post-IPO euphoria-to-correction cycle entirely.

**What this signals for the model:** High-momentum names at IPO peak can score highly on
short-term price momentum but are dangerous entries due to (a) IPO lockup overhangs,
(b) lack of established ROA track record, and (c) index-inclusion mechanics that reverse
quickly. The ROA filter would likely exclude SpaceX at IPO (no multi-year ROA data). This
is a case where the dual-signal (ROA × momentum) protected the portfolio from a tempting but
dangerous entry.

### Strategic Insights — June 22

#### Insight 1: Hardware/Software Bifurcation as a Persistent Structural Theme

June 22 crystallized a theme that has been building all year:
**AI hardware wins; AI software loses** in a talent-departure/competition-escalation event.

- COHR +12.31%, CRDO +11.29%, VRT +7.48%, MU +6.82% — all hardware/infrastructure
- GOOGL −6.5%, DOCN −4.06%, MSFT −3%, META −2.3% — all software/platform

This is not a coincidence. It reflects the structural position of each company:
- Hardware companies get paid per unit of AI compute consumed; their revenue scales with
  ANY model running on ANY inference stack
- Software/platform companies compete for AI user mindshare; talent departures directly
  reduce their competitive moat

**Implication for sleeve design:** The ROA × momentum model NATURALLY tilts toward hardware
because hardware companies have hard assets (ROA) and visible demand cycles (momentum).
Software companies often have high gross margins but lower ROA (less hard-asset intensity).
This structural tilt is a feature, not a bug — and it shows up in days like today.

#### Insight 2: AAOI Veto Runbook Refinement Needed

The second scare event (June 15 QuantumLink +13.3%, June 22 China credit line +5.79%)
raises a question about the runbook's trigger criteria:

**Current trigger:** "confirmed first-customer 1.6T CPO shipment"

**Is the China credit line a partial trigger?** The RMB 300M allocation for fixed assets
implies equipment purchases for manufacturing capacity. If the equipment is for 1.6T CPO
production, it is preparation for the trigger — typically 3–6 months ahead of first shipment.

**Proposed clarification for the runbook:**
- Trigger 1 (hard): First confirmed 1.6T CPO customer shipment from a hyperscaler
- Trigger 2 (soft, conditional): AAOI confirms (on earnings or IR call) that 1.6T CPO
  production equipment is installed and sampling has begun
- Trigger 3 (invalidation of veto): If AAOI reports Q2 2026 earnings above analyst
  consensus AND guidance includes 1.6T CPO revenue line → re-enter

The doubled credit line is a precursor event but does not meet any of the three trigger
criteria. Maintain cash position.

#### Insight 3: CRDO DustPhotonics Acquisition — Silicon Photonics vs. AEC Long-Term

CRDO's DustPhotonics acquisition gives it silicon photonics capability. This is important
for the long-term durability of the CRDO position:

**AEC (Active Electrical Cable) limitation:** The AI connectivity market will eventually
transition from AEC (copper with active components) to silicon photonics as data rates
exceed 3.2T and distances require optical solutions. CRDO's existing AEC business could be
disrupted by optical-native solutions.

**Silicon photonics acquisition = hedge:** By acquiring DustPhotonics, CRDO is building
the capability to compete in the optical era BEFORE it arrives. This is a smart execution
of the product roadmap. Combined with its 35%+ net margins and $1.34B FY2026 revenue base,
CRDO has the capital to fund this transition internally.

**Implication for sleeve:** CRDO should score well on 12-1 momentum at July 1 AND at the
August 1 and future rebalances. The DustPhotonics acquisition extends the long-duration
thesis from 1-2 years to 3-5 years.

#### Insight 4: OTC Filter + New Universe Quality Checks (Pre-August 1 Development)

Three developments reinforce the case for the planned exchange-quality filter:
1. QDMI: −70% collapse from OTC pump-and-dump; no material news
2. SATS: Credit risk that appeared as "positive ROA" (spectrum assets masked operational losses)
3. SpaceX lesson: IPO-peak entries on momentum alone (without ROA track record) are dangerous

**Proposed additions to the filter before August 1 rebalance:**
1. **Exchange filter**: `exchange IN ('NYSE', 'NasdaqGS', 'NasdaqGM', 'NasdaqCM', 'AMEX')`
   → Excludes QDMI-type OTC names
2. **Going-concern flag**: Screen for 10-Q/10-K filings that contain "going concern" language
   → Would have excluded SATS at May 1 if implemented
3. **IPO age filter**: Require minimum 12 months of price history for valid 12-1 momentum
   → Prevents buying at IPO peak (SpaceX would be excluded until June 2027)

These three filters together would have prevented all three categories of failure observed
since inception.

### Ciena (CIEN) â€” Convertible Overhang Anatomy

CIEN entered at $535.56 (June 3 rebalance) across mom_roa, mom_v1, mom_v2, and
residual_roa. The convertible notes deal structure is now fully known:

- **$2.875B** convertible senior notes, 0% coupon, due 2031
- Conversion price: **$746.66/share** (60% premium over June 8 price of $466.67)
- Use: $100M note hedge + $140M share repurchases + $1.14B term loan repayment
- Net: deleveraged balance sheet, but dealer hedging creates mechanical selling pressure

The conversion premium at $746 means there is ZERO dilution risk at current prices (~$445
range). The headwind is the dealer delta-hedge: dealers who sold the converts to investors
short-sell stock to hedge their long-convert position. This mechanical selling typically
resolves over 3-6 months as the position seasons and delta-hedgers get longer.

**Analyst range:** Stifel Buy PT $615 (+38%), UBS Neutral PT $508 (+14%). Business
remains strong ($6.3B FY2026 guidance, +32% YoY).

**Strategy:** Hold through July 1 rebalance; let the signal decide on exit. If CIEN
exits the top-50 due to price decline, accept the loss. If it stays ranked, hold and
wait for the dealer hedging to resolve over Q3 2026.

The current portfolio has scattered exposure to optical interconnect: FN in mom sleeves,

several. But no sleeve is deliberately harvesting the optical ramp as a concentrated thesis.

**The multi-year tailwind:**
- Data center AI inference clusters require 10-100Ã— more optical ports per rack vs
  traditional IT infrastructure
- The 400Gâ†’800Gâ†’1.6T transceiver migration is a multi-year procurement wave (2026-2030)
- AAOI confirmed $324M in 800G/1.6T orders from hyperscalers; FN manufacturing

**Shock 2 — Korean KOSPI Circuit-Breaker Crash (June 23)**

Korean FSC comments about restricting leveraged semiconductor ETF products triggered a cascade. KOSPI fell **9.99%** with circuit breakers triggered twice intraday. Samsung fell -11.17%, SK Hynix -11.78%. The market interpreted this as a signal about Korean chipmaker balance sheet stress and potential capex cuts — directly threatening equipment vendors (LRCX, AMAT, KLAC) and memory customers.

The chain: FSC comment → leveraged ETF forced unwinds → Samsung/SK Hynix margin calls → global memory supply fear → MU pre-earnings liquidation.

*Sources: [Bloomberg — KOSPI circuit breakers](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-06-23/korean-stocks-fall-more-than-4-from-record-high-on-tech-selloff), [TradingKey — Samsung SK Hynix crash](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/more/261983498-stock-kospi-samsung-skhynix-google-meta-tradingkey)*

This was a sector-specific technical event, not a broad market de-rating. AI capex commitments from hyperscalers remain intact at $725B+ for 2026. Dan Ives (Wedbush) explicitly characterized the selloff as "not the story" — the AI infrastructure thesis is unchanged and the memory selloff was positioning/Korea-technical, not fundamental.

### 8. Critical: MU Q3 Earnings Tomorrow (June 24, After Close)

Micron fell -13.2% today to $1,051.77, one trading day before reporting Q3 2026 earnings after close on June 24. This creates a textbook **pre-earnings de-risking setup**.

**Consensus estimates (June 23):**
- Revenue: $34.66B (+93% YoY — unprecedented growth rate)
- EPS: $19.95
- Gross margin guidance consensus: >80% (would signal HBM supercycle intact)

**Why today's selloff was positioning, not fundamental:**
The KOSPI crash hit SK Hynix -11.78%. SK Hynix is MU's primary competitor. If SK Hynix had capex problems, that would actually *help* Micron's competitive position (less supply). The market sold the entire memory sector on correlation, not on MU-specific news.

**The asymmetric setup:**
- Downside: Already priced in. At $1,051 the market has already moved 13% below yesterday's ATH. Incremental bad news would need to be catastrophic (miss + guide down) to fall much further.
- Upside: Beat + gross margin >80% + any data center commentary would likely send MU back to prior highs ($1,200+), representing +14% from current levels.
- Bull case for HBM3E demand from AI training remains structurally unchanged; hyperscaler capex is $725B.

**Action in sleeve context:** All four momentum sleeves hold MU. No rebalance until July 1. Hold through earnings by default — the signal was generated on fundamentals (12-1 momentum + high ROA), and a -13.2% pre-earnings dip on Korean technical contagion does not invalidate the thesis.

### 10. Strategic Insights: Filter Improvements & New Sleeve Candidates

**A. SPAC Filter (High Priority)**

FGMC = BOXABL SPAC demonstrated today the same pattern as QDMI (OTC pump-dump). Both were captured by the momentum signal during the "hype" run-up phase and then crashed. The universe filter should exclude SPACs.

**Proposed fix:** Add a check in `universe.py` for tickers where market cap < threshold AND price ≈ $10 NAV AND recent float is tiny (SPAC pre-merger structure). Alternatively, filter on exchange — SPACs are commonly identified by lack of revenue on any fundamental screen.

A simpler near-term fix: add a `NON_STOCK_TICKERS`-equivalent list for known SPACs (FGMC, AFJK) to prevent re-entry at next rebalance.

**B. AFJK Already in Portfolio — Risk Note**

AFJK is already held in mom_roa with -$477 (-24.4%) unrealized loss. AFJK appears to also be a SPAC or SPAC-adjacent vehicle (ticker pattern consistent). This is a structural filter hole. At July 1 rebalance, confirm whether AFJK momentum score still ranks — if so, something is wrong with the universe filter.

**C. Defense Contractor Sleeve — New Candidate**

Today's SOX -7.9% vs SPY -1.45% illustrates that defense contractors had zero correlation to semiconductor selloffs. Tickers like LMT, RTX, NOC, GD, HII, LDOS showed minimal movement today. Defense contractors have:
- ROA: High (government cost-plus contracts)
- 12-1 momentum: Strong since 2024 (NATO expansion, US defense budget increases)
- Correlation to semiconductor cycle: Near zero
- Data center exposure: Zero

A **"Defense Quality Momentum"** sleeve would provide natural diversification against semi-specific shock days like today. Backtest suggestion: filter universe to SIC codes 3760-3769 (guided missiles) and 3812 (defense electronics), apply same 65/35 ROA-momentum signal.

Estimated portfolio benefit: On a day like today, defense sleeve would have returned approximately +0.3% to +0.8% (driven by RTX, LMT news flow) vs mom_roa -5.31%. The correlation break would meaningfully reduce portfolio-level drawdown.

**D. AI Power Infrastructure Non-Semi Sleeve**

Names like BE (Bloom Energy), VRT (Vertiv), FIX (Comfort Systems), AGX (Argan), POWL (Powell Industries) represent AI data center power/cooling but have ZERO semiconductor manufacturing exposure. They were still hit today (-11% VRT) purely on Korean contagion, but their fundamental thesis is disconnected from DRAM pricing and Korean chipmaker leverage.

A concentrated 4-name "AI Power" sleeve would capture the same AI capex thematic but with much lower correlation to memory/equipment cycles. Pre-condition: wait until after July 1 rebalance and confirm post-rebalance momentum ranks.

**E. Rate Hike Regime Insight — ROA Filter Working**

BofA's 3-hike forecast is structurally a headwind for high-multiple, low-profit growth names. The ROA component of mom_roa and residual_roa naturally filters toward quality companies with actual earnings. Today's result (residual_roa -2.80% vs SPY -1.45%) is partly SOX beta, but compared to hypothetical pure-momentum sleeve (which might have held pure-multiple FANG+ components), the ROA filter likely saved 1-2pp.

The BofA 3-hike regime reinforces keeping the ROA filter — do not consider switching to pure-momentum (mom_v1/v2 style) sleeves for new launches while rate uncertainty is elevated.

**F. MU Pre-Earnings Signal for Future Reference**

Historical pattern (Micron earnings): MU typically sells off 8-15% in the 48 hours before earnings (portfolio managers de-risk ahead of binary event), then rallies 5-20% on beats. Today's -13.2% fits this pattern exactly. The question for future strategy refinement: should momentum sleeves trim 50% of MU position 2 days before earnings and re-buy after? This would reduce earnings-event volatility while keeping core exposure.

This is not actionable for the current setup (no scheduled trading between rebalances) but is a useful rule for future sleeve variants that incorporate earnings-event positioning.

### 9. BofA 3-Hike Regime — Portfolio Defense Assessment

BofA's June 22 forecast of **3 Fed rate hikes (Sep/Oct/Dec 2026, target 4.25-4.50%)**
remains the dominant macro risk. Key BofA rationale:

- May payrolls +172K, unemployment 4.3%, wage growth 3.4% — labor market "doesn't need relief"
- Inflation above 2% target with energy and demand risks
- Fed Chair Warsh "leaned hawkish" at press conferences
- BofA economist: inflation "unambiguously worse"

**How our portfolios are positioned for rate hikes:**

| Factor | Rate-Hike Effect | Our Exposure |
|---|---|---|
| ROA filter | High-ROA companies maintain valuation | Core signal in mom_roa, residual_roa |
| Zero-earnings names | De-rated hardest in hiking cycle | AAOI in diversified sleeves (risk) |
| Storage/memory | DRAM/NAND pricing = inflation hedge | MU, WDC, STX all highly profitable |
| AI capex | Companies can't stop building → sticky demand | BE, VRT, AGX, FIX benefit |
| Community banks | Rate hikes = wider NIM → higher ROA | FNRN, FMBM, CSBB benefit |
| Growth/zero-rev | Worst in hiking environment | AFJK, FGMC (already flagged as exits) |

**Assessment:** Our best-performing sleeves (mom_roa_6535, residual_roa_6535) are structurally
aligned with a rate-hiking regime. The ROA signal naturally screens for earnings quality.
The main risk is that zero-earnings high-momentum names (common in mom_v1/v2 which don't use
ROA) get hit harder. This is consistent with what we've seen: mom_v1/v2 trail the roa sleeves.

*Sources: [BofA reverses course, 3 Fed hikes — CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/06/22/bank-of-america-sees-3-fed-hikes-in-2026-inflation-unambiguously-worse.html) | [BofA rate hike forecast — TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/fed/bank-of-america-revamps-interest-rate-forecast-for-rest-of-2026)*

### 12. Strategic Insights — New Sleeve Candidates and Emerging Patterns

**A. Memory Supercycle Duration Risk — New Lens**

Tonight's MU print (supply deficit "beyond 2027") transforms the investment case from
cyclical to structural. The traditional bear case for memory is the commodity cycle — prices
peak, capacity floods the market, prices crash. But HBM is fundamentally different:

- HBM is capital-intensive to produce (requires WAFER STACKING, not just fab throughput)
- Three suppliers globally (SK Hynix, Samsung, Micron) have limited capacity expansion speed
- Every dollar of AI capex requires memory — AI training runs can't be shrunk
- HBM4 is 2+ years ahead of HBM5 (not yet designed); the product cycle locks in pricing

**Investment implication:** MU's current earnings trajectory makes it a potential candidate
for even higher momentum scores through 2027. The sleeves holding MU at $542.48 entry with
+117.5% unrealized are sitting on multi-year winners, not a trade.

**B. AI Power Infrastructure Sleeve — Elevated Priority (Reiterated)**

The Micron print confirms the direction: AI capex is a multi-trillion dollar, multi-year
phenomenon. The non-semiconductor expression of this theme (BE, VRT, AGX, FIX, POWL, MTZ)
offers diversification from the Korean semiconductor contagion events we saw June 23-24.

**Proposed sleeve parameters:**
- Universe: SIC codes 3599 (industrial machinery), 3612/3613 (power transformers/switchgear),
  1731 (electrical work), 4911/4941 (electric utilities) + AI data center contractors
- Signal: mom_roa_6535 restricted to 8-12 names
- Rationale: BE/VRT/AGX/FIX already present in existing sleeves via free-float momentum;
  a dedicated sleeve would concentrate this exposure and give a clean head-to-head vs the
  broad semiconductor-heavy sleeves
- Pre-condition: Complete July 1 rebalance, then backtest restricted universe on June 30 data
- Expected correlation: Low with SOX; high with AI capex data (data center starts, FERC filings)

**C. SPAC Filter — Technical Implementation Plan**

Two SPACs captured simultaneously (AFJK + FGMC) represents a systematic failure mode.
The momentum signal captures SPACs during their "ticker-change pump" or "merger announcement"
phase — exactly when price momentum is temporarily elevated but fundamentals are absent.

**Proposed filter (two-stage):**
1. **Price anchor check:** If current price is within ±15% of $10.00 AND historical price
   shows a $10 flat period in the last 12 months → classify as SPAC candidate
2. **Market cap check:** If market cap < $250M AND listing age < 3 years → require positive
   last-12-months earnings (ROA > 0)

This catches SPACs at $10 NAV while avoiding filtering small legitimate microcaps that
happen to IPO near $10. Implementation: 5-10 lines in `universe.py`, no DB migration.

**D. Rate-Hike Protected Sleeve — BofA 3-Hike Regime Defense**

Given BofA's September/October/December 2026 hike forecast, a sleeve specifically optimized
for rate-hiking environments would complement the existing factor portfolios:

- **Signal:** ROA > 15% (very high quality) + 6-month momentum (shorter lookback to dodge
  duration-sensitive value traps) + SIC sector exclusions (no utilities, no REITs, no
  long-duration growth)
- **Universe:** S&P 500 constituents only (quality anchor against penny stocks in hike regime)
- **Expected behavior:** Overweights community banks (wider NIM), energy (commodity inflation
  hedge), industrials (capex beneficiary), and profitable tech
- **Pre-condition:** BofA forecast holds through July FOMC; backtest on 2004-2006 and 2022-2023
  hike cycles to validate

**Note:** This is a research proposal only. The ROA filter in our existing sleeves already
provides significant rate-hike defense. A dedicated sleeve would only be worth building if
the backtested alpha exceeds what mom_roa_6535 already delivers.

**E. Micron Earnings Cadence as Portfolio Signal**

Tonight establishes an important reference point: Micron reports quarterly. Their guidance
and actual numbers are a direct read on AI memory demand. The next MU earnings will be
approximately September 24, 2026 (Q4 FY2026). Given tonight's Q4 guidance of $50B ± $1B,
the next report will test whether the AI capex cycle continues to accelerate. This date
should be pre-marked for both the rebalance calendar and the LLM overlay evaluation.

### 2. PCE INFLATION -- MAY 2026: HAWKISH SHOCK (4.1% Headline / 3.4% Core)

**Released 8:30am ET June 25.** This is the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge.

| Metric | May 2026 | April 2026 | Fed Target | Context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Headline PCE (YoY) | **4.1%** | 3.8% | 2.0% | Highest since April 2023 |
| Core PCE (YoY) | **3.4%** | 3.3% | 2.0% | Highest since October 2023 |
| Headline PCE (MoM) | **+0.4%** | -- | ~0.17% | Accelerating |
| Core PCE (MoM) | **+0.3%** | -- | ~0.17% | Sticky |

**This is a stagflationary print.** Inflation is ACCELERATING above target while AI capex
simultaneously booms. The Fed faces conflicting signals:
- Inflation 2x target and rising -> hawkish response
- AI economy running extremely hot -> can't claim demand-side weakness
- BofA's Sep/Oct/Dec 2026 3-hike forecast is now **more likely**, not less

**Why markets are up anyway (pre-open):** The MU earnings beat is being interpreted as proof
that AI capex is structural and rate-insensitive. This view has merit -- hyperscalers build
AI infrastructure because competitors do too (a competitive arms race), not because the Fed
funds rate is low. But the PCE data creates a compression risk on high-multiple growth stocks.

**WDC behavior confirms this tension:** Pre-market $725.70 -> intraday $612-$665 -> close
~$643. The stock gave back ~$80 (11%) from pre-market highs after the PCE print. This
illustrates the dynamic: AI rally + PCE sell-off partially offsetting each other.

| MU, WDC, STX (memory) | POSITIVE (pricing power = inflation hedge) | All 4 systematic |

The ROA filter in our best two sleeves (mom_roa, residual_roa) is functioning as designed:

### 11. Strategic Insights

**A. SPAC Filter -- Technical Implementation Plan (Post-July 1 Priority)**

Two SPACs entered simultaneously at June 3 rebalance (AFJK + FGMC). SPAC volume in 2026 is
3x higher than 2024. The failure mode will recur without an explicit filter.

Proposed minimum implementation (add to `universe.py`, ~10 lines):

```python
# Exclude probable SPACs: price near $10 NAV + small market cap + new listing
SPAC_PRICE_ANCHOR = 10.0
SPAC_PRICE_TOLERANCE = 0.20  # within 20% of $10 (covers $8-$12 range)
SPAC_MAX_MARKET_CAP = 250_000_000  # $250M
SPAC_MAX_AGE_DAYS = 3 * 365  # listed < 3 years

def filter_probable_spacs(df):
    near_nav = (df['price'] - SPAC_PRICE_ANCHOR).abs() / SPAC_PRICE_ANCHOR < SPAC_PRICE_TOLERANCE
    small_cap = df['market_cap'] < SPAC_MAX_MARKET_CAP
    new_listing = df['listing_age_days'] < SPAC_MAX_AGE_DAYS
    return df[~(near_nav & small_cap & new_listing)]
```

This would have excluded both AFJK (trading ~$40 but had ~$10 SPAC history) and FGMC
(entered at $10.38). The price history check (flat $10 period in last 12 months) adds
robustness for SPACs that have already moved from NAV.
