### 1. Market Summary

**Indices (close, 2026-07-07):** Dow Jones Industrial Average 52,925.15 (-130.76, -0.25%); Nasdaq Composite 25,818.69 (-1.16%); S&P 500 7,503.85 (-0.45%). The VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) fell more than 3%. The session reversed Monday's record-Dow rally: chip and chip-equipment names led the market down while broader indices held up comparatively well, consistent with a sector-concentrated rotation rather than a market-wide risk-off move.

**Driver:** Samsung Electronics released preliminary Q2 2026 results showing operating profit of roughly $58B, a 19x YoY jump that beat estimates — yet Samsung shares themselves fell 7% and dragged the complex down with them, as Deutsche Bank flagged the beat was "only" 6% ahead of consensus after a historic 1H 2026 run-up. The selloff's roots trace to early-July reports that SK Hynix was slowing its HBM (high-bandwidth memory) expansion, which the market read as an early signal of cooling AI-chip demand; that, plus reports of China's DeepSeek developing its own AI chip, cascaded through chip-equipment leaders already sitting at stretched valuations. 24/7 Wall St. describes this as the **second week** of a chip-equipment selloff, not a single-day event. Applied Materials -10% to $532, Intel -10%, AMD -8% ("craters," per 24/7 Wall St.), Lam Research -9%, per that same coverage.

**Sector performance (SPDR sector ETFs, 07-06 close → 07-07 close):** Energy (XLE) +2.84% ($53.13→$54.64) — the day's only clearly positive major sector, driven by the Hormuz escalation (see below); Healthcare (XLV) +1.53% ($161.96→$164.44) — continuing 2026's broad biotech/M&A-driven rally; Materials (XLB) -0.90% ($51.98→$51.51) — roughly flat; Industrials (XLI) -1.71% ($185.56→$182.38); Technology (XLK) -2.39% ($183.57→$179.18) — the session's laggard, consistent with the chip-equipment rout concentrated there.

**Macro/geopolitical — Strait of Hormuz escalation, now the dominant cross-portfolio macro story:** Two vessels were struck by projectiles Tuesday in the Strait of Hormuz per the UK Maritime Trade Operations center — one tanker (hit near Limah, Oman, port side, while transiting south) caught fire; a second ship sustained structural damage with no injuries reported. Iranian state TV, quoting anonymous sources, implied Tehran carried out the strike on a vessel it said was carrying Qatari LNG, without an official claim. The US Treasury published a notice July 7 revoking the general licenses (issued 06-21) that had authorized Iranian crude/petrochemical/petroleum sales, effectively phasing out that sanctions relief. Late Tuesday, US Central Command said it had launched "powerful strikes" against Iran in response to the attacks on commercial shipping, per the Washington Post — a sharp escalation from Monday's single-incident framing in yesterday's report. WTI crude rose 2.8% in regular trading to $70.44, then jumped a further 5.4% to $72.25 after-hours as the news of US strikes broke.

**Rates/data calendar:** No FOMC, CPI, or jobs releases fell on 2026-07-07. The June jobs report was released Thursday 07-02; FOMC minutes are due Wednesday 07-08 (expected to detail the dot plot's shift toward a possible 2026 hike); June CPI — the last major inflation print before the 07-29 FOMC decision — lands 07-14.

### 4. LLM Overlay Treatment vs. Control — Day 1 of Live Trading

**This is the actual first live trading day for all 6 LLM-experiment sleeves** (`mom_roa_top1_paper`, `llm_overlay_mom_roa_top1_paper`, `llm_cascade_top1_paper`, `sector_top4_paper`, `llm_overlay_sector_top4_paper`, `llm_cascade_sector4_paper`), deployed today via the one-time `cohort-0706-deploy` scheduled task (see Project Record Appendix AV for full mechanics). Prior "flat at $100k" states in earlier reports do not count toward the 12-month/30-pick kill-switch clock — that clock starts now.

**Stock arm:**
- **Control (`mom_roa_top1_paper`) bought BE (Bloom Energy)** at $263.94 (score 8.80 — this is the raw momentum score, not an LLM judgment; control always buys the #1 pick) — because the control sleeve has no veto mechanism by design.
- **Overlay treatment (`llm_overlay_mom_roa_top1_paper`) VETO'd BE**, score 4/10, citing ~128x forward P/E (~19x NTM revenue) vs. a peer median near 6x, a price ($263.81 at decision time) already above the $181.79 consensus analyst target, -23.7% off its 52-week high and below its 50-DMA, with Q2 earnings not until 07-28 setting a high bar into an already-stretched valuation — the log calls it a "textbook momentum blow-off now rolling over." **Early result: BE fell from Monday's $295.05 close to roughly $263.81–263.94 by the time of the decision (~13:00 CDT) — a further ~10.5% intraday drop — before recovering modestly to close at $269.57.** The stock ended the day above its entry price for the control (+2.13% control return today), but well below Monday's close, and the overlay's cash position avoided the intraday trough. One session is not a verdict, but it's the first data point in the veto's favor.
- **Cascade (`llm_cascade_top1_paper`) walked past the BE veto to WDC**, score 6/10, BUY, at $527.85, invalidation $480. Rationale distinguishes WDC from BE on durability: HDD capacity sold out through 2026 with multi-year hyperscale customer contracts into 2027–2028 (real revenue visibility vs. BE's "unlocked guidance"), 30x forward P/E vs. a 16x tech-sector average (elevated but not extreme). WDC had already fallen from Monday's $577.46 close to the ~$528 entry (~8.6% intraday drop) before the cascade bought — i.e., the cascade bought into the same day's chip-equipment/memory rout, then recovered modestly to close at $532.10 (+0.80% since entry).

**Sector arm:**
- **Control (`sector_top4_paper`) bought all 4 top-momentum sectors** including XLE (score 0.35, momentum-only, no LLM judgment) at $54.03.
- **Overlay treatment (`llm_overlay_sector_top4_paper`) VETO'd XLE**, score 3/10, citing technicals below the 50-DMA with RSI 38, negative 1-month (-8.1%) and 3-month (-9.5%) momentum, -13.7% off its 52-week high, and a bearish EIA 2026 demand outlook (global demand -1.1mb/d, rising non-OPEC+ supply); the log explicitly flags "near-term Hormuz-driven supply cuts are a fragile geopolitical prop that could reverse fast." **XLE was the single best-performing sector ETF of the session, +2.84%, directly on the Hormuz escalation the veto's own rationale anticipated as a risk.** This is a same-day miss for the veto in pure return terms, though the underlying thesis (a geopolitical spike is not a durable reason to hold an otherwise-weak sector) is exactly the kind of call this experiment exists to test over many decisions, not one day. XLK/XLI/XLB (the 3 held slots) were unchanged vs. control.
- **Cascade (`llm_cascade_sector4_paper`) walked to a 5th-ranked pick, XLV (Health Care)**, score 7/10, HOLD, to fill its 4th slot after XLE's veto — citing strong rotation into healthcare (9.6% above 50-DMA, at its 52-week high, GLP-1/oncology earnings strength) against an overbought RSI of 72.2 as the flagged near-term risk. XLV gained +1.53% today, participating in the broad biotech rally described in Section 3 — an early point in the cascade's favor.

**Kill switch reminder:** unchanged — 12 months or ≥30 logged picks, drop the overlay/cascade arm if scores don't predict forward returns or treatment doesn't beat control. Today is trading day 1 of that window for real.

### 5. Week / Period Summary

The week opened with Monday's record Dow close (chip-led rally, Yahoo/TheStreet) and closed Tuesday with the fourth-plus reversal in this complex since the late-June chip-selloff regime began — this time driven by a specific, sourced catalyst (Samsung's earnings "sell the news" + SK Hynix HBM-slowdown reports + DeepSeek AI-chip development) rather than the more diffuse macro unease of prior swings. 24/7 Wall St. frames this as the **second week** of an ongoing chip-equipment selloff, suggesting the whipsaw pattern flagged in the last three reports may be entering a more sustained corrective phase rather than resolving either way. Separately, the Strait of Hormuz situation escalated materially within 24 hours — from a single tanker strike (07-06/07-07 morning) to two vessels hit and, by Tuesday evening, US military strikes on Iran — a much faster and larger escalation than the "watch" framing in this morning's pre-market report anticipated.

### 6. Strategic Insights

**A. residual_roa_6535's resilience pattern held again, with a clean mechanistic explanation visible in today's sector data.** Its -1.59% day move against -3.83% to -4.65% for the other three systematic sleeves is directly attributable to its 25.9% Technology weight (vs. 51–58% for the others) plus a genuine 16.5% Energy book (APA, XOM, NRT) that gained today on the same Hormuz spike that hurt nothing else in the portfolio. This is now four-plus consecutive sessions of the same pattern (see the 07-02 through 07-06 reports) — strengthening, not just repeating, the case that its dual-signal construction does real diversification work rather than having been lucky at inception.

**B. The 07-06-cohort vs. base-May-sleeve divergence today is a clean, real-time illustration of monthly-rebalance timing risk, not a strategy difference.** `mom_roa_6535_0701_paper` (+0.35% today) and `mom_roa_6535_paper` (-4.65% today) run the *same* underlying config and largely overlapping names, but the 0701 twin entered its positions today at ~13:00–13:20 CDT — after the morning's chip-equipment rout had already happened — while the base sleeve has held its 07-01-vintage positions since before the selloff began. The two will reconverge in composition next month, but this session is a concrete demonstration of how much a monthly rebalance's *exact day* can matter when a sector correction lands mid-cycle — worth remembering when comparing the 0701 cohort's early performance to the base sleeves' over the coming weeks, since their starting points are not equivalent.

**C. The LLM overlay experiment produced its first two directionally-opposed early data points on day 1 — exactly the kind of split result the experiment is designed to accumulate before any verdict is possible.** The stock overlay's BE veto looks favorable so far (BE fell further intraday before a partial recovery); the sector overlay's XLE veto looks unfavorable so far (XLE was the day's best sector, on the exact geopolitical catalyst the veto's own rationale flagged as a risk it might be wrong about). Both are one-session, directionally-suggestive-only data points against a 12-month/30-pick kill switch — no conclusion follows from either, and the report explicitly declines to draw one.

**D. The Hormuz-to-US-strikes escalation is the second consecutive session where a fast-moving geopolitical event has landed between scheduled rebalance dates, and it has now directly cut both ways within the same sleeve roster** (hurting nothing yet, but helping residual_roa_6535's Energy book while also being the exact scenario the sector overlay's XLE veto tried to price around and got, at least today, wrong). This continues to be a live test of the accepted "no intraday circuit-breaker" design gap (13 prior reactive-stop attempts rejected per `sleeves_verdict.md`) rather than a new finding — flagging it again because the stakes (an actual US-Iran military exchange) are materially higher than yesterday's single-tanker framing.

**E. No new long-term sleeve concept is confirmed or refuted by today's data.** The session supplies more raw material for judging the LLM overlays (2 real decisions each, first actual trading day) and for the residual-momentum diversification thesis, but not enough of either to change the "watch and accumulate more data" posture from prior reports.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**Geopolitical (dominant driver):** Overnight, the US and Iran exchanged fresh strikes after Iranian-linked attacks on two commercial tankers (Qatari LNG carrier Al Rekayat, Saudi supertanker Wedyan) transiting the Strait of Hormuz on 2026-07-07 [Washington Post](https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/2026/07/07/tanker-fire-after-being-struck-strait-hormuz-british-military-says/). The US struck Iranian targets in response; Iran said it targeted more than 80 US military facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/show/u-s-launches-new-strikes-on-iran-after-attacks-on-tankers-in-strait-of-hormuz). Speaking in Ankara ahead of a NATO summit, President Trump said of the ceasefire, "For me, I think it's over," and the Treasury revoked the waiver permitting Iran oil exports [TheStreet](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-july-8-2026). This is a materially bigger escalation than the single-tanker framing in yesterday's (2026-07-07) report — an actual US-Iran exchange of fire, not just a tanker incident.

**Semiconductor sector:** Tuesday's (07-07) rout — Samsung earnings + weak-yield concerns triggering Intel/AMAT -10%, AMD -8%, Micron/SanDisk/WDC -7% moves — is continuing into Wednesday pre-market rather than reversing (MU -3.88%, INTC -1.41% further). A fresh, distinct catalyst emerged overnight: Reuters/US News reported China's DeepSeek is developing an in-house AI inference chip, adding a new competitive-threat narrative on top of the existing memory-cost and AI-capex-bubble concerns already driving the selloff [U.S. News](https://www.usnews.com/news/top-news/articles/2026-07-07/exclusive-chinas-deepseek-developing-its-own-ai-chip-sources-say).

**Macro calendar:** FOMC minutes from the June meeting — the first meeting under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh — are released today, 2026-07-08 [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/economy/this-weeks-economic-calendar). No CPI or jobs report is scheduled this week per the same source. Markets will be watching for signals on how the Fed is weighing the recent energy-driven inflation pressure against a still-hawkish policy stance.

**Bright spot:** DigitalOcean (DOCN, held in 8 sleeves) jumped 7% on 07-07 after pre-announcing record preliminary Q2 results — RPO expected to top $800M, Q2 revenue growth guided up to ~29% YoY from a prior 24-25% guide — plus a Russell 1000 index promotion effective 2026-06-29 [StocksToTrade](https://stockstotrade.com/news/digitalocean-holdings-inc-docn-news-2026_07_07-2/), [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8947660/digitalocean-docn-anticipates-29-revenue-growth-in-q2-shares-rise-10). A genuine idiosyncratic positive inside an otherwise broadly negative tech tape.

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. Today's data reinforces, rather than newly establishes, the residual-momentum diversification thesis.** `residual_roa_6535_paper`'s Energy exposure (~16% of NAV) turning a broad semiconductor-driven down day into the portfolio's best return is the same structural property (idiosyncratic-momentum signal isn't sector-concentrated the way raw price momentum is) documented at deployment in `sleeves_verdict.md` (2026-06-09). Consistent with, not a new discovery beyond, the existing thesis.

**B. The LLM overlay experiment logged its first same-session sweep where BOTH arms' raw controls beat BOTH LLM-mediated variants.** Stock control (+2.13%) beat cascade (+0.80%) and treatment (0.00%); sector control (+0.40%) beat overlay (+0.11%) and cascade (+0.06%). This is one session against a 12-month/30-pick kill switch — directionally suggestive, not remotely conclusive — but it's the cleanest single-day sweep against the LLM approach the experiment has produced since the 07-01 reset, and it's happening on exactly the kind of day (a fast, geopolitically-driven move) where a rules-free discretionary overlay might be expected to add the most value by avoiding a bad pick. It didn't, this time — worth tracking whether this is noise or a pattern as more sessions accumulate.

**C. The XLE veto is now 0-for-2 on directional accuracy across the two sessions it's applied (07-07 close and, if oil holds its overnight gain, 07-08 pre-market), while explicitly having named the exact risk (a geopolitical premium reversing) that so far hasn't reversed.** This doesn't mean the veto's macro reasoning is wrong — a geopolitical premium is fundamentally fragile by definition, and being right eventually doesn't require being right on any single day — but two sessions of the stated risk running the wrong way is worth flagging as the small-sample evidence accumulates.

**D. No new long-term sleeve concept is confirmed or refuted by this session's data.** No new positions were opened or closed since 07-07 close; the report is pre-market with no fresh trade data to evaluate. The "watch and accumulate more data" posture from the 2026-07-07 report is unchanged.

### 4. LLM Overlay Treatment vs. Control

**The stock arm flipped today.** After Tuesday's clean sweep where the raw controls beat both LLM variants on both arms, Wednesday reversed the stock arm decisively:

**Stock arm (day, 07-07→07-08):**
- **Control `mom_roa_top1_paper` (BE): -5.66%** — the concentrated BE bet took the full brunt of continued profit-taking.
- **Cascade `llm_cascade_top1_paper` (WDC): +3.42%** — WDC rebounded on the Goldman upgrade.
- **Treatment `llm_overlay_mom_roa_top1_paper` (cash): 0.00%** — avoided BE's drop entirely.
- **Result:** both LLM-mediated variants beat the raw control today. **Over the full 3-day cohort life (07-06→07-08): cascade +4.25% > treatment 0.00% > control -3.65%.** The BE veto (score 4/10, logged 06-30 and re-affirmed 07-07) is now clearly vindicated on the sample so far: **BE has gone $295.05 (Mon close) → $254.29 (Wed close), -13.8%**, while the vetoing treatment sat in cash and the cascade's alternative pick (WDC) rose. One cohort-week is still far short of the 30-pick/12-month kill-switch window, but this is the first multi-day stretch where the discretionary overlay has added visible value.

**Sector arm (day, 07-07→07-08):**
- **Control `sector_top4_paper` (holds XLE): -0.17%** — XLE +1.76% again cushioned the control.
- **Overlay treatment `llm_overlay_sector_top4_paper` (no XLE): -0.62%.**
- **Cascade `llm_cascade_sector4_paper` (XLV instead of XLE): -0.94%** — XLV -1.30% was a double drag (missed XLE's gain, ate XLV's loss).
- **Result:** control still beat both, a third straight session. **The XLE veto (score 3/10) is now 0-for-3 on directional day-return**, with oil continuing to rise on exactly the "fragile geopolitical prop" the veto flagged — a prop that has strengthened, not reversed, across all three sessions. This remains a durable-vs-fragile thesis call, not a day-trade, but the small-sample scoreboard runs against it.

No new overlay/cascade decisions were logged 07-08 (checked `llm_overlay_log`/`sector_overlay_log`; latest entries remain 07-07). Kill-switch status unchanged on both arms.

### 5. Week / Period Summary (2026-07-06 → 07-08)

The 07-06 cohort's first three trading days captured a full whipsaw:
- **Mon 07-06:** chip-led rally, record Dow; base sleeves peaked (residual $106,660, mom_roa_6535 $101,717).
- **Tue 07-07:** Samsung-earnings-triggered chip/memory rout; base momentum sleeves fell 3.8–4.7% in a single session.
- **Wed 07-08:** partial reversal — chip-equipment and AI-infra names bounced, energy led on oil, but the Dow still fell 1.1% and the base momentum sleeves only stabilized flat (they did not recoup Tuesday's loss).

Net over the three days, the raw momentum book (mom_v1/v2/mom_roa base) sits roughly 3.5–4% below Monday's peak, while `residual_roa_6535_paper`'s energy diversification let it recover to a fresh cohort high (+6.05%). The macro backdrop hardened: the FOMC minutes revealed a genuinely split committee with **half its members open to a hike**, and the Hormuz situation kept a persistent oil bid alive — both headwinds for a long-duration, tech-heavy momentum portfolio.

### 6. Strategic Insights — Structural Edge or New Sleeve Concepts?

**A. residual_roa_6535's diversification thesis logged its cleanest two-way confirmation yet.** On Tuesday its energy book cushioned the chip rout (-1.59% vs -3.8/-4.7%); on Wednesday that same book turned a down-tape (Dow -1.1%) into a +1.03% gain and a fresh cohort high. This is the *mechanism* — an idiosyncratic-momentum signal that isn't sector-concentrated — doing exactly what `sleeves_verdict.md` (2026-06-09) predicted at deployment, now across a genuine two-sided stress test rather than a single lucky day. Still a confirmation of the existing thesis, not a new finding, but the evidence is strengthening.

**B. The LLM stock overlay produced its first genuinely favorable multi-day data point.** Yesterday's report flagged a clean control-beats-both sweep; today reversed the stock arm hard, and the 3-day cumulative (cascade +4.25% > treatment 0.00% > control -3.65%) now favors the discretionary variants — specifically because the overlay's BE veto correctly identified a "textbook momentum blow-off," and BE has since fallen 13.8%. This is the single strongest piece of pro-overlay evidence the experiment has produced. **Caveat:** it hinges entirely on one name (BE) in a one-position control, so it is high-variance and nowhere near the 30-pick threshold. The honest read: the experiment is doing its job — accumulating decisions where the LLM's veto is being scored against the counterfactual — and the early scoreboard is now split (stock overlay ahead, sector overlay behind).

**C. The sector overlay's XLE veto is 0-for-3 but not yet falsified.** The veto's logic (a geopolitical premium is fragile and XLE's technicals were weak) is a multi-week thesis; three days of oil rising on an escalating US-Iran conflict is precisely the fragile-prop scenario it named and expected it might get wrong short-term. The right posture is to keep scoring it, not to conclude — but if XLE's strength persists past the geopolitical spike, this becomes the first candidate for the kill-switch's "scores don't predict returns" test.

**D. FOMC-minutes hawkishness is the newest structural risk to the momentum book, and no sleeve hedges it.** Half the committee is open to a hike, with inflation risks tilted up on energy — a regime that historically compresses long-duration/high-multiple momentum names, which dominate every systematic sleeve except residual (via its energy weight) and the sector sleeves. This is not a new sleeve concept, but it sharpens the case that the portfolio's only genuine macro diversifier right now is residual's energy exposure — everything else is effectively one long-momentum, long-duration bet.

**E. No new long-term-viable sleeve concept is confirmed or refuted by today's data.** The session added real decision-data to the LLM overlays (now split) and a strong second data point for residual's diversification, but nothing sufficient to propose or retire a sleeve. Watch-and-accumulate posture unchanged.

### 3. Key Position Analysis

#### A. Semiconductor sector — the day's dominant theme, driven by Micron's $250B announcement

The reported chip bounce flagged as unconfirmed in this morning's pre-market report is now confirmed at the close, and it was much bigger than a generic rebound — it was driven by a specific, dated catalyst: **Micron committed more than $250 billion to U.S. chipmaking through 2035**, adding $50B to its existing $200B pledge (New York/Idaho/Virginia fabs) plus up to $3B for the broader U.S. semiconductor supply chain, aiming for 40% domestic DRAM production within a decade. The company poured first concrete at its Clay, NY site the same day [CNBC — Micron stock pops on more US investment](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/09/micron-stock-us-chipmaking.html), [Bloomberg — Micron boosts US spending to $250 billion](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-09/micron-boosts-us-spending-to-250-billion-amid-memory-demand).

### 4. LLM Overlay Treatment vs. Control

No new overlay/cascade decisions were logged 07-09 (`llm_overlay_log`/`sector_overlay_log` checked directly; latest entries remain 07-07 — consistent with no rebalance cycle). All figures below are the informal/unofficial marks from §2, clearly not the pipeline's own output.

**Stock arm:** Bloom Energy (`mom_roa_top1_paper`'s sole holding) drew a new, material development today: short-seller **Hunterbrook Capital** disclosed a short position and alleged BE understated its reliance on Chinese suppliers for scandium (used in its fuel cells), questioning whether BE can secure enough scandium oxide for its long-term manufacturing targets. Bloom "categorically rejected" the claims as "false and misleading," reasserted its 25 GW/year production capability, and the stock — after trading as low as $235.64 intraday — closed at $257.02, **+1.07% on the day** [Seeking Alpha — Bloom Energy rebounds after rejecting short-seller claims](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4612638-bloom-energy-rebounds-after-rejecting-short-seller-claims), [GuruFocus — Bloom Energy rebounds 7.4% amid rejection of short-seller claims](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8951520/bloom-energy-be-rebounds-74-amid-rejection-of-shortseller-claims). This is a new, named risk layered on top of the still-unresolved 07-28-vs-07-30 earnings-date conflict, and it is exactly the kind of idiosyncratic single-name risk the overlay's original BE veto (score 4/10) was designed to avoid — the treatment sidestepped it entirely by sitting in cash. Informal cohort standing (07-06 inception): **cascade (WDC) $109,501 (+9.50%) > treatment (cash) $100,000 (0.00%) > control (BE) $97,380 (-2.62%)** — unchanged ranking from 07-08, control still trailing both LLM-mediated variants.

**Sector arm — first daily flip in the veto's favor:** Control `sector_top4_paper` (holds XLE) informally +0.33% today; overlay treatment (no XLE) +0.70%; cascade (XLV instead of XLE) +0.68%. **Both LLM variants beat the raw control for the first time since the 07-06 cohort inception**, because XLE was the only one of the four sector ETFs to fall today (-1.40%), exactly the reversal the original veto rationale flagged as possible ("a fragile geopolitical prop that could reverse fast"). The XLE veto's scoreboard moves from 0-for-3 to (informally) 1-for-4 on directional accuracy. Informal cohort standing: control $100,556 (+0.56%) > overlay $100,190 (+0.19%) > cascade $99,794 (-0.21%) — the control still leads cumulatively, but the gap narrowed today rather than widened for the first time. One day does not resolve a multi-week thesis; still far short of the 30-pick kill-switch threshold.

### 6. Strategic Insights — Structural Edge or New Sleeve Concepts?

**A. The M2.2 coverage gate just did its job for the first time, and that is itself the most important operational finding of the day.** Deployed at 13:30 today, it caught a real ~16% shortfall in the daily price publication at 17:17 and correctly refused to mark 17 sleeves against incomplete data rather than silently producing a wrong NAV. This validates the ops-infrastructure investment (M2 series: coverage gate, anomaly detector, cache-gap auditor) exactly as designed. It also leaves a genuine open question this report cannot answer: does the pipeline retry coverage tomorrow and simply never backfill an official 07-09 NAV, or does something need to be re-run manually? That is an operational decision for Evan, not something this report should attempt or assume.

**B. The sector-arm LLM veto scored its first directional win today, right after the FOMC-minutes/Hormuz thesis had gone 0-for-3 against it.** The XLE veto's stated worry — that the Hormuz-driven oil premium was "fragile" and could reverse fast — is exactly what happened today (oil fell despite continued strikes, XLE was the sole losing sector ETF). This is one data point, not a trend reversal, and the control still leads the cohort cumulatively, but it is the first session where the pattern flagged in the last two reports (control winning every day) broke.

**C. Micron's $250B announcement is a distinct, larger catalyst than the "generic oversold bounce" this morning's pre-market report could only describe directionally** — it explains why today's chip rally (SMH +2.5%, several held names +5-11%) was materially bigger than Wednesday's partial reversal. This reinforces the observation (flagged 07-08) that the momentum book's heaviest concentration (semiconductors/memory/AI-infrastructure) continues to swing on dated, idiosyncratic company news as much as on macro sentiment — a three-session round-trip (rout → partial bounce → confirmed rally) that has now resolved to the upside, at least for one day.

**D. Bloom Energy's short-seller episode adds a new, specific tail-risk to the single largest concentration position in the book** (`mom_roa_top1_paper` is 100% BE, no stop by design). The stock absorbed the attack and closed positive, which is mild evidence the market didn't find the scandium-supply-chain allegations credible enough to sell into — but it is a fresh, named risk that didn't exist in prior reports and is worth tracking alongside the earnings-date conflict.

**E. No new long-term-viable sleeve concept is confirmed or refuted by today's data.** The day's real news was operational (the coverage gate) and about existing theses gaining or losing evidence (residual's diversification, both LLM overlay arms), not about a new sleeve idea. Watch-and-accumulate posture unchanged.

**SK Hynix US IPO — the day's dominant single event.** SK Hynix raised $26.5B in the largest-ever US listing by a foreign company; shares priced at $149 and traded around $170-173 midday, a 14-17% pop. Demand was reportedly >7x the shares offered (~$185B in orders). SK Hynix supplies high-bandwidth memory to Nvidia and other AI-hardware makers, positioning it as a direct Micron competitor — sources describe the semiconductor sector "splitting into winners and losers based on AI proximity," with SK Hynix/Nvidia on one side. VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) reported +2.5%, Micron +4.5%, SanDisk +7.6% per midday reporting — though our own `price_cache` shows MU essentially flat (-0.28%) 07-09→07-10 near-close, a discrepancy likely explained by the two figures being measured from different reference points (midday-vs-midday move vs. our prior-close-to-near-close snapshot); not reconciled further given time constraints. ### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. The diversification-vs-concentration pattern from the 07-08/07-09 reports held again today, on a calmer macro tape.** With the broad market flat-to-up and no acute portfolio-specific shock, the diversified sleeves (`spy_benchmark` +4.78%, `sector_top4_full` +3.25%, `residual_roa_6535` +6.33% informal since-inception) still comfortably outperform the concentrated momentum book (0701-cohort momentum sleeves +1.4-2.0%, legacy momentum sleeves -1.5% to -3.9%, both dragged by DOCN's single-name -6.99% today). This is now consistent across a volatile session (07-07/08), a mixed session (07-09), and a calm session (07-10) — the pattern isn't just a crisis-alpha story, it holds on ordinary days too, which is a somewhat stronger claim than what the 07-08/07-09 reports could support. Still not a new finding, but the sample is thickening in the diversification thesis's favor.

**B. The LLM stock-overlay's WDC cascade pick is now the best-performing sleeve in the entire 17-sleeve roster** (+10.52% informal since 07-06, vs. the next-best `residual_roa_6535_paper` at +6.33%). One name over four trading days is a small sample and today's WDC gain was driven by a single analyst price-target raise (Wells Fargo, +27% target increase) rather than fundamentals shifting — worth resisting the urge to over-read this as validating the overlay concept broadly; the kill-switch's 30-pick threshold exists precisely because single-name, few-day performance is noisy. The more informative comparison remains cascade-vs-control-vs-cash on the *same* underlying signal, which continues to favor the LLM veto (BE) and BUY (WDC) decisions.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** SK Hynix's IPO is a notable one-off market-structure event (largest foreign US listing ever) rather than a repeatable signal; nothing here suggests a new systematic edge distinct from what's already being tracked (idiosyncratic-momentum diversification, LLM veto/BUY discretion). Today's honest read: the portfolio's known mechanisms behaved as expected, no surprises, no new evidence either direction on kill-switch thresholds.

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

No new evidence either direction since Friday's report; today's status check surfaces one dated, trackable setup rather than a new finding:

**A. The XLE control-vs-veto divergence is now a live, real-world test, not a hypothetical.** The 07-07 sector-overlay veto of XLE was made on valuation/momentum grounds (below 50-DMA, RSI 38, EIA demand cut, negative 1m/3m) explicitly *despite* acknowledging "near-term supply cuts are a fragile geopolitical prop that could reverse fast." That prop is being tested directly by this weekend's Hormuz closure and third round of US strikes — a genuine escalation, not the on-again-off-again ceasefire noise of the prior week. If energy equities rally hard on the supply shock Monday, the systematic control sleeves (holding XLE) would benefit while the LLM-overlay sleeves (which excluded it) would not — a clean, dated comparison to watch, not a conclusion to draw yet.

**B. The diversification-vs-concentration pattern (flagged in the 07-08 through 07-10 reports) has no new data point today** — no trading occurred. The pattern's next real test is Monday 07-13.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed.** The weekend's dominant news (Hormuz escalation, bank/semi earnings ahead) is exogenous macro/geopolitical risk already within the scope of existing sector and momentum sleeves' natural exposure — nothing here suggests a new systematic signal distinct from what's already tracked.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**Iran / Strait of Hormuz — escalated further over the weekend, not resolved.** After Saturday's report described the Strait as declared "closed until further notice," the situation worsened: the US struck roughly 140 Iranian military targets overnight 07-11→07-12, followed by a further wave beginning ~5pm ET 07-12 hitting air-defense systems and IRGC small boats near Hormuz; Iran retaliated against US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Jordan, Oman, and Qatar, and a security guard was killed by a projectile strike on a water-pumping station in Mahshahr County, Iran. [Bloomberg — US says it began launching more strikes against Iran at 5pm ET](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-12/us-says-it-began-launching-more-strikes-against-iran-at-5pm-et), [Al Jazeera — US launches new wave of strikes against Iran aimed at degrading military](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/12/us-launches-new-wave-of-strikes-against-iran-aimed-at-degrading-military). Into Monday, both sides traded fresh strikes — the US using one-way attack drones for the first time — while Trump/CENTCOM claim the Strait is open and Iran's strait authority says passage is "not possible"; Iran's Foreign Ministry called the strikes a "serious threat to international peace and security." [CNBC — US-Iran war, Hormuz, oil, Trump](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/13/us-iran-war-hormuz-oil-trump.html), [Bloomberg — US and Iran trade fresh strikes, dispute whether Hormuz is open](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-13/us-and-iran-trade-fresh-strikes-dispute-whether-hormuz-is-open). Only ~14 vessels (half Iranian-flagged) were transiting Hormuz as of last weekend, well below normal. [The National — Is the US-Iran ceasefire over? A timeline](https://www.thenationalnews.com/news/2026/07/09/is-us-iran-ceasefire-over-a-timeline-of-how-agreement-has-come-to-brink-of-collapse/)

**Fed leadership / rate path — a flagged discrepancy, not resolved.** Saturday's report (sourced to a CNBC 07-10 "week ahead" piece) cited "futures currently price a 61% chance of a September cut per CME FedWatch." Today's research instead surfaces that the Fed is now chaired by **Kevin Warsh**, confirmed mid-June 2026 as Jerome Powell's replacement, and turned hawkish: the Fed held rates 06-17 but signaled hikes ahead, and CME FedWatch reportedly priced **60-67% odds of a September rate hike** (not cut) after Warsh's 06-18 press conference, up from 27-49% pre-meeting. No current (07-13) rate-cut probability was found in this research pass. **These two claims — a 61% cut odds and a 60-67% hike odds — are contradictory and this report does not attempt to resolve which is stale or in error; flagged for Evan to reconcile before either is cited again.** Separately confirmed: 10-year Treasury yield was 4.56-4.57% at Friday 07-10 close. ### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. The diversification-vs-concentration pattern (flagged 07-08 through 07-11) faces its first real stress test this week, not just a calm-day confirmation.** Prior reports noted diversified sleeves (`spy_benchmark`, `sector_top4_full`, `residual_roa_6535`) beating the concentrated momentum book on both volatile and calm sessions. This week adds a genuinely new stressor — a sector-specific memory-chip selloff (SK Hynix) layered on top of the ongoing Hormuz/oil shock — hitting the momentum book's heaviest concentration (WDC/MU/semiconductor names) directly. If the pattern holds through a week with two simultaneous, unrelated shocks rather than one, that would be somewhat stronger evidence than anything gathered so far; if it breaks, that's informative too. No conclusion drawn today — Monday's close is the first real data point.

**B. The sector-arm LLM veto's XLE exclusion is being tested by conflicting forces simultaneously, which complicates rather than clarifies the read.** The 07-07 veto rationale explicitly worried the Hormuz oil premium was "fragile" and could reverse — instead it has intensified for a second consecutive week. Ordinarily that would be expected to favor the control (XLE holder) this week. But the same morning brings a memory-chip-driven tech selloff that both the control and overlay/cascade sleeves are equally exposed to (both hold XLK). The net effect on the sector-arm comparison specifically is not something this report can predict — worth checking directly once 07-13 closes.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** The week's news (Hormuz re-escalation, SK Hynix's reversal, a Fed-chair discrepancy needing reconciliation, and a genuinely heavy earnings/data calendar) is exogenous macro/company-specific risk already within the scope of existing sleeve mechanisms — nothing here suggests a new systematic signal distinct from what's already tracked. The more actionable finding today is operational: the WDC/cascade stop-enforcement gap in §5, which is a process question for Evan rather than a research finding about markets.

### 6. Strategic insights

**A. The sector-arm XLE veto cost the overlay/cascade sleeves real, measurable return today — the cleanest single-session read this comparison has produced.** The 07-07 decision to exclude XLE (on valuation/technical grounds, while explicitly flagging the oil-premium risk as "fragile") is now down a combined ~0.3-0.8pp against the control on this one session alone, driven entirely by the Hormuz-shipping-blockade announcement. This is exactly the risk the veto's own rationale anticipated could materialize — it materialized. One session isn't a verdict on the veto's process (a geopolitical supply shock is a poor test of a valuation-based sector call), but it's a real, dated data point against the LLM sector-overlay's stock-picking edge so far.

**B. The diversification-vs-concentration pattern extended through its first genuinely dual-shock session.** Flagged 07-08 through this morning: diversified sleeves (`residual_roa_6535`, `spy_benchmark`, `sector_top4_full`) again outperformed the concentrated momentum book (-4.1% to -4.9% today) on a day with two simultaneous, unrelated shocks (chip selloff + oil spike) rather than one. This is now five-plus sessions of the same pattern holding under different shock types — still not proof of a structural edge (concentration risk showing up as expected volatility isn't itself informative about long-run returns), but the pattern has not broken once since it was first flagged.

**C. No new sleeve concept proposed.** Today's moves are squarely within the existing framework: a geopolitical oil shock and a sector-specific chip-valuation unwind, both mechanisms the current sleeves are already built to be exposed to (via sector ETFs and momentum-driven stock selection respectively). The one process item worth flagging again is the cascade stop-enforcement gap (§5) — an operational decision for Evan, not a new research finding.

**June CPI — a materially cooler-than-expected print, the dominant catalyst of the morning.** Released 8:30am ET: headline **-0.4% MoM, +3.5% YoY** vs. consensus of -0.2% MoM / +3.8% YoY; core (ex food/energy) **0.0% MoM, +2.6% YoY** vs. +0.2% MoM / +2.9% YoY consensus (May core was 2.9%) — a decline in energy prices plus easing services/housing costs were the cited drivers (CNBC, 2026-07-14, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/14/consumer-price-index-inflation-report-june-2026.html). Futures reaction as of ~7:39am CDT (Yahoo Finance live blog, 2026-07-14, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-july-14-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-070833816.html): Dow -0.34% (52,586, -178), S&P 500 -0.22% (7,546, -17), Nasdaq +0.17% (29,526.50, +50.75) — a muted/mixed reaction given bond markets had already been pricing in hike risk ahead of the release.

**June PPI is NOT releasing today** — correcting an assumption in today's research brief: BLS has June PPI scheduled for **2026-07-15**, tomorrow, not today. The most recent actual PPI print remains May 2026 (final demand +1.1% MoM, +6.5% YoY, largest 12-month rise since Nov 2022 — BLS, https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_06112026.htm). Do not cite a "June PPI" figure until tomorrow's report.

**Bank earnings, pre-market:** JPMorgan beat sharply — EPS **$6.14** vs. $5.85 consensus, revenue **$58.02B** vs. $50.19B consensus, described as one of JPM's largest beats in recent history and the "highest quarterly profit in US banking history" (Yahoo Finance live page, CNBC live-updates, 2026-07-14, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/14/jpm-bank-of-america-citi-bank-earnings-live-updates.html). Wells Fargo also beat: EPS **$2.00** vs. $1.72 estimate. Citigroup was described qualitatively as a "turnaround" quarter with no exact figures found. **Goldman Sachs and Bank of America exact EPS/revenue figures were not found** in this research pass — both are described generally as "positive"/"strong," which this report will not convert into specific numbers without a direct source.

**Fed Chair Kevin Warsh testifies before the House Financial Services Committee today, 10:00am ET** (day one of two — Senate Banking Committee tomorrow, 07-15, after the PPI release). Prepared testimony reportedly calls this "a hinge point in history," stating the Fed needs "humility about what we know — and the courage to revisit our prior views," and "if we get policy right ... the inflation surge of the last five years will be a thing of the past" (source: financial-news aggregation of prepared remarks, 2026-07-14; CNN live-updates page, https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/14/business/live-news/cpi-inflation-kevin-warsh-capitol-hill-testimony). Lawmakers are reportedly expected to press him on Fed independence from the White House. No post-testimony market reaction distinct from the CPI-driven futures move was found as of this research (testimony had not yet concluded).

**Rate-path discrepancy (flagged Monday) — partially clarified, still not fully resolved.** Pre-CPI, July-hike odds had climbed to roughly 50% from under 10%, driven partly by hawkish comments from Fed Governor Christopher Waller (Bloomberg, 2026-07-14, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-14/fed-rate-hike-bets-mount-before-inflation-data-warsh-testimony). Post the cooler CPI print, one source (exact methodology/publisher unclear) put July-hike odds back down to roughly 17% from roughly 42% Monday. A separate Kalshi-based source from 07-09 (CNBC, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/09/kalshi-traders-see-roughly-50percent-odds-of-a-rate-hike-in-2026-as-fed-is-split-on-policy.html) had traders at ~50% odds of a hike sometime in 2026. **No current source was found citing any "rate cut" probability** — every current reference is to hike odds, which supports treating Saturday's "61% September cut" framing as stale, but no single clean same-methodology CME FedWatch snapshot was found to formally supersede it. Treat as resolved-in-direction (hike framing, not cut framing, is current) but not resolved-in-magnitude.

### 5. Risk flags and upcoming events

- **WDC's reported pre-market reversal needs same-day confirmation before being treated as real.** If genuine, it resolves Monday's sub-$560 stop concern for the cascade sleeve; if it's a sourcing artifact, the sleeve's largest position may still be sitting below its stated stop levels with no automated enforcement (unchanged gap, first flagged 2026-07-13: no `check-invalidation`-equivalent exists for either cascade sleeve).
- **AEHR reports after today's close** (6 sleeves hold it) — consensus EPS -$0.02, revenue $18.69M; prior quarter's pattern was an EPS beat paired with a revenue miss, so a repeat mixed print is plausible and this report does not predict the outcome.
- **Rate-path discrepancy** (§3) is directionally clarified (hike framing is current, not cut) but not magnitude-resolved — avoid citing a specific probability until a single clean source is found.
- **Iran/Hormuz risk has escalated again**, now with a concrete new mechanism (the 20% cargo toll) rather than just rhetoric — this is the fourth consecutive report flagging this as the dominant unhedged macro risk, and it has not abated once across that span.
- **07-13 coverage remains PENDING** (4,386/5,241 baseline closes per the last `mtm_catchup` run) — official NAV is still anchored at 07-10; all 07-13 figures in this report remain self-computed, not verify-confirmed.
- **EACO/KFII** (residual_roa_6535 sleeves) remain the recurring stale-price NOCLOSE anomaly — immaterial, thin micro-caps, unresolved but not escalating.
- **Monthly rebalance** next fires 2026-08-01 per the `monthy-llm-rebalance` scheduled task; no activity since 07-01.

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. Today is the first "good macro news" data point after a string of bad ones, and it's a genuine test of the diversification-vs-concentration pattern from the other direction.** Every prior instance of that pattern (flagged 07-08 through 07-13) involved a shock hitting the concentrated momentum book harder than the diversified sleeves. A cooler CPI print plus bank-earnings beats is, directionally, good news — if the pattern is really about volatility exposure rather than a one-way bad-news bias, today should show the concentrated sleeves (cascade especially, if the WDC reversal is real) outperforming on the way up too. That would be more informative than another down day confirming the same thing again.

**B. The rate-path whipsaw itself (sub-10% to ~50% to ~17% hike odds within days) is arguably more consequential to the sector arm's framework than any single stock-specific headline this week.** The sector LLM overlay is explicitly trying to synthesize macro regime shifts into sector allocation; a week where the market's own rate-hike probability estimate swings by 40+ percentage points in under 72 hours is close to the hardest possible test case for that framework, independent of how the Hormuz/oil story resolves.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** CPI, bank earnings, and Fed testimony are all within the scope of existing macro exposure already embedded in the sector-arm design; nothing here suggests a new systematic signal. The one process item still open is the cascade stop-enforcement gap (§5), unchanged from Monday — an operational decision for Evan, not a research finding.

The week was dominated by two shocks in opposite directions: the SK Hynix/chip-complex rout (Monday, hit all momentum sleeves for -4% to -4.8% single-day) and today's CPI-driven relief rally (recovered roughly half of Monday's damage across the momentum book in one session). Net effect over the week: diversified/value-tilted sleeves (residual, sector, SPY benchmarks) stayed flat-to-positive throughout; concentrated momentum sleeves (`mom_v1/v2`, `mom_roa_6535`, both cohorts) round-tripped through a -4% drawdown and partial recovery, ending the week only modestly negative; the two single-name LLM sleeves diverged hardest — cascade (WDC) +5.86% vs. control (BE) **-9.70%**, the widest same-week gap seen in this experiment so far, driven mostly by BE's short-report overhang rather than WDC's own strength.

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. This week is the cleanest test yet of the diversification-vs-concentration pattern flagged repeatedly since 07-08, and it confirms the pattern cuts both ways.** Monday's chip-complex shock hit concentrated momentum sleeves far harder than diversified ones; today's CPI-driven chip rally reversed roughly half of that in a single session, again for the concentrated book specifically. This is consistent with a volatility-exposure explanation (concentrated momentum sleeves carry more single-factor/single-sector beta, so they overshoot on both the downside and the recovery) rather than a one-way "momentum sleeves have bad luck" story. It does not, on its own, argue for or against running concentrated momentum sleeves going forward — it argues that their higher realized volatility is symmetric, which is a more favorable (if still noisy) finding than an asymmetric-downside pattern would be.

**B. The sector-arm veto's first same-direction "miss" (XLV underperforming XLE today) is worth logging as a counterpoint, not treated as a verdict.** Every prior sector-arm data point since 07-07 favored the control's XLE holding; today the substitute (XLV) underperformed for a plausible, distinct reason (sector-wide biotech rotation, not an oil-thesis failure). A single day's reversal driven by an unrelated cause doesn't change the standing evaluation of the 07-07 XLE veto, but it's a reminder that the cascade's XLV pick carries its own uncorrelated risk that the original veto rationale didn't price in.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** CPI, bank earnings, Fed testimony, and today's individual stock catalysts (AAOI capacity expansion, FCEL analyst upgrade, WDC target raises, BE short-covering, biotech-sector rotation) are all within the scope of existing exposures already embedded in the current sleeve roster. The two open process items remain unchanged from prior reports: the cascade stop-enforcement gap (§3, first flagged 07-13) and the still-not-fully-reconciled ANAB/SPHR price discrepancies (§3) — both are operational/data-hygiene items for Evan, not research findings that argue for a new strategy.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**ASML earnings — the dominant catalyst of the morning, driving the whole semiconductor complex.** Reported Q2 net sales of €9.33B and net income of €2.92B, both above estimates, and **raised full-year 2026 guidance for the second time this year** to €43-45B sales ($49B) with 54-56% gross margin, citing "extremely strong" AI-driven orders as customers accelerate capacity expansion (CNBC, 2026-07-15, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/15/asml-2q-earnings-ai-chips-orders.html). ASML also announced plans to expand its own chipmaking-equipment production capacity by 30% over the next two years, and disclosed a "High-NA" lithography validation win with Intel. Stock +3% pre-market/early session; Intel and Lam Research each +3%; SMH +1.2% (FX Leaders/NAI 500/CNBC, 2026-07-15). This is a read-through catalyst for every semiconductor-heavy sleeve in the roster (mom_v1/v2, mom_roa_6535, and both 0701 cohorts, all top-heavy in chip/chip-equipment names).

**June PPI — a second consecutive cooler-than-expected inflation print.** Released 8:30am ET: final demand **-0.3% MoM** (vs. 0.0% consensus), core (ex food, energy, trade services) **+0.1% MoM** (down sharply from +0.8% in May) (Bloomingbit/BLS, 2026-07-15, https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_07152026.htm). **Fed Chair Kevin Warsh testifies before the Senate Banking Committee today, 10:00am ET** — his second and final congressional appearance of the week (House Financial Services was yesterday, 07-14). This is the Fed's Semiannual Monetary Policy Report. Background context found: inflation had climbed to around 4.2% earlier in the year on an energy shock, and one source describes markets pricing roughly **69% odds of no rate cuts at all in 2026** — Warsh reportedly became the first Fed chair since the dot plot's 2012 debut to withhold his own personal rate projection, shifting the signaling burden onto testimony itself (CryptoTimes/CryptoBriefing, 2026-07-09/07-14, https://www.cryptotimes.io/2026/07/09/fed-chair-kevin-warsh-testifies-before-senate-july-15-what-it-means-for-crypto/). ### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. AEHR's guidance beat is a genuinely different kind of catalyst than most of what this week has produced, and it's worth distinguishing from noise.** Most of this week's held-name moves (AAOI, FCEL, BE, WULF, the biotech-sector rotation) have been sentiment/analyst-driven or macro-pass-through. AEHR's FY27 guidance of $130-150M against an $85M consensus is a **62-76% guidance beat**, not a modest raise — a genuine re-rating catalyst with a specific fundamental driver (semiconductor test/burn-in capacity tied to AI-chip production ramps). If it holds through 07-15's close, it would be the single largest fundamentally-driven (not macro-driven) daily gain any held name has produced in the period this report series has covered. Worth tracking whether the momentum-factor sleeves' exposure to genuine small-cap fundamental catalysts like this — versus large-cap macro-beta names — is where any structural edge in the momentum book actually lives, as opposed to the macro-whipsaw exposure that has dominated headlines the past week.

**B. WDC's Kioxia talks are a reminder that the cascade sleeve's largest position carries idiosyncratic M&A risk the original 07-07 BUY thesis didn't price in.** The 07-07 rationale for WDC (multi-year HDD supply contracts, AI/cloud demand, valuation discipline vs. BE) was a pure fundamentals-and-momentum case. A NAND-flash merger with Kioxia would change WDC's business mix, balance sheet, and possibly trigger deal-arbitrage-style volatility unrelated to the original thesis — not necessarily bad, but a distinct risk category (M&A execution/regulatory risk) that the invalidation-level framework (a price stop) may not be well-suited to capture. This is a design observation, not a call to act.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** ASML/chip-equipment strength, cooler PPI, Warsh's testimony, and the individual stock catalysts (AEHR, WDC, STX, BE) are all within the scope of exposures already embedded in the current roster (momentum-factor concentration in semiconductors/storage, macro-sensitive sector overlay, single-name LLM overlay experiment). The two open process items remain the cascade stop-enforcement gap (§5) and the unresolved 07-14 coverage lag (§1/§5) — both operational items for Evan, not research findings that argue for a new strategy.

### 1. Market summary — 2026-07-15

**Indices, close:** S&P 500 **7,572.40 (+0.38%)**, Nasdaq Composite **26,269.23 (+0.62%)**, Dow Jones **52,658.64 (+0.29%, +150.37pts)** (CNBC, 2026-07-15, https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/07/14/stock-market-today-live-updates.html; The Motley Fool, https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/07/15/stock-market-today-july-15-markets-rise-on-cooler-inflation-and-strong-earnings-start/). **Mega-cap tech vs. AI-hardware/memory — the day's central divergence.** Apple **+4% to a fresh all-time-high near $327**, its 15th intraday record of 2026, on a report the iPhone maker gained approval to launch generative-AI features in China; the stock has added over half a trillion dollars in market value this month, nearing a $5T valuation (Yahoo Finance/247wallst, 2026-07-15, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-july-15-dow-sp-nasdaq-waver-asml-091813320.html; https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/07/15/apple-is-up-20-in-2026-what-will-it-take-for-aapl-stock-to-hit-350/). Amazon and Alphabet each **+~3%**, Microsoft **+~3%** (CNBC, 2026-07-15). In sharp contrast, AI-hardware and memory/storage names sold off hard: **Dell -14%** intraday, **HPE -8%**, **Super Micro -5%** — the proximate trigger was a report that Meta Platforms is developing a plan to lease surplus AI training/inference capacity to enterprise customers, reviving concern that hyperscale cloud providers over-built AI infrastructure and could slow future server orders; compounding factors included Evercore ISI flagging memory-pricing margin pressure (Dell gross margin compression toward 18%) and a GF Securities downgrade of Dell to Hold on valuation after a ~200% YTD run to a ~34x forward P/E (Cryptonomist/AOL/FXLeaders/247wallst/MoneyCheck, 2026-07-15, https://en.cryptonomist.ch/2026/07/15/dell-technologies-inc-stock-plunges-14-in-ai-hardware-selloff/; https://www.aol.com/articles/dell-falls-14-hpe-super-164251000.html; https://www.fxleaders.com/news/2026/07/15/dell-stock-dips-below-400-as-cheaper-competition-hits-hardware-sector/; https://moneycheck.com/dell-dell-stock-plunges-13-amid-ai-overcapacity-concerns-and-downgrade). Micron fell (sources range -3% to -8% across outlets, https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/micron-shares-slide-semiconductor-selloff-122643510.html) and SanDisk/Marvell also declined (-6% to -8%, -6.62% respectively) as the memory-and-AI-hardware complex gave back more of its parabolic 2026 gains after Monday's SK Hynix-triggered rout paused Tuesday, per 24/7 Wall St. (2026-07-15, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/07/15/sk-hynix-drops-5-sandisk-slides-6-western-digital-slips-4-as-traders-take-profits-in-memory-stocks/) and TradingKey market-movers pages (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262032735-market-movers-mrvl-20260715).

**Fed:** Chair Kevin Warsh testified before the **Senate Banking Committee** — his second and final congressional appearance this week, following Tuesday's House Financial Services Committee session, and his inaugural semiannual Monetary Policy Report testimony overall as the 17th Fed Chair (sworn in 2026-05-22). He reaffirmed the Fed's inflation-fighting commitment and gave no new forward guidance on the rate path (CNBC, 2026-07-15, https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/15/watch-fed-chairman-kevin-warsh-testify-live-before-senate-banking-committee.html). Elizabeth Warren pressed him on whether he had questioned a colleague about a reported blackout-period meeting with bankers that may have violated Fed rules, producing a heated but market-irrelevant ethics exchange (CNN, 2026-07-15, https://us.cnn.com/2026/07/15/economy/fed-chairman-kevin-warsh-senate-testimony).

### 3. Key position analysis

**WDC — the Kioxia merger talks are the single biggest story of the day for this portfolio.** WDC fell **-8.78%** in our own data ($563.32→$513.84); external sources confirm a ~9% move to roughly $510-514 (TradingKey/GuruFocus, 2026-07-15, https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262032737-market-movers-wdc-20260715; https://www.gurufocus.com/news/8960543/western-digital-wdc-reopens-merger-talks-with-kioxia). The trigger: WDC "initiated renewed discussions regarding a merger with Kioxia, aiming to consolidate their NAND flash production" — a real structural M&A catalyst, distinct from the momentum/analyst-target story that had been driving the stock upward. This matters far beyond WDC's own price because `llm_cascade_top1_paper` holds **189.26 shares of WDC as its sole position** — the sleeve went from the single best performer in the entire 27-sleeve roster yesterday (+6.71%) to -2.65% today, a swing of roughly 9.4 percentage points in one session. The current invalidation level on this position is **$480** (logged 2026-07-07, `llm_overlay_log`), and today's self-computed close of $513.84 sits above it — not breached, but the closest any tracked position has come to its stop in this report series (~6.5% cushion). The broader semiconductor sector was also weak: Micron -7.34%, SanDisk -7.91% same-day (TradingKey, 2026-07-15). WDC's Q4/FY26 earnings remain scheduled for **2026-08-05**.

**Dell and the AI-hardware complex — a sector-wide "overbuild" scare, not company-specific to any held name individually, but MRVL/GLW/CIEN ride the same wave.** DELL -9.80% in our data (external: as much as -14% intraday before settling), MRVL -7.27%, GLW -7.05% (Corning's own guidance cut on carrier-network/display demand — a distinct, company-specific driver), CIEN -6.37% (no distinct news found; likely swept into the same networking/AI-infrastructure-adjacent selloff). None of these four are individually large positions in any sleeve (all sub-5% weights, per `paper_positions.qty`), but their simultaneous decline explains a meaningful share of the broad -2.2% to -2.7% single-day decline across every momentum-family sleeve (`mom_v1/v2`, `mom_roa_6535`, both 05-01 and 07-06 cohorts) despite the S&P 500 itself closing up +0.38%.

**CELC — an FDA approval that the market read as a disappointment.** -17.60% ($111.05→$91.51), the day's largest decliner among held names. The FDA approved gedatolisib (brand name Revtorpyk) for PIK3CA-wildtype advanced breast cancer — Celcuity's first-ever marketed product — but shares fell because the commercial launch is delayed to **late Q3 2026** (company cited the need to secure adequate drug supply) and because of lingering treatment-tolerability concerns (Yahoo Finance/Daily Political, 2026-07-15, https://finance.yahoo.com/healthcare/articles/celcuity-shares-fall-delayed-breast-124344986.html; https://www.dailypolitical.com/2026/07/15/celcuity-nasdaqcelc-shares-gap-down-heres-why.html). ### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. The cascade sleeve's single-name concentration risk, flagged as hypothetical yesterday, is now an empirical data point — and it argues for treating the LLM-cascade design's risk profile as a feature to study, not dismiss.** A single stock swinging a sleeve's since-inception standing from #1 to #20 (of 27) in one session is a direct, measurable illustration of why the underlying experiment design (single-name concentration, tiny n) carries far more idiosyncratic risk than the diversified systematic sleeves it's compared against. This doesn't invalidate the cascade concept — it's exactly the kind of result the 12mo/30-picks kill-switch window exists to average out — but it's a concrete example worth citing when that review happens, since M&A/deal risk is a distinct category from the momentum/earnings risk the underlying strategy was designed to capture.

**B. Today's AI-hardware "overbuild" scare (Dell/HPE/SMCI) is a new, distinct narrative from the memory-supply-glut story that dominated the prior week, and it's worth distinguishing the two going forward.** The 07-13/07-14 memory selloff was about SK Hynix's HBM shipment guidance (a supply/execution question). Today's Dell-led move is about a demand-side worry — whether hyperscalers over-built AI infrastructure capacity, per the Meta capacity-leasing report. Both narratives pressure overlapping tickers (WDC, Micron, SanDisk all appear in each), but they're causally distinct, and conflating them would misread how correlated these positions' risk actually is going forward.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** PPI, Apple's China-AI-approval rally, Fed testimony, and the day's individual stock catalysts (CELC's launch-delay disappointment, AAOI's giveback, WDC's Kioxia news, the Dell-led AI-hardware selloff) are all within the scope of exposures already embedded in the current 27-sleeve roster (momentum-factor concentration in semiconductors/storage/AI-hardware, macro-sensitive sector overlay, single-name LLM overlay experiment). The standing open process items are unchanged: the cascade stop-enforcement gap not going live until tomorrow (§3/§4, first flagged 07-13, fix deployed 07-15 per record BZ) and the 07-15 coverage-pending lag (§2) — both operational items for Evan, not research findings that argue for a new strategy.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**Retail sales + jobless claims — a stronger-than-expected consumer/labor print, read as hawkish for the Fed.** June retail sales rose **+0.2% MoM** (vs. +0.3% consensus) to $768.6B, held back by a -5.3% drop in gasoline-station receipts; ex-gas sales were **+0.7%**, nonstore/e-commerce **+1.9%** (the largest gain among major categories), autos **+1.9%** — a headline miss masking real underlying strength (Census Bureau/CNN, 2026-07-16, https://www.cnn.com/2026/07/16/economy/us-retail-sales-june). Separately, initial jobless claims fell **8,000 to 208,000** (vs. 217,000 consensus) for the week ended 07-11 (Bloomberg, 2026-07-16, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-16/us-jobless-claims-decline-to-208-000-below-economist-forecasts). Combined, markets read this as evidence the labor market and consumer remain resilient — reinforcing bets toward a hawkish Fed (no 2026 cuts, per the ~69%-odds figure cited in yesterday's report around Warsh's Senate testimony) rather than near-term easing.

**TSMC's Q2 beat + capex raise — a "good news is bad news" reaction that set today's semiconductor tone.** TSMC posted record Q2 revenue and raised 2026 capex guidance to $60-64B, but the market read the bigger number as a signal of capex-sustainability risk (are hyperscalers/foundries overbuilding?) rather than confirmed demand strength — TSM itself fell -3.9% despite the beat (24/7 Wall St., 2026-07-16). This is the direct read-through driver of today's broad semiconductor selloff (§2) and compounds the ChangXin-IPO-driven memory-specific selloff hitting WDC hardest.

**Oil/Iran escalation risk — see §2.** The reported consideration of a Kharg Island operation, if it materializes, would be a materially larger step than the naval-blockade/coastal-strikes actions taken so far this week.

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. If tonight's stop fires on WDC, it will be the first real-world test of both the LLM-overlay experiment's risk-control mechanism AND the newly-deployed stop-enforcement fix, on the same day — worth flagging as a coincidence of timing, not by design.** The fix (record BZ/CA) was deployed 07-15 specifically because the original mechanism had been silently dormant since inception; its first scheduled live evaluation happens to land on the same day WDC first breaches its logged level. Whatever happens tonight is a genuine out-of-sample data point on whether the mechanism works as intended — not something this report can pre-judge.

**B. The memory/semiconductor complex has now produced three distinct shocks to the same overlapping tickers inside one week** (SK Hynix guidance 07-13, Kioxia-merger-talk 07-15, ChangXin IPO 07-16) — each with a different underlying cause (execution/supply, M&A/business-mix, competitive-oversupply) but the same handful of names absorbing all three. This reinforces the point raised in yesterday's report: single-name concentration in the LLM-cascade design carries meaningfully more compounding idiosyncratic risk than the diversified systematic sleeves it's benchmarked against, and today is the clearest illustration yet.

**C. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** Retail sales, jobless claims, TSMC's capex guidance, and the individual stock catalysts (WDC, BE, AEHR, AAOI, oil/Iran) are all within the scope of exposures already embedded in the current 27-sleeve roster. The standing open process items are: (1) whether tonight's stop-enforcement fix fires as designed on WDC (§4, the report's central open question), and (2) the still-unresolved coverage-lag pattern that has left 07-15/07-16 without confirmed closing NAVs at report time — both operational items for Evan to check after tonight's `daily.bat` run, not research findings that argue for a new strategy.

### 0. Data status and methodology note

This report is compiled 2026-07-16 ~18:15 CDT (~19:15 ET), roughly 2h15m after the 4:00pm ET close — genuinely post-market this time (the same-day AM report published earlier today was mid-session, ~1pm CDT). `daily.bat` ran on schedule at 17:19–17:33 CDT (`var/last_daily_run.log`): overlay/sector-overlay stop checks ran `--settled` (priced as-of 2026-07-15, the last settled day), `mtm_catchup` found 2026-07-16 coverage at 4,414 tickers (below the 5,000-auto-mark floor) and left it **PENDING**, and `verify_run` passed 27/27 sleeves through 07-15 (`var/verify_report.log`). By the time this report queried `price_cache` directly (~18:05 CDT), coverage for 2026-07-16 had grown to **8,826 rows** (vs 9,723 for 07-15) — apparently past the 5,000 floor, but the day was already marked PENDING by the earlier run and will only get an official `paper_nav` row once a subsequent `mtm_catchup` pass (tomorrow's `daily.bat`, per the self-healing design in HANDOFF.md) re-evaluates it. **This report is READ-ONLY and does not run any MTM, rebalance, or catch-up script** — per its own rules — so all 07-16 figures below are computed directly from `price_cache` closes joined against each sleeve's actual open positions and cash (both read from `var/trades.db`), explicitly labeled "unofficial/estimate," never treated as the settled mark. One held ticker, EACO, has no 07-16 close (flagged by `check_anomalies` at 17:28 CDT: "NOCLOSE EACO no close on 2026-07-16 [HELD residual_roa_6535_paper]") and is excluded from that one sleeve's estimate (immaterial — EACO's cost basis is a small fraction of the 50-name book).

- **Residual-signal sleeves (weight ladder + residual_roa_6535) far more resilient**: −0.71% to −1.62% across all 11 residual-family sleeves, roughly a quarter to a third of the raw-momentum drawdown over the same week.
- **Flat-to-positive**: llm_overlay_mom_roa_top1 (cash) +0.00%, sector_top4_full +0.09%, sector_top4 +0.22%, both SPY benchmarks +0.41%.
- This is the clearest week-over-week illustration yet of the residual-momentum thesis (idiosyncratic/residual signal should carry less single-factor/single-name concentration risk than raw price momentum) — consistent with, not a new finding beyond, the original residual_roa_6535 backtest case for lower drawdown (HANDOFF.md backtest table: residual_roa_6535 held-out maxDD −20.1% vs. mom_v2's −34.8%).

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. The residual-momentum family's live drawdown resilience this week (§5) is a genuine, if still-short, forward data point supporting its designed edge** — not a new finding, but the sharpest real-time confirmation since the 06-09 deployment decision (record: residual_roa_6535 beats mom_roa_6535 on return+Sharpe+DD in both backtest windows). A week of a real semiconductor-driven selloff hitting raw-momentum sleeves 4-7x harder than the residual-signal sleeves is exactly the kind of out-of-sample stress period the original backtest thesis predicted.

**B. The stock-level LLM overlay experiment produced its most striking single data point yet today.** Treatment (cash, VETO'd BE twice) vs. control (BE, down an estimated ~23% from its 07-07 peak) is now a ~21-22 percentage-point NAV gap on one ticker. This is still n=1 decision and n=8 total logged picks — nowhere near statistically meaningful, and the kill-switch design (30 picks/12 months) exists precisely because early divergences like this can reverse. But it is the single clearest illustration since inception of what the experiment is designed to test.

**C. The llm_cascade_top1_paper design gap (§3/§4) is worth flagging as a process item, not a sleeve-concept idea.** An "always-invested, walk-past-the-veto" cascade concept that holds a name through a stop-level breach with no mechanical exit is a coherent design choice (it's explicitly not meant to have the overlay's veto-and-cash behavior), but it means WDC's current position has no risk control beyond the next LLM re-evaluation cycle (which, per the log history, has run roughly monthly at rebalance, not on stop breaches). Worth Evan confirming this is intended before the position potentially deepens further.

**D. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** TSMC's capex-guidance reaction, the CXMT IPO date, the BE short-seller allegations, and the GOOGL Gemini-3.5-delay report are all within the scope of exposures already embedded in the current 27-sleeve roster (momentum universes hold WDC/MU/GOOGL-class names broadly; the stock-arm experiment already holds BE directly). The standing open items are: (1) whether Evan wants a stop mechanism added to the cascade design given today's WDC breach (§4/C), (2) the still-pending 07-16 official NAV mark (§0) — expected to resolve on a future `mtm_catchup` pass per the self-healing pipeline design, and (3) the EACO stale-price watch item (§0), which mirrors the pattern that produced the BKGM ghost-price finding in the 2026-06-01 audit and may be worth a manual check the next time Evan is in the DB.

- **Residual-ladder sleeves far more resilient**: the low-residual/high-ROA-weight end of the ladder (`residual_w0595`, `residual_w1090`, `residual_w1585`) held losses to −0.1% to −0.6% for the entire week — a small fraction of the raw-momentum drawdown over the same window; the high-residual end (`residual_w7030_2wk`, `residual_w8020_2wk`) fared worse, in the −3% to −4.4% range, but still well ahead of any raw-momentum sleeve.
- **Best performers of the week**: `llm_overlay_mom_roa_top1` (cash) +0.00% — flat beat every invested sleeve this week; both SPY benchmarks −0.56%; `sector_top4` −0.49%.
- This is the second straight week the residual-momentum thesis (idiosyncratic signal should carry less single-factor/single-name concentration risk than raw price momentum) has shown up clearly in live forward data — not a new finding, but a second independent confirmation after 07-16's single-day version of the same pattern (HANDOFF.md backtest table: residual_roa_6535 held-out maxDD −20.1% vs. mom_v2's −34.8%).

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge or new sleeve concepts?

**A. The residual-momentum family's resilience is now a two-session-plus-one-week pattern, not a single data point.** Both yesterday's crash and this week's cumulative drawdown show the same 4-7x gap between raw-momentum and residual-signal sleeves. This remains consistent with, not a new finding beyond, the original 06-09 deployment thesis — but the sample is accumulating in the direction the backtest predicted.

**B. Today's reversal is the first genuinely two-sided data point for the LLM stock overlay experiment.** Every prior divergence since the 07-07 double-VETO favored the cash treatment (avoiding BE's slide). Today, for the first time, the treatment's structural inability to participate in a bounce (BE +3.98%, WDC +2.23%) cost it real relative ground versus control and cascade. This doesn't change the cumulative picture (treatment is still far ahead since 07-07), but it's a useful, honest data point: a veto-to-cash design trades upside capture for downside avoidance, and today is when that trade was visibly costly rather than free. Still n=8 decisions, nowhere near the 30-pick kill-switch threshold.

**C. The CELC correction (§3) is a process note worth Evan's attention.** The 07-16 report's research pass searched specifically for 07-16-dated news and correctly reported nothing found — but the actual FDA approval, dated 07-14, apparently wasn't surfaced by that day's search terms (which were framed around the "pending PDUFA date," not "FDA approval announcement"). No held-sleeve action resulted from the gap (CELC's price was accurately captured both days regardless of the narrative attached to it), but it's a reminder that "no news found for today" doesn't guarantee "no relevant news exists a day or two prior" — worth keeping in mind for future high-stakes binary-catalyst names in the momentum universe.

**D. The semiconductor bear market (SOX >20% off its late-June high) is now the dominant sector-concentration risk sitting inside this portfolio, not a new sleeve concept.** At least 15 held tickers (AMAT, ALAB, MU, STX, VICR, MRAM, ICHR, UCTT, VSH, TTMI, CIEN, GLW, NVTS, MXL, WATT among them) are semiconductor/memory/AI-infrastructure-adjacent names spread across 40-65 sleeves each, per §3. None of the momentum or residual-momentum strategies apply an explicit sector cap — sector exposure is an emergent property of the ranking, not a designed constraint. This is not a proposal to add a sector-cap sleeve (that would cut against the "buy the strongest factor signal, unconstrained" design the backtests validated), but it is worth Evan explicitly knowing that a chip-sector regime shift (like this week's) will show up as correlated, not diversified, risk across most of the 76-sleeve roster simultaneously — which is exactly what happened 07-16 and, in reverse, today.

**E. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** The Moonshot Kimi K3 story, the Iran/Hormuz oil spike, the NFLX guidance miss, and the GOOGL Gemini-delay continuation are all within the scope of exposures already embedded in the current 76-sleeve roster. Standing open items carried forward: (1) the still-pending 07-17 official NAV mark (§0) — expected to resolve via tomorrow's `mtm_catchup`; (2) whether Evan wants a stop mechanism added to the cascade design (§3, unchanged from 07-16, now less urgent after today's WDC bounce but not resolved); (3) the FMBM/UYSC sparse-coverage watch items (§0) — same chronic-gap pattern as EACO, immaterial individually but worth a manual DB check if the pattern spreads to more names.

**A. No new sleeve concept is proposed from today's data.** Today's developments (Iran/oil spike-and-partial-reversal, a chip-sector bounce that faded into the close, GOOGL's pre-earnings AI-chip headline, AAPL's profit-taking) are all exposures already embedded in the existing 76-sleeve roster.
