### 6. Strategic read — what today's data says about structural edge

**6a. The re-mark validation is the most useful methodological result this book has produced in two weeks, and it should be written down as a rule rather than an anecdote.** §0b closed a prediction exactly: the error was **−$179.65**, it lived **entirely** in the six sleeves the prior entry named, and it decomposed **position-by-position** into the two tickers the prior entry named. Seventy of 76 sleeves matched to the cent.

**What that licenses and what it does not.** It licenses continuing to publish indicative re-marks on pending-coverage evenings **provided the disclosure names every missing ticker, sizes its exposure per sleeve, and states which sleeves are affected** — that disclosure is what made this auditable after the fact. **It does not license treating the small error as evidence of a small error bound.** VSAT moved −1.96% overnight; VPG, whose carry-forward was the more dangerous of the two, had moved **−27% in a single session four days earlier**. The realised error was small because the two names happened to be quiet, not because two stale marks out of 192 are structurally safe. **The correct rule to carry forward: publish, but state the worst-case error alongside the point estimate — the stale exposure times a plausible adverse move, per sleeve, not per book.** Friday's entry had the exposure table; it did not have the bound. That is a one-line addition and it would have made Friday's caveat quantitative.

**6b. The equipment/product split inside the semiconductor cluster is now on its second session and is the most interesting live structural question in the book.** Friday: AMAT +2.21%, KLAC +2.53%, LRCX +1.82% against STX −4.71%, WDC −3.81%, MU −0.44%. This morning: AMAT **+2.76%**, LRCX **+1.88%** against MU **−1.89%**, STX **−1.69%**, WDC **−0.94%**. **Two sessions is not a regime and this is not being treated as one.** But the mechanism is legible and dated: **Intel raised 2026 capex to $20B from $18B** (bullish equipment) while **Citi called the memory-price peak for Q2 next year** and **SK Hynix announced $38B of new capacity** (bearish product pricing, bullish equipment orders again). **Capacity expansion is unambiguously good for the equipment vendors and ambiguous-to-bad for the memory vendors selling into the capacity it creates.** If that is what the tape is pricing, it is a genuine within-sector factor and not noise — and this book holds **$414,000 of equipment and $642,600 of memory/storage** without distinguishing between them anywhere in its construction.

**This does not support a new sleeve and no recommendation is made.** What it supports is the same infrastructure gap §6a of Friday's entry identified from a different direction: **per-sleeve return attribution splitting factor exposure from idiosyncratic name selection.** Friday's version of the question was "did the momentum-weight gradient reverse, or did the residual sleeves draw five bad earnings tickets?" This morning's version is "is the book long a semiconductor factor, or is it long six names that happen to be correlated until they aren't?" **Two independent questions in three sessions now route through the same unbuilt tool. That is the strongest argument yet for building it, and it is an observation for the roadmap, not a request.**

**6c. INSW is the cleanest test yet of the "beat quality" hypothesis, and it will be readable by tonight.** The hypothesis under test (recorded 2026-08-07) is that the market pays for beats whose upside is *retained* — margin, cash, debt paydown — and sells beats whose upside is *spent* or whose forward guide steps down. **INSW is a maximal retained beat**: record net income, record EBITDA, record free cash flow, and a **record dividend that hands the upside straight to shareholders**. It also carries the largest forward-uncertainty overhang in the book, because the entire earnings power is a function of the **Strait of Hormuz staying shut** — a variable resolved by negotiation, not by the company.

**Pre-market says +1.72% on a beat of that size, which is a muted response.** If INSW closes near that, the hypothesis needs a third category beyond retained/spent: **beats whose driver is exogenous and reversible**, which the market discounts regardless of quality. **That is a falsifiable statement about tonight's close and it is written before the open.** Ten of twelve confirmations with two clean counterexamples (EZPW retained-and-sold, EVER spent-and-bought) was the standing tally; INSW is the thirteenth case and the first where the *source* of the beat, rather than its disposition, is the variable.

**6d. No new sleeve concept is supported by this morning's data. No recommendation.** The Jefferies Apple downgrade, the Citi Micron target cut, the Berkshire/Alphabet disclosure and the INSW print are all single-name events. **The one macro fact with book-wide reach — Hormuz talks stalling, Brent +1.4% — is a repricing of an existing 4.24% energy weight and an existing sector-overlay XLE position, not a signal for anything new.** The July CPI print on **2026-08-12** is the first datapoint this week capable of moving the systematic sleeves' construction, and it will not: **the sleeves rebalance monthly and next trade 2026-09-01.** Everything between now and then is mark-to-market on positions already set.

|---|---:|---:|---:|
| NLST | 3.92 | 3.92 | **4.03** |
| NWBO | 0.18 | 0.18 | **0.186** |
| ^VIX | 14.90 | 15.40 | **15.46** |

Each pre-open value equalled the prior close (or, for ^VIX, a stale intraday quote), and each was replaced. **No sleeve holds any of the three.** The artifact is therefore harmless in this instance — but the mechanism is unchanged: **for part of a trading day the cache contains a row dated in the future relative to the last completed session.** Any code that reads "the latest `key_date`" without checking it against the last settled session can still pick it up. Left as an open item, downgraded from "new class of artifact" to "confirmed self-healing, still latent."

Continuity and reconciliation clean across all 76 sleeves.** `verify_run` at 17:17:37 reported `RESULT: PASS (76/76 sleeves OK)`, with `recon(delta $±0.00)` and `preinc(0)` on every sleeve, and `last_rebalance(2026-08-03/nostatus) settled_month(2026-08)` on the cadence check. **No position changes today** — `paper_positions` shows the most recent entries and exits both dated **2026-08-03** (727 entries, 751 exits) and nothing since. H.15 is the official series and its 4.70%/4.25% is what this entry uses.

**The whole curve steepened upward on a day equities were flat** — the 2s rose more than the 10s, which is a policy-expectations move, not a growth move. This morning's entry recorded the 10-year at 4.668% and the 2-year at 4.22% intraday; both finished higher.

**2b. Oil rallied on a hardening Hormuz stalemate — and the settle is in source conflict.** Last week oil sold off more than 7% after Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told CNBC a deal to reopen the Strait "with freedom of movement for ships" could come soon. No agreement materialized, and over the weekend positions hardened: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman said the U.S. must lift its naval blockade first — ["As long as the U.S. naval blockade continues, the necessary conditions for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz do not exist"](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/10/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-iran.html) — while Tehran claimed over the weekend that the strait was closed.

| [Al Jazeera, 2026-08-10](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/10/oil-prices-stocks-surge-as-hormuz-closure-drags-on) | **+3.3% to $84.64** | **+3.1% to $80.63** |

Both agree on direction and on a mid-single-digit magnitude; the levels differ by ~$3. Recorded as unresolved. Tanker transits hit their post-crisis high late last week and then "traffic slowed to a dribble" after Tehran's weekend closure claim. **The spot rate environment behind INSW's record quarter is not deteriorating — which makes today's price reaction harder to attribute to the tanker cycle and easier to attribute to positioning.** Note: the specific Baltic level above is week-on-week and is not dated to 08-10 itself; the 08-07 Capesize conflict (5,128 vs 4,480) recorded in prior entries remains unresolved.

**The price path:** Friday close **$92.41** → this morning's pre-market **$94.00 (+1.72%)** → open **$93.25** → high **$94.50** → low **$89.67** → **close $90.40, −2.18%**. **A −$4.83 round trip from high to close on the day of a record print.** Book impact **−$2,267.73** across **41 sleeves** on **$101,991.40** of exposure.

**Why this matters more than the dollar amount.** This morning's entry named INSW "the largest scheduled binary in the book" and treated the earnings outcome as the thing to resolve. It resolved **unambiguously to the upside on every reported line** — and the position lost money. One analyst framing offered for the muted reaction is that investors ["have already rewarded the company for the strong tanker cycle this year"](https://simplywall.st/stocks/us/energy/nyse-insw/international-seaways/news/will-analyst-upgrades-and-tanker-demand-shifts-change-intern) and want clarity on rate durability. **And §2b shows the rate environment is still spiking, not fading.** So the cleanest available reading is positioning, not fundamentals.

**The transferable lesson for this project is narrow and worth stating precisely: the overlay experiments log a conviction score and an invalidation level, both of which are implicitly fundamental judgments, and are then graded on price. Today is a dated instance where a correct fundamental call would have produced a losing position.** That is not an argument against the overlay design; it is a measured estimate of the noise floor any such overlay has to clear.

| `mom_roa_top1_paper` | control | 87,434.68 | **85,785.32** | −1.89% | **−14.21%** | MU |
| `llm_cascade_top1_paper` | cascade | 97,586.26 | **96,174.51** | −1.45% | **−3.83%** | STX |

**Treatment leads control by 14.21pp and the cascade by 3.83pp.** The treatment has been in full cash since the 2026-08-03 decision, when all four candidates were vetoed:

| Date | Ticker | Score | Verdict | Invalidation |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 2026-08-03 | MU | 3 | **VETO** | 800.00 |
| 2026-08-03 | WDC | 4 | **VETO** | 500.00 |
| 2026-08-03 | VICR | 2 | **VETO** | 195.00 |
| 2026-08-03 | BE | 3 | **VETO** | 200.00 |
| 2026-08-03 | STX | 6 | **BUY** (cascade) | 730.00 |

**The full scorecard on the current cycle, every logged name, from the 2026-08-03 decision-day close to today's close:**

| Name | Verdict | Score | 08-03 close | **08-10 close** | **Since decision** | Call |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| WDC | **VETO** | 4 | 527.22 | **438.34** | **−16.86%** | **RIGHT — large** |
| BE | **VETO** | 3 | 218.32 | **210.63** | **−3.52%** | right |
| VICR | **VETO** | 2 | 213.54 | **208.81** | **−2.21%** | right |
| MU | **VETO** | 3 | 829.50 | **861.00** | **+3.80%** | **wrong** |
| STX | **BUY** (cascade) | 6 | 831.06 | **800.99** | **−3.62%** | **wrong** |

**Three of four vetoes are right, and the largest one is right by a wide margin.** The WDC veto is the strongest single piece of evidence the overlay has produced to date, because the stated rationale named the mechanism in advance: *"Q4 earnings Aug5 = 2-day binary catalyst on a name below 50DMA (562 vs 527) amid memory/storage valuation correction; risk-veto despite Citi/Wells PTs 800/730."* **WDC reported on 08-05 and fell 16.86% over the following three sessions.** The veto was a dated, specific, falsifiable call about an identified event, and the event went the way it said.

**An equal-weight basket of the four vetoed names would be −4.70% since the decision. The treatment held cash and is 0.00%.** On that basis the veto set added ~4.70pp this cycle.

**Against the pre-registered comparator, though, the treatment is behind this cycle.** The control does not hold the veto basket — it holds only the #1-ranked name, **MU, which is +3.80% since it was vetoed and has never come within $61 of its own $800 invalidation.** So the cycle reads: **the veto process was right about the population and wrong about the specific name that determines the control's return.** The MU rationale ("post-earnings momentum unwind, −28% in 30d, below 5/20/50 EMAs, RSI40") described the tape accurately on 08-03 and the stock rose anyway.

**The cascade's BUY is also wrong so far** — STX at −3.62% since the decision underperformed the cash the treatment held, though its $730 invalidation was never threatened.

**Both readings are recorded and neither is adopted as the verdict.** The kill-switch criteria (12 months / 30 picks; drop if scores don't predict returns or the treatment doesn't beat control) are unaffected at **n = 16 logged stock decisions**. One observation worth logging for the eventual score-vs-return regression: **the two lowest scores in this cycle (VICR 2, BE 3) both fell, the score-6 BUY fell, and the other score-3 veto rose** — no rank ordering yet at this n.

**One structural note that is not a scoring question: a treatment that vetoes everything holds cash and therefore cannot lose, which mechanically flatters it in a drawdown and starves it in a rally.** Since 07-06 the SPY benchmark twin is **+2.90%** and the treatment is **+0.00%** — so against a passive alternative the all-cash stance has cost 2.90pp, even as it beat its designated control by 14.21pp. **The control is the pre-registered comparator and stays the scorekeeper; the SPY line is recorded as context, not a re-definition of the experiment.**

**4d. XLU — the invalidation level was set ABOVE the purchase price. New finding.**

The 2026-08-03 cascade log records XLU as **HOLD, score 6, invalidation $44.50**, rationale: "Above 50DMA (44.96) and 200DMA (44.78), RSI56 healthy; rate-proxy headwind offset by structural AI-datacenter power demand + defensive bid in hawkish regime."

**The actual tape since that decision:**

| Date | XLU close | vs $44.50 stop |
|---|---:|---|
| 2026-07-31 | 44.35 | below |
| **2026-08-03 (decision day)** | **44.36** | **BELOW** |
| 2026-08-04 | 44.11 | below |
| 2026-08-05 | 43.66 | below |
| 2026-08-06 | 43.38 | below |
| 2026-08-07 | 43.61 | below |
| **2026-08-10** | **43.13** | **below — 6th consecutive marked close** |

**`llm_cascade_sector4_paper` bought XLU at $44.38 on 2026-08-03 — $0.12 below the invalidation level assigned to it in the same decision.** The position was in violation of its own stop from the moment it was opened, and has closed below it on every one of the six marked sessions since. XLU is now **−2.82% vs entry** and closed at its lowest level in the window.

**This reclassifies the item.** Prior entries recorded it as "stop breached, no enforcement path in code" — an execution gap. It is also a **decision-generation defect**: the invalidation level and the entry price came from the same 08-03 process and were mutually inconsistent, and nothing checked them against each other. **Two separate fixes are implied — (i) a post-decision assertion that `invalidation_level < entry_price` for a HOLD/BUY, and (ii) an enforcement path that acts on a breach.** Neither exists. Recorded; not acted on (this task is read-only).

**Count correction:** prior entries described this as the "seventh" and "eighth" consecutive session by counting pre-market quotes alongside marked closes. **Against marked closes the correct count today is six** (08-03 through 08-10). The underlying fact — breached continuously since inception of the position — is unchanged.

**Two things are visible and they point in different directions.**

**(i) On the day, losses are inverted-U in momentum weight in all three cadences.** The extremes lose least (w05: −0.47/−0.43/−0.46) and the middle-to-upper-middle loses most (w50–w70: −1.07 to −1.17), with w95 recovering to −0.66/−0.69/−0.77. **This is the second consecutive observation of non-monotonic short-horizon behavior** — last week's entry recorded a U-shaped week where the two extremes won and the 30–55% middle lost.

**(ii) At the three-month horizon the biweekly column is still cleanly monotonic** — w05 **+8.29%** descending to w80 **−4.98%** — while the **monthly column is not monotonic at all** (w60 +6.05% sits above w25 +3.50%, and w95 +4.73% sits above w50 +2.75%). **The since-inception gradient that prior entries described as "the single most durable structural fact this cohort has produced" is clean in the biweekly and weekly cadences and messy in the monthly one.**

**The honest read on the inverted-U:** it does not require a factor explanation. **The extreme sleeves hold different names** — w05/w10 hold 49 positions, w90/w95 hold 44 — because the ranking blend changes which names clear the top-50 screen. On a day dominated by semi-cap equipment and small-cap industrials, "which portfolio happened to hold less AMAT and ATEX" is sufficient to produce this shape. **Two observations of an inverted-U across a 5-session and a 1-session window is a pattern worth continuing to log, and nothing more. It is not evidence of a mid-weight penalty.**

---

### 6. Strategic assessment

**6a. Today did not support a structural edge for any systematic family, and the benchmark comparison is the finding.** Since the 07-06 cohort inception the SPY twin is **+2.90%** and the QQQ twin **−0.27%**; since 05-01 the older SPY is **+7.27%** and QQQ **+6.93%**. Against those, **no systematic family's mean beats the benchmark mean (+4.21%)** — the sector sleeves reach +3.15%, the 57-sleeve residual sweep +2.70%, and `mom_*` is at **−9.43%**. **Only two sleeves in the entire 76-sleeve book beat the older SPY line, and both are the same idea: `residual_w0595_2wk_paper` (+8.29%) and `residual_w0595_paper` (+7.53%) — the two lowest momentum weights in the sweep.** That is a 2-of-76 hit rate against a passive alternative over three months.

**The uncomfortable inference, stated plainly: the residual sweep's best performers are the ones that use the least of the signal the sweep exists to test.** w05 means 95% ROA / 5% residual momentum. If the top of the leaderboard is nearly-pure quality, then what this cohort has demonstrated over three months is that **quality beat residual momentum**, not that the residual-momentum construction has edge. That is still a result — it is just not the result the sweep was designed to find, and it argues that the next honest test is a pure-ROA sleeve (w00) as an explicit control, which the current grid does not contain. **Recorded as an observation. No recommendation, and nothing in one day's data justifies acting on it.**

**6b. The genuinely new observation today is the pre-event decline pattern, and it is testable.** Four held names fell into or on a scheduled event today with no explanatory headline in any of them:

| Name | Event | Day | Volume tell |
|---|---|---:|---|
| **ATEX** | reports 08-11 after close | **−6.52%** | **1.88× Friday**, closed near low, never traded above open |
| **COHR** | reports 08-12 after close | **−14.24%** | after +44.22% in five sessions |
| **CIEN** | optics complex, peer prints this week | **−5.99%** | — |
| **INSW** | **reported this morning, beat everything** | **−2.18%** | opened +0.9%, high $94.50, closed $90.40 |

**The pattern is consistent enough to state as a hypothesis with a falsifiable form: in this tape, names that have run hard sell off into their own scheduled catalysts, and beating on the catalyst does not reverse it.** The cited coverage for COHR is explicit that no catalyst exists ("no new company release, analyst action, or macro headline"), and the ATEX tape (gap down, no bounce, near-double volume) matches. INSW is the strongest version because the outcome is known and was good.

**Why this matters to sleeve design rather than to trading:** the momentum and residual-momentum sleeves systematically hold names that have run hard — that is what the factor selects for. **If pre-event de-risking is a persistent feature of this regime, the sleeves are structurally long a population that bleeds into earnings dates, and the effect is invisible in a monthly rebalance because it is absorbed between marks.** A testable version exists entirely within data already in `var/trades.db` and `price_cache`: **for every held position, measure the return over the N sessions preceding a known earnings date versus the sleeve's own average, across the full history.** No new data source, no new sleeve, no trading. **This is the first observation in several weeks that suggests a specific, cheap, falsifiable experiment rather than another parameter sweep.** Flagged for the roadmap; not acted on tonight.

**Honest caveat: four names in one session is an anecdote, and the base rate matters** — plenty of held names also fell today with no event at all (ELA −6.52%, ECPG −5.27%, BLBD −4.99%). The proposed measurement is exactly the thing that would separate a real pre-event effect from ordinary small-cap beta on a down day. **Until that measurement runs, this is a hypothesis with a test attached, not a finding.**

**6c. The coverage floor is measuring the wrong population — an infrastructure finding with a concrete fix.** Tonight the global check failed (**4,357 closes against a 5,000 floor**) and blocked the mark. Simultaneously, **every one of the 192 tickers the book actually holds had a 2026-08-10 close** — the re-mark carried zero stale prices, and the recomputation method was validated to 0/76 mismatches on official data.

**Those two facts together mean the system declined to mark a day on which it had complete information about its own portfolio.** The floor exists for a real reason (record Appendix AU: marking on a partially-published day corrupts NAV), but it is a proxy — universe-wide publication completeness standing in for held-name publication completeness. **The direct measurement is available and cheap: `SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT ticker) FROM paper_positions WHERE status='open'` intersected against `price_cache` for the target date.** Tonight it would have returned **192/192** and the book would have marked on time.

**This is not a recommendation to weaken the guard.** The correct shape is almost certainly **both** checks — mark when held-name coverage is 100% *and* the universe count is not catastrophically low (which would signal a feed-level failure rather than publication lag) — because the rebalance path selects from the full universe and genuinely needs universe-wide coverage. **The rebalance path still has no coverage guard at all** (next fire 2026-09-01), which is the more serious of the two gaps and remains open.

**6d. What today says about the `mom_*` drawdown.** The six `mom_*` sleeves average **−9.43%** since inception and fell **−1.60%** today, worst of any family — but they are also **+3.5% to +5.0% month-to-date**, better than the residual sweep's roughly flat MTD. **The pattern noted in last week's entry holds: the momentum sleeves' losing side recovers fast when it recovers, and gives it back fast.** Today's −1.60% against the residual sweep's −0.82% is the give-back leg. **Nothing today changes the standing conclusion that the momentum-vs-quality gradient is a real three-month result whose weekly volatility is too high for a deployment decision without a full-cycle test.**

**6e. No new sleeve concept is supported by today's data.** The one candidate today's tape might seem to argue for — energy/refining momentum, on XLE +4.66%, VLO +5.58%, FTI +6.48% — is driven by an unresolved geopolitical event (§2b) whose direction reversed twice in five sessions (down 7% last week on a Bessent deal comment, up 3–5% today when it did not materialize). **The project's own closed research line (record BU, 2026-07-14) established that catalyst-dependent trend overlays fail out-of-sample on clean data. Building a sleeve around a headline that flips weekly would repeat exactly that error.** No recommendation.

**Zero held tickers are missing an 08-10 close now** — the mismatch is not a gap, it is a *superseded mark*. The 57 non-ladder sleeves were marked at 07:47 against the healed 5,165-close set and reconcile to under half a cent; the 19 ladder sleeves were marked at 20:32 against the 4,357-close set, where any held name Yahoo had not yet published fell back to its prior close.

**Magnitude.** Summing the 19: **$282.88 overstated** against a full re-mark, on a $7,712,688.17 book — **0.0037%**, or **0.035% at the worst single sleeve** (`residual_w2080_wk_paper`). This is a *bookkeeping* error, not a P&L error of consequence. **The consequence is the guard, not the dollars.**

**0c. Why this is different from every prior coverage event, and why it will not heal itself.**

1. **It defeated a gate that worked.** `check_coverage` did its job at 17:17 and `mtm_catchup` correctly left 08-10 pending. Three hours later a *different scheduled task* wrote NAV rows for that same date from the same rejected data. The guard protects the MTM path; it does not protect the rebalance path.
2. **The exposure was mis-scoped in this journal.** Nine consecutive entries recorded the missing rebalance guard as a risk whose next test was the **2026-09-01** monthly fire. `TradingLadderRebalance` runs **8:30pm daily** (weekly + biweekly residual ladders), so the real exposure was **every night**, and it had been every night since the ladder was deployed.
3. **`mtm_catchup` cannot repair it.** Catch-up marks *missing* days. 08-10 is not missing for these 19 sleeves — it is present and wrong. Tonight's 17:15 run will mark 08-11 and leave 08-10 as-is, so **`verify_run` will keep returning FAIL until someone re-marks 08-10 for those 19 sleeves**. Per the project's standing rule, a NAV row that looks wrong gets **reported, not silently rewritten** — this entry is that report. **No data was modified.**

**Attribution of the individual deltas is not fully recoverable.** The pre-heal price snapshot was not retained, so which names fell back cannot be proven after the fact. A brute-force search over 1- and 2-ticker subsets found exactly one exact single-name match — **BTSG explains `residual_w5050_wk_paper`'s $34.03 to the cent** — and BTSG is held in 36 sleeves at $65,300, which makes it a plausible member of the fallback set. It is **suggestive, not proof**, and the two-tier structure of the deltas (−$22 to −$37 for the ten sleeves `w0595`–`w5050`, +$0.60/+$0.67 for the nine sleeves `w5545`–`w9505`) implies at least two distinct names split across the ladder's momentum-weight gradient. **Recorded as partially attributed.**

One thing the ladder log *does* rule out: **price revision**. All 73 tickers the ladder transacted price within **±0.05–0.09%** of the healed 08-10 close, in the direction of the trade (buys above, sells below) — that is the 5bps half-spread, not a changed close. The 08-10 closes for transacted names are unchanged.

**0d. Last night's re-mark scored.** Published indicative: **$7,713,385.26**. Official stored: **$7,712,688.17** → error **−$697.09 (−0.0090%)**. Against a fully recomputed book on healed prices (**$7,712,405.29**, i.e. official less the $282.88 above) the error is **−$979.97 (−0.0127%)**. Both are larger than 08-07's $179.65 miss, and unlike that one they are **not** attributable to stale marks — last night's entry verified that all 192 then-held tickers had an 08-10 close. The residual is the ladder's 20:32 rebalance, which moved positions *after* the indicative was computed: the book held **192** distinct tickers when the estimate was published and holds **201** now.

### 6. Strategic insights

**6a. The most valuable thing today produced is an infrastructure finding, not a market one — and it is a finding about how this journal reasons.** For nine consecutive entries the missing rebalance coverage guard was logged with the note "next fire 09-01." The item was correctly identified and **incorrectly scoped**: the reasoning attached the risk to the *monthly* rebalance because that is the rebalance the project thinks about, and never checked that a *different* scheduled task performs a rebalance-and-mark every single night. **The gap between "we know about this risk" and "we know when this risk is live" cost ten sessions of exposure, and it only surfaced because the risk finally fired.** The generalizable lesson: an outstanding-items list that records *what* without recording *which scheduled task, at what time* is not a risk register, it is a wish list.

**6b. The ladder's cadence dimension is now confounded, slightly, and this should be recorded before it is forgotten.** The three ladder cadences (monthly +4.29%, weekly +2.26%, biweekly +1.52%) are meant to isolate rebalance frequency at fixed momentum/quality weights. **The weekly arm is the one that rebalances nightly-eligible and therefore the only one that can transact on rejected coverage data.** Today's break is 0.0037% of the book and cannot meaningfully move the comparison — but the *mechanism* means the weekly arm systematically fills at whatever price snapshot exists at 20:32, which on lag days is a partially-stale set, while the monthly and biweekly arms mostly fill on complete data. **That is a small, real, one-directional execution-quality difference between the arms of a controlled experiment, and it was not part of the design.** It should be quantified before the cadence result is cited as evidence for anything.

**6c. On whether current sleeves have structural edge: the momentum-weight gradient survived another week and it is the only thing in this book that looks like a finding.** Within all three cadences, lower momentum weight → higher return, monotonic at the extremes (monthly `w0595` +7.50% vs `w9010` +2.30%; biweekly `w0595` +8.26% vs `w8020` −4.98%), and the pure-momentum `mom_*` family at −9.43% is the natural extension of that line. **Three months and 69 marked sessions is not enough to call it structural** — the 08-07 entry already recorded the losing side recovering 5–6% in a single week, which means the gradient's weekly volatility is high relative to its cumulative signal. **What today adds is one more session consistent with it, and nothing more.**

**6d. Today's tape actively argues against a new sleeve concept, and the argument is worth writing down.** The two candidate patterns visible today are (i) buy the semi-cap bloc after a down day, on the pre-market bounce, and (ii) trade AI-optics around earnings positioning. **Both fail on this journal's own evidence.** For (i): the pre-market direction in this exact bloc has inverted by the close three times in six sessions — 08-10 pre-market had AMAT +2.76%/LRCX +1.88% and they closed −3.16%/−1.59%. A sleeve built on the pre-market print in this complex would have been wrong twice in a week. For (ii): the record's closed research line (record BU, 2026-07-14) established that catalyst-dependent overlays fail out-of-sample on clean data, and the INSW event of 2026-08-10 is the cleanest possible demonstration — **the company beat on every line, declared its largest dividend ever, and the stock closed −2.18%.** **No recommendation. No new sleeve concept is supported by today's data.**

**6e. **Six marked sessions, seven actual closes, zero above the stop.** Today XLU was the second-best sector in the market and *still* closed 1.96% under its invalidation. The position is **−1.69% against its $44.38 entry** and worth **$24,268.38**.

**Two distinct defects compound here, and they should not be conflated:**
1. **No enforcement path in code.** The `sector_overlay_log` records an invalidation level; nothing reads it and exits.
2. **The level was set above the purchase price.** The 08-03 decision recorded `invalidation_level = 44.5` and the fill was **$44.38**. **The position was in violation of its own stop the instant it was opened.** This is a design defect in how the level is chosen, not an ops gap — and it means that even a working enforcement path would have exited on day one, which is almost certainly not the intent.

### 6. Strategic insights

**6a. Today is the first clean read on whether this book's factor tilt is an edge or a liability — and one day says "it is a beta bet on semiconductors."** The book was flat while SPY fell 0.32%. The decomposition is unambiguous: **semi-cap +$14,401 and memory/storage +$8,067 against mega-cap −$9,715**. The residual across the other ~195 names was roughly −$12,800. **The book did not outperform because of stock-selection breadth; it outperformed because it is structurally long semiconductor equipment and the S&P is structurally long Alphabet.** Yesterday the same tilt cost 0.71pp; today it earned 0.32pp. **Over the eight sessions of August, that tilt has produced +0.63% against SPY's +3.15%.** The honest conclusion: **the tilt is a source of tracking error, and so far its sign has been negative.** Two sessions do not change that, and the 2.52pp August gap is the number that matters.

**6b. The momentum-weight gradient is holding, and it is the most durable structural finding in the book.** Within the residual ladder, the *lowest* momentum weight leads all three cadences: monthly **w0595 +7.10% vs w9010 +1.85%**; biweekly **w0595 +7.90% vs w8020 −5.22% (a 13.1pp spread)**; weekly's best is w2080 at +5.81% against w7030 at −1.81%. **The ladder was built precisely to measure this, and it is measuring it consistently across three independent rebalance cadences over 14 weeks.** That is real evidence that the *residual* (idiosyncratic) leg carries the signal and the momentum leg dilutes it — consistent with `residual_roa_6535` beating `mom_roa_6535` since May, and with the `mom_*` family being the only one underwater at −8.78%.

**The corollary is uncomfortable and should be stated: `residual_w0595` is 95% quality / 5% momentum. If the gradient's endpoint is the winner, the ladder is telling you the momentum signal contributes approximately nothing, and the honest next experiment is a 0/100 rung to find out whether momentum's optimal weight is actually zero.** The current grid cannot answer that — it stops at 5%.

**6c. Cadence ordering — monthly (+4.14%) > weekly (+2.13%) > biweekly (+1.40%) — remains unexplained and is now 14 weeks old.** It is not monotonic in turnover (weekly trades most, biweekly least among the two sub-monthly cadences, yet biweekly is worst), which rules out the simplest transaction-cost story. **This is a standing open question, not a finding.** Something a future session could actually test: whether the biweekly ladder's anchor date happens to align with adverse rebalance days, which would be a scheduling artifact rather than a signal-decay result.

**6d. The LLM overlay's failure mode is now legible enough to state as a hypothesis.** Across both arms the pattern is the same: **the vetoes are directionally right on risk and wrong on cost.** The stock overlay vetoed four names, was right on three, and still lost to its control because the control held the one it got wrong. The sector overlay vetoed XLE, was wrong, and forfeited 9.2pp in the period's best sector while parking 23.9% in cash. **The overlay appears to be selecting for "names likely to fall" and being paid in avoided losses that are smaller than the foregone gains — which is what a risk filter with no positive expected return looks like.** That is testable at the kill-switch review: if scores correlate with subsequent returns but the *treatment* still loses, the signal is real and the position sizing / cash drag is the defect. **n = 13 of the 30-pick threshold; do not conclude yet.**

**6e. No new long-term-viable sleeve concept is supported by today's data, and today argues against one specific idea.** A tempting read of today would be "add a semi-cap sleeve." **Reject it.** Today's semi-cap gain is the exact reversal of yesterday's semi-cap loss, neither had a dated ticker-specific catalyst at the index level, and the AEHR/KLIC/TER moves are small-cap high-beta names that moved 4–10% largely on sector sentiment. **A concentrated semi-cap sleeve would be a leveraged bet on the AI-capex cycle wearing a factor costume**, and the book already carries $536,490 of that exposure implicitly. The residual-vs-momentum evidence in §6b is a far better-supported concept and it is already deployed.

**6f. The infrastructure lesson from the ladder bug outranks any strategy insight this week.** A $282.88 bookkeeping error on a $7.7M book is immaterial as P&L and material as a *measurement* failure: it turned a −0.0008% day into a reported −0.0045% day, a factor of 5.6. **A track record's value is precisely its measurement fidelity — that is the whole deliverable here.** The generalizable rule the incident establishes: **every process that writes to `paper_nav` must pass the same coverage gate, not just the MTM path.** One gate on one path is not a guard; it is a guard-shaped hole.

**Every 08-10 delta is unchanged to the cent for a fifth consecutive reading. Every 08-11 row is exact.** That combination is the whole finding:

1. `verify_run`'s cash-reconciliation test evaluates the **latest settled day**. On 08-11 that day is now correct, so all 76 sleeves pass.
2. Its continuity test only asks whether a row **exists** for each trading day. The 08-10 rows exist.
3. Therefore **the wrong rows are no longer detectable by the system that detected them.** Yesterday's entry predicted the FAIL would repeat nightly "until someone re-marks it." ### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**3a. July CPI landed at 08:30 ET and came in line.** Primary release: [BLS, *Consumer Price Index — July 2026*, published 2026-08-12](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/cpi_08122026.htm).

| Measure | July 2026 | Prior | Consensus |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Headline CPI, m/m SA | **+0.1%** | −0.4% (June) | **+0.1%** |
| Headline CPI, y/y | **3.4%** | 3.5% | **3.4%** |
| Core CPI (ex food & energy), m/m | **+0.2%** | — | — |
| Core CPI, y/y | **2.5%** | — | — |

Component detail: **shelter +0.1% m/m, accounting for roughly two-thirds of the headline increase**; **used cars and trucks +0.4% m/m**. Year-over-year: **energy +14.7%**, **gasoline +24.6%**, **airline fares +25.5%**, **food +3.0%** with food-away-from-home **+3.4%** ([Quartz, 2026-08-12](https://qz.com/us-cpi-july-2026-consumer-prices-inflation-081226); [NBC News, 2026-08-12](https://www.nbcnews.com/business/economy/cpi-inflation-july-2026-rcna591698)).

**The structure of this print matters more than the headline for a book that is 24.82% Technology.** Core at **2.5% y/y** against headline **3.4%** means the overshoot is concentrated in energy — a supply shock traceable to the Strait of Hormuz closure — while the demand-side measure is within a percentage point of target. **That is the composition that argues against a hike, and the market read it that way.**

**3b. September Fed odds moved toward a hold.** Ahead of the print, markets priced roughly a **51–52% probability of a 25bp September hike**, itself down from **67% a week earlier** ([CNBC, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/treasury-yields-inflation-cpi-data.html)). After the print, traders "shifted bets toward a Federal Reserve rate hold in September, moving from a roughly 50-50 split the previous day" ([Yahoo Finance live blog, 2026-08-12](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-august-12-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-cpi-report-091555133.html)).

Chair **Kevin Warsh** is reported by the Financial Times, via unnamed sources, to remain open to a September hike if the coming weeks' data run hot ([Yahoo, *The Aug. 12 Inflation Report Could Decide Whether Kevin Warsh Raises Rates in September*](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/aug-12-inflation-report-could-140522541.html)). **That sourcing is second-hand and is recorded as such.** A MarketWatch economic-calendar post lists "CPI, then testimony from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh"; **the post carries no date I could verify, so no Warsh testimony is asserted for today.**

**3c. Treasury yields — no post-CPI level is adopted.** The only 08-12 figures located are **pre-print**: 10-year **4.682%**, 2-year **4.212%**, 30-year **5.231%**, all described as "little changed as investors await key inflation data" ([CNBC, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/treasury-yields-inflation-cpi-data.html)). Federal Reserve **H.15** has not posted 08-12. **Standing note from yesterday still applies: H.15 revised its own 08-10 figures (10-year 4.70%→4.72%, 30-year 5.23%→5.25%, 3-month 3.91%→3.89%), so same-day citations are provisional for at least one business day.**

**3d. The semiconductor and memory move has a dated, specific driver — and a stale imposter that must be rejected.**

**Adopted (dated 2026-08-11/08-12):**
- **Super Micro Computer (SMCI)** closed fiscal 2026 with Q4 revenue **$11.12B, +93% y/y**, and guided Q1 revenue to **$14.5–15.5B against ~$11.7–11.8B consensus** with adjusted EPS **$1.01–1.10 vs ~$0.72–0.76 consensus**, plus **more than $60B of new orders** booked in FY2026. The stock is **+7.5% to +9.5%** pre-market ([TipRanks, 2026-08-12](https://www.tipranks.com/news/why-are-micron-nvidia-amd-intel-and-super-micro-stocks-rising-today-8-12-26); [CNBC premarket movers, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/stocks-making-the-biggest-moves-premarket-crwv-smic-cohr.html)).
- **CoreWeave (CRWV)** reported Q2 revenue **$2.58B vs $2.56B** expected and an adjusted loss of **$1.03 vs $1.20** expected, with **revenue backlog at $104B**; the stock is **+17.4%** ([CNBC, 2026-08-11](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/11/coreweave-crwv-q2-earnings-report-2026.html); [Timothy Sykes, 2026-08-12](https://www.timothysykes.com/news/coreweave-inc-crwv-news-2026_08_12/)).
- **Micron executives told a technology forum on 2026-08-10** that AI is reshaping the memory cycle and demand is growing faster than industry supply ([TipRanks, 2026-08-12](https://www.tipranks.com/news/why-are-micron-nvidia-amd-intel-and-super-micro-stocks-rising-today-8-12-26)).
- **Lumentum (LITE, not held)** reported Q4 FY2026 on **2026-08-11** with revenue **+109% y/y** and Q1 guided to **~$1.25B**, and is up sharply pre-market — the direct read-through to the held optics names and to **COHR, which reports today**.
- **SanDisk (SNDK, not held)** is **+4%** pre-market on AI-storage demand signals — the direct read-through to **WDC and STX**.

**REJECTED — STALE, NOT ADOPTED.** A prominently-surfaced article headlined *"Chip Stocks Surge as SK hynix, Micron Lead AI-Fueled Rally"*, quoting **MU +7%, STX +8%, WDC +10%, SNDK +9.5%, AMD +5.5%, INTC +6%**, is **published 2026-07-21** and refers to a Tuesday three weeks ago ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/chip-stocks-surge-sk-hynix-174430156.html), publication date verified in-page). **Those percentages are not today's and must not be cited as such.** This is the **fourth stale-attribution catch this week** — after the TER $1B revolver (8-K dated 08-07 cited as an 08-11 catalyst), the "rate-hike fears ease" pieces citing the 08-07 payroll print, and the VTR/WELL quotes dated 08-12 that were actually 08-10 levels. **The pattern is now frequent enough to treat as a standing hazard of this research method: always date-check the article, not just the headline.**

**3e. ATEX — the reaction to last night's print is opening +1.57%, and there is a second, separate catalyst.** ATEX is at **$94.40 pre-market (08:50 ET) against a $92.94 close**, held in **59 sleeves at $121,543.73**.

- **Q1 FY2027 results** (reported 4:05 PM ET 08-11, [SEC Form 8-K, atex-20260811](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001304492/000130449226000045/atex-20260811.htm)): spectrum revenue **$1.958M vs ~$1.97M consensus** (+38% y/y), EPS **+$0.01 vs −$0.58 consensus**, driven by a **$10.7M gain on exchange of broadband licenses**, net income **$0.240M vs $25.180M**, no forward guidance, **$116.0M cash / no debt / $226.7M buyback remaining**. The earnings call is **today at 09:00 ET** ([Anterix IR](https://investors.anterix.com/news-releases/news-release-details/anterix-sets-first-quarter-fiscal-2027-earnings-conference-call)).
- **Separately, on 2026-08-11 Anterix issued a statement supporting a SpaceX ex parte filing at the FCC** on buildout requirements for **5/5 MHz broadband licenses in the 896–901/935–940 MHz band**, backing technology-neutral buildout via existing Section 27.1505 terrestrial requirements or waiver-based satellite direct-to-device criteria, on the argument that optionality brings the spectrum to market faster ([GlobeNewswire, 2026-08-11](https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/08/11/3343105/0/en/anterix-issues-statement-in-support-of-spacex-proposal.html); [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/ATEX/anterix-issues-statement-in-support-of-space-x-xbftk7nubd7h.html)).

**The second item is the more consequential one for a spectrum-asset company and it was not in yesterday's entry.** ATEX's value case rests on the regulatory path for its 900 MHz holdings; a filing that widens the buildout options — and the presence of SpaceX as an interested party in the same band — is a structural datum, not a quarterly one. **Attribution between the two catalysts is not separable from a +1.57% pre-market print, and no attribution is claimed.**

Alphabet is bouncing +0.54%/+0.56% after yesterday's −3.84%/−3.61%, with no resolution of the three drivers.** The capex guide (**$195–205B for 2026**, quarterly capex **$44.9B, +100% y/y**), the **$25B senior-notes 8-K filed 2026-08-10**, and the appellate filings targeting search-remedy default-payment terms are all unchanged. Fresh, dated items overnight: **Gemini passed 1 billion users**, **Koray Kavukcuoglu was named head of DeepMind**, a **five-year Ryanair–Google Cloud Gemini deal**, and a **French newspaper competition complaint over AI summaries**. **A +0.5% bounce after a −3.8% distribution day retraces about an eighth of it; this book holds GOOGL in 59 sleeves and GOOG in 57, so the exposure is doubled and unresolved.**

Energy — a fourth day of unresolved crude sourcing, and a pre-market divergence.** [Fortune](https://fortune.com/article/price-of-oil-08-12-2026/) puts Brent at **$91.60 at 06:35 ET on 2026-08-12**; [TradingEconomics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil) has Brent at **$89.24 on 2026-08-11, +1.73%**; the Yahoo live blog says Brent "approached $90" on Strait-of-Hormuz enforcement. **No single settle is adopted.** Geopolitically: Pakistan's defense minister says Washington and Tehran are "close to some sort of arrangement" and Iran–Oman talks are advanced, while a senior Iranian official says the Strait stays closed until Tehran's conditions are met, and President Trump has said Tehran should pay reparations.

Sector-level context, not dated to today: State Street's Q3 2026 outlook upgraded healthcare from neutral to positive. **The practical point is compositional: on a day the book's Technology sleeve is up ~4% and its Healthcare sleeve is down ~0.5%, the two 25% blocks work against each other, and net book performance is decided by the size of the semiconductor leg.**

### 6. Strategic insights

**6a. Today is the cleanest test the book has had of whether its factor tilt is an edge or a beta bet — and unlike yesterday, the test runs in the favorable direction.** Yesterday's entry concluded that the book "is structurally long semiconductor equipment and the S&P is structurally long Alphabet," that this is a source of tracking error, and that "so far its sign has been negative." **This morning that same tilt implies +0.71% of NAV against SPY's +0.45%, on 36.2% coverage.** Three observations follow, and only the third is a finding:

- The mechanism is identical to yesterday's and the day before's — **the same six names (STX, MU, LRCX, AMAT, WDC, KLAC) account for $46.2k of the $54.8k implied gain**, i.e. **84% of it from six tickers that are 3.0% of the book's names and 13.9% of its open market value**.
- **The `mom_*` family is the family that owns this move.** It is the only family below inception capital (−8.78% average) and it is the momentum book, which is currently the semiconductor and memory complex. If today closes as it opens, the seven `mom_*` sleeves will post their best relative session in weeks.
- **The finding is that this is a one-factor book wearing seven strategy names.** Whether the sleeve is called `mom_v2`, `mom_roa_6535` or `residual_w9010`, the top-of-book exposure converges on the same AI-capex complex. **A 76-sleeve experiment whose daily P&L is decided by six tickers is measuring the AI-capex cycle with high precision and measuring the factor hypotheses with very little.** That is worth stating even though nothing in today's data suggests an action.

**6b. The verifier finding outranks every market observation in this entry, and it generalizes.** Yesterday's §6f drew the rule *"every process that writes to `paper_nav` must pass the same coverage gate."* **Today establishes a second and sharper one: a monitor that checks only the newest record cannot detect a corrupted older record, and worse, it will silently retract a true alarm as soon as a fresh good record arrives.** The 19 ladder rows produced four consecutive `verify_run` FAILs and then a PASS, with nothing repaired in between. **From an audit-trail standpoint this is the failure mode that matters most: not a wrong number, but a wrong number that the system has stopped calling wrong.** Two shapes a future session could evaluate — neither is proposed as work today, and neither is free:

- **Reconcile a rolling window** (say the last 5 settled days) rather than only the newest, at the cost of a longer verify run.
- **Reconcile the day any writer touched**, keyed off the rebalance/ladder logs, which is cheaper but only catches writer-caused divergence, not publication-lag divergence.

The standing constraint is unchanged and is the reason neither is a one-liner: **`daily_price_refresh.py` re-downloads the trailing 30 days with `INSERT OR REPLACE` by design**, so a stored NAV row is a snapshot of an input the system revises nightly (record CK). **A historical recon will produce false positives from legitimate upstream revisions, and telling those apart from real corruption is the actual design problem.**

**6c. Does today's macro support a new long-term-viable sleeve concept? One idea is weakly supported and one is actively contradicted.**

**Contradicted: an energy-tilt sleeve.** The CPI print shows energy **+14.7% y/y** and gasoline **+24.6% y/y** driving the entire headline overshoot while core sits at **2.5%** — a textbook supply-shock regime, and superficially the case for an energy overweight. **But the book's own energy names refuse to track it.** XLE is **−0.59% pre-market on a morning crude is reported higher**, and yesterday XLE rose 1.25% while ESEA fell 3.77% and INSW fell 1.48%. **The crude-to-equity transmission in this book is loose enough that an energy sleeve would be a bet on a specific transmission mechanism, not on the commodity.** The 4.85% incidental energy weight already carries the exposure.

**Weakly supported: nothing new — the residual-vs-momentum evidence remains the best-supported live concept and is already deployed.** The ladder gradient (monthly w0595 +7.10% vs w9010 +1.85%; biweekly w0595 +7.90% vs w8020 −5.22%) still points the same way, but **today is precisely the kind of session that would push the gradient the other way** — a strong momentum day in the semiconductor complex is exactly what the high-momentum-weight rungs are built to capture. **The right use of today is not to update the conclusion; it is as an out-of-sample check on it.** Tonight's post-close entry should report the ladder gradient's one-day slope: **if the high-momentum rungs (w80–w95) lead today by a wide margin, the gradient is a regime artifact of July rather than a structural finding**, and the whole §6b conclusion from the 08-11 entry weakens. **That is a falsifiable prediction, registered here before the close, and it costs nothing to check.**

**No recommendation is made from today's data.** The pre-market is a single unopened session, the tilt's sign has flipped twice in three days, and the honest summary of August remains **+0.63% for the book against +3.15% for SPY**.

| J | 4 | 57 | 7.0% |
| Z | 2 | 30 | 6.7% |

The refresh runs **"30 batches of up to 200 tickers"** in alphabetical order. **V misses at 3.2× the all-alphabet rate and 8× the best bucket.** The likeliest reading is a partially-failed or rate-limited tail batch rather than 875 independent publication lags — the same failure shape as the record CI rate-limit episode. **This is an observation about the refresh, not a proven cause**; distinguishing "batch failed" from "Yahoo publishes alphabetically and we sampled mid-publication" needs a timestamped retry log the refresh does not currently write.

**Macro — July CPI, released 08:30 ET.** Headline **+0.1% m/m**, annual rate **3.4%** (down from 3.5%); core monthly and annual changes also matched the Dow Jones consensus ([CNBC, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/08/12/treasury-yields-inflation-cpi-data.html)). Rate traders cut the odds of a **September hike to 38% from 48% a day earlier**, with the September decision described as coming down to the August payrolls and CPI combination (same source).

**Treasuries barely reacted:** 10-year **4.682%**, 2-year **4.212%**, 30-year **5.231%**, all reported flat or unchanged ([CNBC, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/08/12/treasury-yields-inflation-cpi-data.html)). **Caveat: it is not stated whether these are 3pm settlement values or an intraday read**, and Fed H.15 has not posted 08-12 as of this writing — the same caution applies as on 08-11, when H.15 subsequently revised its own 08-10 figures.

**Why this matters for the book.** An in-line print that lowers hike odds without moving the long end is the ideal configuration for the book's largest exposure: it supports long-duration growth multiples (semis, AI infrastructure) without a rates shock, and it removes a tail risk that had been suppressing the exact names the momentum sleeves own.

### 3. Key position analysis

**3a. Lumentum's FQ4 print was the day's true origin event, and the book does not own Lumentum.** LITE reported revenue **above $1 billion, roughly +109% y/y and +24% q/q**, with EPS **$3.23 against consensus of ~$2.90–3.00** and y/y EPS growth of **267%**, materially above the optimistic end of its own guidance. It guided FQ1 FY27 revenue to **$1.225–1.275B** and EPS to **$4.05–4.35**, on **39.5–40.5% non-GAAP operating margins**, citing record cloud transceiver shipments and the start of 1.6T transceiver shipping ([XTB market analysis](https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/lumentum-earnings-the-photonics-industry-is-accelerating-thanks-to-ai); [Investing.com earnings call transcript](https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-lumentum-tops-q4-2026-forecasts-as-ai-demand-lifts-outlook-93CH-4852933); [24/7 Wall St.](https://247wallst.com/cards/lumentum-holdings-inc-q4-2026-earnings-lite-01kzs8he4gd98w6nxkfgbb2vyy)).

**The read-through is what the book captured.** CIEN and COHR are the two optical names it holds:

| Ticker | 08-11 | 08-12 | Day | Book impact | Sleeves |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| **CIEN** | $387.53 | $432.05 | **+11.49%** | **+$5,454.22** | 31 |
| **COHR** | $328.57 | $355.64 | **+8.24%** | +$168.28 | 2 |

Ciena's move is explicitly attributed to Lumentum: *"a blowout earnings report from optical networking peer Lumentum that triggered a sweeping rally across the AI-driven optical communications complex,"* with Lumentum's optical-component demand commentary read directly into Ciena's order pipeline ([Investing.com, 2026-08-12](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/why-is-ciena-stock-surging-today-93CH-4855861); [Benzinga, 2026-08-12](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/08/61152475/why-is-ciena-stock-surging-on-wednesday)).

> **Position-sizing note that is worth stating plainly.** COHR is **+8.24%** and contributed **$168.28**, because the book holds **$2,210.82** of it across 2 sleeves. CIEN is **+11.49%** and contributed **$5,454.22** on **$52,931.17**. Same catalyst, same direction, **32× the P&L difference from position size alone**. The cascade arm's projection was likewise beaten — it was marked to ≈$103,228 pre-market and closed indicative at **$105,436.66**.

**Equal-weight vetoed basket: +2.63%.** Yesterday the same basket read **−4.19%** and the veto looked like it was adding 4.19pp of value. **One session flipped the sign: the veto now costs ~2.63pp on an equal-weight read.** Against the pre-registered control — which holds **only MU** — the treatment is behind by **9.86pp** this cycle.

**The single most uncomfortable datapoint in today's entry:** the treatment's four vetoes included **the day's best percentage performer in the entire book (BE, +12.29%)** and **the day's second-largest dollar winner (MU, +$13,019.15)**. Its one correct call, WDC, rose **+3.69%** today, eroding that too. Meanwhile the BUY it *did* log — STX, score 6 — was **the book's single largest dollar winner at +$17,428.67**.

> **What this is and is not.** **n = 13 logged stock decisions** (`llm_overlay_log` holds 13 rows; ids run to 16 with gaps at 4, 5 and 9 — the correction first recorded on 08-11 stands). The kill switch is **12 months / 30 picks**. Nine trading days of a single decision cycle is not evidence about the hypothesis; it is one draw. **What it does establish is that the treatment's variance is enormous** — a 13.47pp lead can become 9.21pp on one tape day, because holding 100% cash is itself a large active position against a high-beta control.

### 6. Strategic insights — does the current lineup have structural edge?

**6a. Today produced the cleanest single-day ladder-gradient reading since the 05-01 seeding, and it points the opposite way from July.** Regressing each rung's day return on its residual-momentum weight:

| Cadence | w05 day | w95 day | Slope (pp per weight point) | r |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Monthly | +0.17% | +1.91% | **+0.0249** | **+0.930** |
| Weekly | +0.13% | +1.33% | **+0.0214** | **+0.896** |
| Biweekly | +0.08% | +2.00% | **+0.0275** | **+0.943** |

Full monthly-arm profile, w05 → w95: `+0.17 +0.21 +0.31 +0.33 +0.24 +0.25 +0.43 +0.61 +0.74 +1.08 +1.37 +1.88 +2.09 +1.90 +1.63 +1.94 +1.78 +1.92 +1.91`. It is monotone through the first thirteen rungs and flat-to-noisy across the top six.

**Why this matters.** Record CW pinned the July adverse-month gradient at roughly **−0.10 to −0.14pp of return per weight point per month**. **One session today delivered +0.021 to +0.028pp per weight point — about 20–25% of a full adverse month, with the sign reversed.** That is a live, dated confirmation that CW's "sizing number" is real and symmetric: the weight axis is not a cosmetic knob, it is a genuine exposure dial, and the exposure it dials is residual momentum, which in August 2026 means AI infrastructure.

**Why this is not a finding about which rung is better.** CW's caveat binds fully and is repeated here so no future reader quotes the r-value as significance: **the 19 rungs are not 19 independent observations** (adjacent-rung Jaccard 0.74–0.94; **w05 vs w95 = 0.04, four shared names out of ~48**). This is a dose-response curve between two near-disjoint portfolios sampled once. An r of +0.93 across 19 correlated rungs on one day is a statement about *shape*, not about *evidence*.

**6b. The book is, functionally, one factor with 201 names attached to it.** Today's decomposition:

| Slice | Share of book | Share of day P&L |
|---|---:|---:|
| Semiconductor/optical basket (14 priced names) | **16.9%** | **72.0%** |
| Technology sector (all names) | **24.5%** | **86.9%** |
| Healthcare sector (all names) | **23.6%** | **−8.1%** |

**Technology and Healthcare are 49% of the book by weight and moved in opposite directions (+4.54% vs −0.42%) on the same day.** The nominal diversification — 201 tickers, 3,227 legs, 76 sleeves — is diversification *within* factors, not *across* them. Everything the book actually earns right now comes from one AI-infrastructure trade, and the second-largest exposure is a biotech book that is not hedging it so much as sitting beside it.

**This is a measurable fragility, and it is currently unmeasured.** The system has coverage gates, anomaly scans, cash recon, continuity checks and cadence checks — and **nothing at all that reports factor concentration or effective breadth.** A book can pass `verify_run` 76/76 while being a single levered bet.

**6c. Does the lineup have structural edge? Honest answer: not demonstrated, and today does not move that.** Three facts, none of which today changed:

1. **Month-to-date the book trails SPY by 1.55pp and QQQ by 3.33pp** (§5). Its best relative day of August still leaves it behind both indices for the month.
2. **The `mom_*` family is −6.08% to −10.01% since inception** while SPY is +7.19% and QQQ +7.35% over the comparable window. Today's +2.6% family day is a recovery within a large deficit, not evidence of edge.
3. **The residual family's leaders are the LOW-residual rungs** (`residual_w0595_2wk` +7.98%, `residual_w0595` +7.28%), which is the inversion of the BV backtest's w80–90 plateau that record CW explicitly declined to treat as a refutation. Today's positive gradient narrows that inversion by one day's worth and nothing more.

**6d. Is any new long-term-viable sleeve concept supported by today's data? No new sleeve — but today does support building one new *instrument*.** Stating this carefully, because a single session is the weakest possible evidence base for a strategy:

- **Not supported: an "AI infrastructure" or "optical" sleeve.** Today's evidence for it is one catalyst (LITE's FQ4) propagating through correlated names in one session. That is exactly the shape of the overfits already closed in this project — the turn-of-month and restricted-universe families died on more evidence than this.
- **Not supported: re-weighting the ladder toward high-residual rungs.** The July and August-12 gradients have **opposite signs of similar magnitude**. Two observations, one each way, is a coin flip with extra steps.
- **Genuinely supported: an effective-breadth / factor-concentration monitor.** §6b is computable read-only from data already in the DB (`paper_positions` × `price_cache` × `sector_cache`), needs no new data source, and answers a question no existing check asks: *how much of today's P&L came from how little of the book?* Today's answer — **72% from 16.9%** — would have been worth knowing on every day of the −23.5% July momentum drawdown, and it is the number that would tell Evan whether the 76-sleeve lineup is 76 experiments or one. It fits the existing `check_*.py` read-only pattern exactly.
- **Also worth logging, not yet a proposal:** the `verify_run` tolerance question from §0b. The pattern is now established beyond argument. **Each day's defect freezes the moment the next day marks correctly.** `verify_run` recons the newest settled day only, so:

| date | defect | magnitude | flagged when? | flagged now? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-08-10 | 19 weekly-ladder rows | **−$282.91** | never (marked before it was measurable) | **no, permanently** |
| 2026-08-11 | 20 rows, TRS half-cent | **+$4.97** | FAIL 56/76 on 08-12 evening | **no, permanently** |
| 2026-08-12 | none | $0.00 | — | PASS 76/76 |

Two properties of this make it worse than a one-off. First, **severity is inverted**: the $4.97 error triggered a loud 20-sleeve FAIL while the $282.91 error has never triggered anything, because the tolerance is an absolute **$0.05** rather than proportional to sleeve NAV. Second, **the defect rate is set by the vendor, not by us**: Yahoo revised a two-day-old TRS close by half a cent and that alone was enough. Every such revision arriving after a day is marked produces one more permanently-frozen row.

This is a reported finding, not a repair. Rewriting a stored `paper_nav` row is Evan's call, and record CK already ruled out the broad-span rewrite; `remark_nav_day.py --date 2026-08-10` exists and is the one-date instrument, but running it is a live-DB write and outside this task's read-only scope.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**3a. July PPI came in cold and is the second cool inflation print in two days.**

The Producer Price Index for final demand was **unchanged in July, seasonally adjusted**, released by the BLS on **Thursday 2026-08-13 at 8:30 a.m. ET** ([BLS PPI news release, 2026-08-13](https://www.bls.gov/news.release/archives/ppi_08132026.htm)). Consensus was **+0.2%** ([Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-13](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-trending-higher-on-rate-hike-bets-earnings-100145282.html)), so this is a **downside surprise**.

Composition, from the BLS release:
- **Final demand goods −0.7%**
- **Final demand services +0.2%**
- **Final demand construction +2.2%**
- **12-month unadjusted: +4.7%**

The annual rate is the more striking number: **5.5% in June → 4.7% in July, the lowest since March 2026** ([Trading Economics, US Producer Prices Change](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/producer-prices-change)). For context, May was 6.0%. That is 130bps of deceleration in two months, driven by the goods side rolling over.

This follows Wednesday's **July CPI: headline +0.1% m/m / 3.4% y/y** (from 3.5%), **core 2.5% y/y**, in line with consensus ([Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-12](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-wednesday-august-12-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-cpi-report-091555133.html)).

**Rate path.** The Fed left rates unchanged in July and the market is pricing a possible **hike**, not a cut — an unusual configuration worth restating. Traders were at **~52%** for a September 25bp hike earlier in the week, down from **~67%** a week prior; yesterday's post-close entry recorded the CPI print cutting it toward **38%** ([CNBC, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/treasury-yields-inflation-cpi-data.html); [Bloomberg, 2026-08-12](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-12/bond-traders-keep-cointoss-wager-on-september-fed-hike-post-cpi)). **No post-PPI probability reading was located and none is asserted here.**

**Treasuries.** The 10-year fell **3bp to 4.654%** after the CPI print on 08-12, and was quoted at **4.66%** ahead of an auction ([CNBC, 2026-08-12](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/12/treasury-yields-inflation-cpi-data.html)). **No verified post-PPI 08-13 yield was found** — this is the second consecutive day the entry cannot adopt a same-session yield, and it is a real gap given 24.5% healthcare and 2.05% real-estate exposure.

**Labour.** Initial jobless claims for the week ended **2026-08-08** came in at **209,000**, up 9,000 from an upward-revised 200,000; the **4-week moving average was 199,000, unchanged**; insured unemployment rate **1.2%** for the week ended 08-01 ([DOL/ETA weekly claims release, 2026-08-13](https://www.dol.gov/ui/data.pdf)). A 209k print with a flat 4-week average is not a labour-market signal in either direction.

**3b. Technology / semiconductors — 25.60% of the book, and the dominant theme is a reaction-function problem, not a fundamentals problem.**

Three companies reported strong numbers this week and all three sold off:

**Cisco (not held, but the read-through matters)** — FQ4 FY26 on **2026-08-12**: record revenue **$17.3B, +18% y/y**; non-GAAP EPS **$1.22, +23%**; both above guidance. FY27 guide **$72.2–73.4B** (~15% growth at the midpoint). **AI orders exceeded $4B against $3.7B guided**, and FY27 AI revenue targets were raised to **$6.5–7B**. The stock closed the regular session at **$123.95, +2.92%**, then **fell 4.6% after hours to $118.18** on gross-margin guidance pressured by a heavier hardware mix ([Investing.com, 2026-08-12](https://www.investing.com/news/company-news/cisco-q4-fy26-slides-ai-orders-surge-45x-shares-dip-on-margins-93CH-4856377); [TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262098676-cisco-csco-q4-fy2026-earnings-9-billion-ai-orders-networking-124-resistance-tradingkey)).

**Coherent (COHR — held, 2 sleeves, $2,211)** — FQ4 FY26 on **2026-08-12**: revenue **$2.05B, +33.8% y/y**; GAAP gross margin **38.5%**, non-GAAP **40.2%**; GAAP diluted EPS **$1.19**, non-GAAP **$1.74 versus $1.62 consensus** (+$0.12); revenue beat the **$1.98B** estimate. FQ1 FY27 guidance: revenue **$2.2–2.4B**, non-GAAP gross margin **39.5–41.5%**, non-GAAP opex **$400–420M**, tax rate 18–20%, **non-GAAP EPS $1.85–2.05**. Full-year revenue **$7.118B, +22.5%**. **Shares slid 5% after the announcement**, reversing an 8% intraday gain earned on Lumentum's read-through, and are **−3.84% pre-market at $342.00** ([Investing.com, 2026-08-12](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/coherent-posts-a-blowout-q4-and-aggressive-guidance-yet-shares-take-a-5-haircut-4856014); [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/COHR/coherent-corp-reports-fourth-quarter-and-full-year-fiscal-2026-4dp7hm0orxpy.html)).

**Cerebras (not held)** — **missed** Q2 revenue estimates and is **−19% pre-market** ([TheStreet, 2026-08-13](https://www.thestreet.com/stock-market-today/stock-market-today-dow-jones-sp-500-nasdaq-updates-aug-13-2026)).

**Applied Materials reports today after the close, conference call 4:30 PM ET.** Consensus **$3.39 EPS on approximately $9B revenue**, about **+23% y/y**; an alternative compilation has adjusted EPS **$3.36, +35.5%** from $2.48 a year ago. Company guidance was **revenue ~$8.95B ±$500M and adjusted EPS $3.36 ±$0.20** (i.e. **$3.16–3.56**). Street consensus is **Moderate Buy** with an average target of **$603.23**, ~12% above current levels; AMAT has beaten in each of the last four quarters. The stock is **~27% below its YTD peak of $739.67** but **+190% over the past year** ([Blockonomi](https://blockonomi.com/applied-materials-amat-earnings-preview-q3-results-due-thursday-august-13/); [Barchart via Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/dear-applied-materials-stock-fans-134930135.html); [TradingKey](https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262098841-applied-materials-amat-q3-earnings-august-13-2026-semiconductor-equipment-ai-tradingkey); [Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-13](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-trending-higher-on-rate-hike-bets-earnings-100145282.html)).

**The exposure is $141,621 across 56 sleeves — 1.84% of book — and the stock enters the print +4.29% from yesterday and +0.31% pre-market.** On the three-for-three precedent above, a beat is not sufficient for a positive reaction; margin commentary is what the tape is trading.

**Individual semi/storage catalysts:**

- **STX** rose **7.41%** on 08-12 on continued enthusiasm following a strong fiscal Q4 beat and FQ1 guidance well above consensus issued in late July, plus sector strength; the sector group was up 2.34% and STX outperformed it. Average analyst target **$1,090.19**; median of 15 targets over six months **$1,000** ([TradingKey, 2026-08-12](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262099791-market-movers-stx-20260812); [GuruFocus](https://www.gurufocus.com/news/9029051/is-seagate-technology-holdings-plc-stx-overvalued-after-70-rally-gf-value-says-overvalued)). STX is the **largest single-name driver in the book at $265,315 across 66 sleeves**, and GF Value tags it **overvalued** after the rally.
- **MU** traded lower Thursday morning despite the favourable backdrop. Supporting datapoint: **enterprise SSDs were 48% of global NAND shipments in Q2, nearly double the 26% share a year earlier**. On **2026-08-07 Citigroup's Atif Malik maintained Buy but cut the target to $1,150 from $1,400**; 40 of 45 analysts surveyed by S&P Global in July rated it buy/strong buy ([Benzinga, 2026-08-13](https://www.benzinga.com/analyst-stock-ratings/analyst-color/26/08/61166926/chinas-ymtc-tops-micron-in-nand-shipments-but-micron-wins-where-it-matters-revenue) — headline reachable, full text 403; [Intellectia](https://intellectia.ai/blog/micron-stock-analysis-august-2026)). A **"Micron's Memory Boom Is Heading For A Peak, Analyst Warns"** piece is also circulating ([Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/micron-memory-boom-heading-peak-100028273.html)); **its date and the analyst were not verified, so it is noted but not adopted.**

**3c. Healthcare — 24.49% of the book (25.83% including the XLV row), and it is the book's quiet underperformer.**

Yesterday healthcare **lost $7,621.03 (−0.42%)** while technology gained 4.54%. Pre-market **XLV is +0.46%**, the best of the five sector ETFs quoted.

Sector-level positioning: **State Street's Q3 2026 sector outlook upgraded healthcare from neutral to positive** after roughly a year of caution ([Seeking Alpha](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4629874-high-flyer-healthcare-stocks-ten-names-with-strong-momentum-weak-valuations)). **No dated 08-12/08-13 sector-wide healthcare catalyst was found**, and the searches returned mostly undated commentary — reported as a gap, not filled with narrative.
