### 6. Strategic insights — does the current sleeve set have structural edge?

**6a. The ladder gradient: no pre-market signal, and the cumulative picture survived Wednesday intact.**

Applying the 37 verified pre-market quotes to each rung and regressing implied day return on residual-momentum weight:

| cadence | slope (pp per weight point) | r | w05 | w95 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| monthly | −0.0001 | −0.064 | +0.077% | +0.073% |
| weekly | −0.0002 | −0.140 | +0.074% | +0.068% |
| biweekly | −0.0002 | −0.201 | +0.082% | +0.077% |

**That is a flat line, and it should be read as "no information", not as "no gradient".** Only 37 of 201 held names are quoted and most ladder constituents are among the unquoted, so every rung's implied move is dominated by the same handful of large shared names. This is a coverage artifact.

The cumulative gradient, computed on marked 08-12 NAVs from each sleeve's own inception:

| cadence | cross-rung spread | best rung | worst rung | slope | r |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|---:|
| monthly | 4.21pp | w60 **+7.95%** | w25 +3.74% | +0.0030 | +0.073 |
| weekly | 6.14pp | w20 **+6.15%** | w70 +0.02% | −0.0517 | −0.814 |
| biweekly | 11.25pp | w05 **+8.04%** | w80 −3.21% | −0.1135 | −0.913 |

**Wednesday's dramatic sign-flipped one-day gradient (+0.021 to +0.028 pp per weight point, r +0.90 to +0.94) did not change the cumulative conclusion.** The biweekly slope is still **−0.1135**, essentially identical to the **−0.1153** that record CW measured for the buy-and-hold decomposition, and the low-residual/high-ROA end still leads two of three cadences. One extraordinary session recovered a fifth of an adverse month and moved the cumulative regression barely at all — which is the correct behaviour for a cumulative statistic and a useful sanity check on it.

**The monthly cadence is now the odd one out**: its slope has gone slightly *positive* (+0.0030, r +0.073, i.e. no relationship) while weekly and biweekly remain strongly negative. Per record CW's own caveat this is not 19 independent observations — adjacent-rung Jaccard is 0.74–0.94 and w05-vs-w95 is 0.04 — so **the r-values are shape descriptors, never significance**. What can be said: **the sizing number CW pinned at 0.10–0.14pp of return per weight point per adverse month is holding up**, and that is the ladder's actual deliverable.

**6b. The structural finding of this week is about the monitor, not the strategies — and it is the more valuable one.**

The system now has a demonstrated, reproducible mechanism that manufactures permanent silent data errors:

1. `daily_price_refresh` re-downloads a rolling 30-day window nightly with `INSERT OR REPLACE`, by design.
2. Vendor revisions therefore arrive *after* a day has been marked.
3. `verify_run` recons only the **newest settled day**.
4. Therefore a stale row is flagged for **at most one evening**, and only if the revision lands before the next day marks.
5. Therefore **every revision that lands after the next mark is permanent and invisible.**

Two instances now exist, 24 hours apart, with opposite signs and a 57× magnitude difference: **−$282.91 (never flagged) and +$4.97 (flagged loudly, then frozen)**. Record CK established that stored historical NAV is **not reproducible in principle** for exactly this reason, and that finding blocked the M7.4 span rewrite. What this week adds is that **the same non-reproducibility is silently accumulating going forward**, at whatever rate the vendor revises.

**This is a genuine engineering finding with a defensible fix, and it is the kind of thing the project exists to produce.** The obvious candidate fix — make `verify_run` recon a rolling window rather than one day, and make the tolerance proportional to sleeve NAV rather than an absolute $0.05 — would have caught both defects and neither false alarm. **Recommending nothing here; it is a code change against a live monitor and Evan's call.** But the diagnosis is complete and the evidence is two clean paired cases.

**6c. Does any sleeve have structural edge? The honest read is: not demonstrated, and the month is going the wrong way.**

Facts, not narrative:

- **The book trails both indices MTD by −1.55pp (SPY) and −3.34pp (QQQ)** after its best day of the month.
- **`sector_top4_full_paper` (+7.71%) is the only systematic sleeve beating both benchmarks from inception** — and it is the ETF sleeve, i.e. the one with the least stock-selection content. It beat SPY (+7.19%) and QQQ (+7.35%) by 0.52pp and 0.36pp over 15 weeks. That is inside noise.
- **`residual_roa_6535_paper` (+4.46%) trails both benchmarks by ~2.7–2.9pp** despite being the backtest champion on risk-adjusted held-out metrics.
- **The three `mom_*` sleeves are −5.95% to −9.88% from inception** after a violent July and a strong August. Their August recovery (+6.7% to +7.9%) is real and is beating SPY handily this month, but it is recovering their own drawdown, not generating alpha.
- **The 07-06 cohort tells the same story with a cleaner clock**: five weeks in, **both index benchmarks lead all four systematic sleeves**, spy_benchmark_0701 at +2.82% against −0.86% to −4.19%.

**The single most defensible statement available from this data: across two independent inception cohorts (05-01 and 07-06), a passive index sleeve is beating the systematic stock-selection sleeves, and the one systematic sleeve that beats the index is the one that holds ETFs.** That is a coherent, uncomfortable signal and it is exactly what a forward out-of-sample test is for.

**6d. On new sleeve concepts — today's data supports one observation and no recommendation.**

The recurring pattern in this week's earnings is worth naming because it is measurable: **Cisco, Coherent and Cerebras all reported into a tape that punished them, and two of the three beat.** Lumentum beat on 08-11 and the read-through carried CIEN +11.49% and COHR +8.24% — then COHR's own beat the next day was sold. **That is a post-earnings-announcement-drift environment with an inverted sign for the reporting company and a positive sign for its peers.**

If a sleeve concept were to be drawn from this it would be a read-through/peer-reaction factor rather than a reporter-reaction factor. **It is not supported by today's data.** Three observations in one week, all in one sector, during an AI-capex regime, is an anecdote. **PEAD is also already on the ruled-out list** (HANDOFF, "Factor combos / sleeves (dilution/correlation)"), which raises the prior against it substantially. **No recommendation. Logged as an observation for the record so that if the pattern recurs across sectors and months it can be tested against a real prior rather than reconstructed from memory.**

The genuinely useful strategic output from today is §6b — a reproducible monitoring defect with a clean diagnosis — and §6c's uncomfortable cohort comparison. Both are worth more than a new sleeve idea.

**0c. THREE FROZEN NAV DEFECTS NOW EXIST, AND THE NEWEST IS 8× THE OTHER TWO COMBINED.** Recomputing all 76 sleeves read-only as `cash + Σ(qty × close)` against the stored `paper_nav.total_nav`:

| 2026-08-11 | 22 | **+$5.13** | TRS half-cent vendor revision | FAIL 56/76 on 08-12 | **no, permanently** |
| 2026-08-12 | 21 | **+$2,212.02** | VECO/VIAV/VLO/VSH carry-forward | **FAIL 55/76 tonight** | **no — freezes when 08-13 marks** |

The 08-10 block is unchanged to the cent for an eighth consecutive reading (−$36.61 to +$0.67, all 19 on the weekly ladder). The 08-11 block has **grown by two rows** since last night's reading of 20 — `mom_v1_paper` (+$0.07) and `mom_v1_0701_paper` (+$0.10) have joined it, which is itself evidence that the vendor is still revising 08-11 three days later.

**The trend is the finding.** $282.91 → $5.13 → $2,212.02. The magnitude of each frozen defect is set by *how much data was missing at mark time and how far it moved afterwards* — neither of which the system controls or records. `verify_run` recons only the newest settled day, so each error is visible for exactly one evening and then becomes permanent and invisible.

**Two structural observations, reported not fixed.** First, the tolerance is inverted with respect to severity: an absolute **$0.05** per sleeve fired on a half-cent last night and has never fired on 08-10's real −$36.61 row. Second, and more useful: **tonight's failure was informative and last night's was noise, and the monitor cannot tell them apart.** A proportional tolerance (say 1 bp of sleeve NAV, ≈$10) would have passed the TRS half-cent, failed tonight's $232 carry-forward gap, and failed 08-10's $36.61 — the correct answer in all three cases. That is a one-constant change, and it is Evan's call, not this task's.

**Repair remains Evan's decision.** `scripts/data_audit/remark_nav_day.py --date 2026-08-12 --execute` is the one-date instrument and would cure the newest defect *if run before 08-13 marks*; after that it becomes a rewrite of frozen history. **0d. A NEW BKGM-CLASS DATA GHOST — AND BOTH UNIVERSE FILTERS WOULD LET IT THROUGH.** `check_anomalies` flagged two items tonight:

```
=== 2026-08-13 17:17 | anomaly scan  close=2026-08-13  prior=2026-08-12  held=201
    cache_new=4347  thresholds held>300% cache>1000%@>=$1.00 ===
  MOVE  CFNB       +4112.1%  $33.9500->$1430.0000  [cache]
  NOCLOSE DMAA     no close on 2026-08-13  [HELD residual_w8020_wk_paper,
                   residual_w8515_wk_paper,residual_w9010_wk_paper,residual_w9505_wk_paper]
ANOMALIES: 2 flagged for 2026-08-13.
```

CFNB's cached history makes the corruption unambiguous — it printed **$33.95 to the cent on 08-05, 08-06, 08-07, 08-10, 08-11 and 08-12**, then $1,430.00 today. Its full cached span is 2010-01-04 → 2026-08-13, 4,177 rows, min $11.82, max $1,697.50.

**Why this matters, stated precisely.** CFNB is held by **zero sleeves**, so there is no live P&L or NAV impact today. The forward risk is the universe filter, and I checked both against the code in `trading_bot/factors/universe.py`:

- **`MAX_PRICE_USD = 5000.0`** rejects a corrupt *current* price above $5,000. **$1,430 passes.**
- **`MAX_HIST_RATIO = 100.0`** rejects a ticker whose *historical* price on `as_of` exceeds 100× its *current stable* price (median of the last 60 closes). CFNB's corruption runs the other way — the current print is the bad one — and against a stable median near $34 the historical max of $1,697.50 gives roughly **50×. It passes too.**

This is structurally the same hole that let **BKGM** rank #1 by momentum across the 2025_H1 frozen window until the 2026-06-01 audit, and `MAX_PRICE_USD` was added specifically to close it — at a threshold this ghost sits comfortably under. The mitigating facts are real: `check_anomalies` caught it the same evening, and 12-1 momentum skips the most recent month, so a single stale print would not enter the ranking signal immediately. The risk is if it **persists and ages** into the lookback before the 2026-09-01 rebalance. `check_anomalies` is non-blocking and nothing auto-cleans `price_cache`.

**DMAA is the second flag and is now a three-part pattern:** identical $10.71 closes on 08-10, 08-11 and 08-12, then **no 08-13 close at all**. Four weekly-ladder sleeves hold it. Total exposure is ~$9,050 (0.12% of held value), so it changes nothing quantitatively, but it should not be read as a live mark.

**3b. AMAT: a beat, a very large guidance raise, and a lower stock. Fourth consecutive one this week.**

This morning's entry named the setup risk precisely — "a beat is not the setup risk; the reaction function is" — and the reaction function won again.

| Metric | Result | Consensus | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-GAAP EPS | **$3.50** | $3.40 (Benzinga) / $3.45 (Quiver) | **Beat** |
| Revenue | **$9.115B** (record) | ~$9.176B | Marginal miss (−$60.7M) |
| Operating income | **$3.08B, 33.7% of revenue** (record) | — | — |
| FQ4 revenue guide | **~$10.3B** | ~$9.62B | **Very large raise** |

Management raised its **Semiconductor Systems revenue expectation for calendar 2026**, citing "unprecedented demand for its materials engineering solutions."

**The stock fell anyway.** One report has it at **$506.51, −5.24%** from the $534.54 regular-session close; another has **−3.14% at $517.78**. Bloomberg headlined the reaction as "tepid." The options market had priced an implied move of roughly **11%** either way, against a ~6% average one-day move over the prior four quarters.

**Position:** AMAT is held in **56 sleeves, $138,104.25 (1.78% of held market value)**, and it **fell −2.48% into the print today** ($548.15 → $534.54) after rising +4.29% yesterday. At the midpoint of the two reported after-hours prints (~−4.2%), the mark-to-market exposure into tomorrow's open is roughly **−$5,800** across the book — real but not structural.

**The pattern is now four for four this week, and it is the most useful thing in this report.** Cisco (record revenue, guidance raise, AI orders above plan) **−4.6%**. Coherent (revenue +33.8%, EPS beat, guide above) **−5%**. Cerebras (miss) **−19%**. Applied Materials (beat, ~7% guidance raise over consensus) **−3% to −5%**. **Three of the four beat and raised, and all three sold off.** That is a market that has already priced the AI capital-expenditure cycle and is now selling the confirmation — a regime observation with direct bearing on §6.

### 6. Strategic assessment — does the current book have structural edge?

**6a. The ladder gradient flipped positive for a second day, but far more weakly, and the monthly cadence has now gone flat.**

| Cadence | Day slope (pp/wt point) | r | Cumulative slope | r | Spread | Leader |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Monthly | **+0.0015** | +0.232 | **+0.0045** | **+0.105** | 4.54pp | **w60** |
| Weekly | **+0.0074** | +0.749 | **−0.0446** | −0.755 | 6.27pp | w15 |
| Biweekly | **+0.0044** | +0.534 | **−0.1098** | −0.895 | 11.43pp | w05 |

Yesterday's day slopes were **+0.0249 / +0.0214 / +0.0275 at r +0.90 to +0.94** — monotone and clean. Today's are a quarter to a third of that size with r between +0.23 and +0.75. **One strong day for high-residual-momentum rungs does not repeat as a trend.**

**The cumulative picture is where the interesting change is.** The monthly cadence's cumulative slope is now **+0.0045pp per weight point at r = +0.105** — statistically indistinguishable from zero — and its leader has migrated from the w05 end to **w60, the middle of the ladder**. Weekly and biweekly still show the low-residual/high-ROA lead (r −0.755 and −0.895), but monthly no longer does.

**Read this against record CW's decomposition, and do not over-read it.** CW established that essentially the entire gradient is **2026-05-01 stock selection, not trading**, that the three cadences are **not statistically distinguishable** over 3/13/7 rebalance events, and that **the 19 rungs are not 19 observations** (adjacent-rung Jaccard 0.74–0.94; w05 vs w95 = **0.04**, four shared names of ~48). It is a dose-response curve between two near-disjoint portfolios sampled once. **The monthly slope going flat is exactly what you would expect from a curve whose sign is driven by one adverse month (July) as later months accumulate — it is not new evidence that weight does not matter.** Never quote r here as significance.

**6b. Two structural properties of the current book, both visible in today's data.**

**First: the book is a concentrated semiconductor bet that its own construction did not intend.** Technology is 25.35% of held value and produced **81% of the day's net P&L (+$50,547 of +$62,026)**. Four names — MU, STX, WDC, LRCX — are 11.4% of the book and produced 65% of the net gain. Add AMAT and KLAC and the memory/semi-cap complex is **~$1.14M, 14.7% of held value**. No sleeve has a sector constraint; momentum and ROA screens selected into this cluster independently, and MU, STX, WDC and LRCX are each held by 60–66 of the 76 sleeves. **The diversification implied by "76 sleeves and 201 names" is much weaker than it looks** — the sleeves are highly overlapping, and the ladder's own Jaccard evidence (adjacent rungs 0.74–0.94) already said so.

**Second, pointing the other way: the book's factor screens found the correct side of the energy trade without being told to.** Crude fell 2% on a demand-forecast cut and the book's Energy sleeve **rose 2.41%**, because its energy exposure is a refiner and a tanker operator rather than an upstream producer. That is a genuine, if small (3.49% of book), example of the screens producing a sensible economic position.

**6c. The evidence on whether the current sleeves have structural edge is not improving, and it should be stated plainly.**

**In both cohorts, both index controls beat every active systematic sleeve.**

- **May family:** QQQ +8.59% and SPY +7.94% beat residual_roa_6535 (+5.11%), mom_roa_6535 (−5.31%), mom_v1 (−9.52%) and mom_v2 (−9.78%). Only `sector_top4_full_paper` (+7.95%) is level with SPY, and it is an ETF-rotation sleeve, not a stock-selection one.
- **07-06 cohort:** SPY_0701 +3.54% and QQQ_0706 +1.28% beat residual_roa_6535_0701 (−0.25%), mom_roa_6535_0701 (−1.31%), mom_v1_0701 (−2.72%) and mom_v2_0701 (−4.33%).

**That is 3.5 months of forward out-of-sample data in the May family and 6 weeks in the 07-06 cohort, and no stock-selection sleeve is beating a passive index in either.** The window is far too short to be a verdict — the held-out backtests that justified these sleeves ran 2.4 years — but it is also no longer a handful of days, and the direction has been consistent. The honest framing is that **the forward test is currently failing to confirm the held-out result**, and the correct response is to keep running it, not to reinterpret it.

**One genuinely notable relative result:** `residual_roa_6535` remains the best active stock sleeve in both cohorts (+5.11% and −0.25%), which is what the 2026-06-13 revalidation predicted (best held-out Sharpe 1.21, best drawdown −20.1%, best Calmar 1.60). **The ordering among the systematic sleeves matches the backtest even though the absolute level does not.** That is weak but real corroboration that the ranking methodology is measuring something.

**6d. Does today's data support any new long-term-viable sleeve concept? One observation is worth logging; it is not a proposal.**

**The week's earnings reaction function is the most striking thing in this report, and it is not a sleeve.** Four AI-infrastructure names reported this week; three beat and raised guidance materially (Cisco, Coherent, Applied Materials) and all three sold off 3–5% after hours, while the one that missed (Cerebras) fell 19%. **A market that punishes beats and punishes misses harder is a market with asymmetric positioning — and that is a regime observation with a direct implication for this book, whose largest sector cluster is precisely these names.**

The tempting inference — an earnings-drift or reaction-asymmetry overlay — is exactly the kind of idea this project has already killed repeatedly. **PEAD is on the ruled-out list.** Reactive risk controls (stops at −10/−15/−20/−25%, stop-and-reenter) are on the ruled-out list. Preemptive overlays (trend-200DMA, vol-target) were closed 2026-07-14 as a family, pre-registered, on clean data. **The base rate for the overlay family in this project is zero for roughly a dozen attempts.** An n=4 pattern observed over four days in one sector is not a candidate; it is a note in a journal.

**No recommendation. What today actually justifies is one thing:** the concentration measured in §6b — 14.7% of the book in one earnings-correlated cluster, arrived at without any sleeve intending it — is a portfolio-construction fact worth tracking as a number, not a strategy idea worth testing. **The `experiment_report.py` and dashboard concentration panels already exist for this;** nothing new needs building.

**3a. The dated catalyst behind the memory move: SanDisk's 2026 Investor Day, held in New York on 2026-08-13.**

SanDisk laid out an **FY2028–FY2030 financial framework of mid-to-high-teens revenue growth, ~80% non-GAAP gross margins and ~50% adjusted free-cash-flow margins**, and jointly with Kioxia unveiled a **ninth-generation two-terabit QLC 3D NAND** device engineered for AI-workload bandwidth and datacenter energy efficiency ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-13](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/13/sandisk-unveils-multi-year-financial-model-and-growth-strategy-memory-stocks-soar/)). SNDK **closed +13.67%** after trading up more than 17% intraday, taking its market capitalisation to **$227.688 billion** ([TradingKey, 2026-08-13](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262103029-market-movers-sndk-20260813)).

Intraday on 08-13 the complex moved together: **SK Hynix +8% to $166.26, Micron +6% to $963.28, Western Digital +8% to $490.10**, Roundhill Memory ETF +5% to $57.33 ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-13](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/13/memory-stocks-open-flat-then-soar-micron-up-6-sk-hynix-8-sandisk-up-15-heres-whats-driving-the-move/)). Our official closes came in below those intraday marks — MU $949.83, WDC $487.29 — and the pre-market has now taken MU to **$980.00** and WDC to **$506.30**, i.e. **through** yesterday's intraday highs. Stockanalysis.com's own 08-14 headline attributes it directly: *"Why Are Memory Chip Stocks SNDK, MU, and WDC Rising in Pre-Market Today?"* — the rally following SanDisk's Investor Day guidance ([stockanalysis.com/stocks/mu/](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mu/), retrieved 2026-08-14 08:09 ET).

**The equal-weight vetoed basket is +5.32%. The veto costs 5.32pp on the cycle.** One of four vetoes (WDC) was right; three were wrong, and the largest miss (MU, +14.51%) is the one the pre-registered control actually holds — so **against its own control the cash treatment is behind 14.51% this cycle**, and MU's +3.18% pre-market widens that to roughly 17.9% intraday-equivalent.

**The lead the treatment still shows is entirely a July artifact.** It is +5.37pp ahead on cumulative NAV only because it sat in cash while the control lost 21% in July. On this cycle it is losing badly, and the gap has compressed from **13.47pp on Monday → 9.21pp Thursday morning → 5.37pp Thursday close → 2.37pp on this morning's pre-market**. **Four consecutive readings in one direction.**

**Kill-switch counters, stated exactly:** the pre-registered thresholds are **12 months / 30 picks**. Decisions logged in `llm_overlay_log` since the 2026-07-01 reset: **07-01 (3), 07-07 (2), 08-03 (5) = 10 decisions across 3 monthly cycles.** Nowhere near the threshold. **n=10 over 6 weeks is noise and this entry is not claiming the experiment has failed** — it is recording that the scores have not predicted returns in the two cycles where an outcome is observable (2026-07-07: WDC scored 6 → BUY → the cash treatment was flat while WDC fell; 2026-08-03: score 6 STX +10.87% correct, but the three lowest-scored vetoes returned +14.51%, +8.20% and +6.13%). **Score-to-return rank correlation is currently negative. That is the metric the kill switch is written against, and it is moving the wrong way.**

**Named, dated risks ahead:**
1. **SLGL reports Monday 2026-08-17** (16 sleeves, $28,459 at the 08-13 close). It has moved −15.63% then +17.54% in three sessions with no explanation across six searches. Reporting into that is a high-variance event on a position that has already proven it can move 17% on nothing.

4. **The 09-01 rebalance will re-rank the universe with CFNB in it** at a corrupted $1,430.00 and neither `MAX_PRICE_USD` nor `MAX_HIST_RATIO` rejecting it. This is the BKGM 2026-06-01 failure mode with 18 days of warning.

### 6. Strategic insights — does the current sleeve set have structural edge?

**6a. What the ladder says today, and what it does not.**

Cumulative from inception, on the 08-13 indicative:

| Cadence | slope (pp per weight point) | r | spread | leader | laggard |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| monthly | **+0.0045** | +0.105 | 4.54pp | w6040 **+8.82%** | w2575 **+4.28%** |
| weekly | **−0.0446** | −0.755 | 6.27pp | w1585_wk **+6.88%** | w7030_wk **+0.61%** |
| biweekly | **−0.1098** | −0.895 | 11.43pp | w0595_2wk **+8.78%** | w8020_2wk **−2.65%** |

Monthly's gradient is now **flat with its leader in the middle of the ladder** (w60), which is the third consecutive session it has read that way. Weekly and biweekly still carry the low-residual/high-ROA tilt.

**This morning's pre-market slope is the tightest positive fit of the week and it is worth naming precisely why:**

```
monthly  +0.00321 pp/wt  r +0.911
weekly   +0.00317 pp/wt  r +0.946
biweekly +0.00307 pp/wt  r +0.938
```

**r above +0.91 on all three cadences is not a factor signal — it is a concentration signal.** The high-residual rungs hold proportionally more MU/STX/WDC, so on a day when exactly those three names gap up, the gradient is almost perfectly monotone in weight. **That is the mechanism record CW already established from the other side: the ladder gradient is a dose-response curve between two near-disjoint portfolios (w05 vs w95 Jaccard = 0.04), so any single-day slope measures whichever names happen to differ between the ends.** It says nothing about whether residual momentum works. Never quote today's r as significance.

**6b. The uncomfortable read: the systematic sleeves are not beating their own index controls, and the 07-06 cohort is the cleanest evidence in the project.**

The 07-06 cohort exists precisely because it started on clean data with no contamination history. Five and a half weeks in, on the 08-13 indicative:

| Sleeve | cum from $100k |
|---|---:|
| `spy_benchmark_0701_paper` | **+3.54%** |
| `qqq_benchmark_0706_paper` | **+1.28%** |
| `residual_roa_6535_0701_paper` | **−0.25%** |
| `mom_roa_6535_0701_paper` | **−1.31%** |
| `mom_v1_0701_paper` | **−2.72%** |
| `mom_v2_0701_paper` | **−4.33%** |

**Four of four systematic factor sleeves are below their starting capital while both index controls are above it. All four lose to both controls.** The May family says the same thing with a longer window: `residual_roa_6535_paper` **+5.11%** against `spy_benchmark_paper` **+7.94%** and `qqq_benchmark_paper` **+8.59%**, with `mom_roa_6535` **−5.31%**, `mom_v1` **−9.52%** and `mom_v2` **−9.78%**.

**The one systematic sleeve holding its own is the ETF one.** `sector_top4_full_paper` is at **+7.95%** against SPY's **+7.94%** — dead level over 3.5 months, and it is the only sleeve in the systematic set that has not underperformed its control.

**The honest framing.** 3.5 months (May family) and 5.5 weeks (07-06 cohort) is far too short to falsify a monthly-rebalanced factor strategy — the held-out backtests that justified these sleeves covered 2.4 years, and record CW already showed that the entire cross-sectional spread in this book traces to **one adverse month (July)** in which `spy_benchmark_paper` returned +0.03% while the momentum sleeves lost ~23.5%. **What the live data does establish is narrower and still useful: this book's tracking error to the index is dominated by concentration, not by factor selection.** On 08-13, four names on 11.4% of held value produced 65% of the day's gain. This morning, three names produce more than 100% of the pre-market gain. A strategy whose daily P&L is decided by three correlated semiconductor tickers is not expressing a diversified momentum factor — it is expressing a sector bet that the ranking happens to keep re-selecting.

**6c. What today's data does and does not support as a new sleeve concept.**

**It raises one hypothesis with a real mechanism, and I am explicitly not recommending it.** The observation is that `residual_roa_6535`'s live tracking error is dominated by a handful of names inside one industry, and that the ranking re-selects that industry month after month because residual momentum measured against a market factor alone does not remove industry co-movement. The corresponding variant — **residual momentum computed against a market *and industry* factor, or an explicit per-sector cap in `paper_rebalance`** — is a standard construction, and it would mechanically reduce the concentration this journal keeps documenting.

**Three reasons it is a hypothesis and not a proposal.** (1) It has **no in-sample or held-out evidence** in this project; the last full re-validation (2026-06-13) tested none of it. (2) The project's own history is that overlays which look obviously right fail — the entire reactive *and* preemptive risk-control family was closed on 2026-07-14 (record BU) after preemptive overlays failed on clean data against both champions. (3) Proposing a variant on the strength of a **single morning's pre-market tape** is precisely the data-mining this project's validation discipline exists to prevent. **The only legitimate path is the standard one: pre-register it, backtest it in-sample and held-out with the frozen tests unmoved, and only then discuss deployment.**

**No recommendation is being made today.** The disciplined reading of the current data is: the sleeves are inside the range their backtests predict for a bad stretch, the sample is too short to conclude anything about edge, and the one thing that *is* measurable and actionable — concentration — is being recorded here so that a later decision can cite a dated observation rather than a memory.

```
TTMI   39.76 sh   $5,522.46 @ 138.88   4 sleeves
```

**TER and TTMI are ordinary late publication.** Both traded normally all week (TER 365.10 → 379.56 → 402.74 → 410.52; TTMI 130.08 → 130.74 → 138.10 → 138.88) and both will almost certainly publish overnight. **TER is tonight's largest carry-forward at $63,117 — 0.81% of held value — and it is the single biggest source of error in tonight's indicative.**

**DMAA is different, and the case against it has strengthened.** Its full cached run:

```
07-27 10.70 | 07-28 10.71 | 07-29 10.71 | 07-30 10.71 | 07-31 10.71 | 08-03 10.71
08-04 10.71 | 08-05 10.71 | 08-06 10.71 | 08-07 10.705 | 08-10 10.71 | 08-11 10.71
08-12 10.71 | 08-13 10.71 | 08-14 absent
```

**Fourteen consecutive sessions between $10.70 and $10.71**, with `check_anomalies` having flagged it `NOCLOSE` on 08-11, 08-12, 08-13 and again tonight. Yesterday's entry described this as six sessions; the true run is fourteen. A $10 name can be unchanged once. Fourteen sessions to the cent, with four publication gaps inside them, is a stale-feed shape and the $9,050 should be read as unmarked rather than flat.

**0d. THE CFNB GHOST RECURRED, AND LAST NIGHT'S INSTANCE WAS SILENTLY REVERTED.**

Tonight's `var/anomaly_report.log`:

```
=== 2026-08-14 17:16 | anomaly scan  close=2026-08-14  prior=2026-08-13  held=201 cache_new=4264 ===
  MOVE  CFNB       +4097.3%  $33.9500->$1425.0000  [cache]
  NOCLOSE DMAA     no close on 2026-08-14  [HELD 4 weekly-ladder sleeves]
  NOCLOSE TER      no close on 2026-08-14  [HELD 27 sleeves]
  NOCLOSE TTMI     no close on 2026-08-14  [HELD 4 sleeves]
ANOMALIES: 4 flagged.
```

Last night the same scanner flagged `CFNB +4112.1% $33.9500->$1430.0000` **on 08-13**. Read from `price_cache` tonight:

```
07-27 33.95 | 07-28 33.95 | 07-29 33.95 | 07-30 33.95 | 07-31 33.95 | 08-03 33.95
08-04 33.95 | 08-05 33.95 | 08-06 33.95 | 08-07 33.95 | 08-10 33.95 | 08-11 33.95
08-12 33.95 | 08-13 33.95 | 08-14 1425.00
```

**The 08-13 row now reads $33.95 again.** The overnight and evening refreshes overwrote yesterday's $1,430.00 with the correct value, and the corruption re-landed on the new date at a *different* price. That changes the finding materially: **this is not a one-off bad print, it is a recurring vendor defect that self-heals on a one-day lag.** Two consequences:

1. **Zero live P&L impact — CFNB is held by zero sleeves** (`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM paper_positions WHERE ticker='CFNB' AND status='open'` → `0`).
2. **The 09-01 rebalance is the real exposure, and both universe filters would pass it.** `MAX_PRICE_USD` is $5,000 and $1,425 is under it. `MAX_HIST_RATIO=100` compares *historical* to *current stable* price, and CFNB's corruption is in the *current* price — the BKGM direction, at roughly 42× against a 100 threshold. `check_anomalies` is non-blocking by design.

The mitigating fact is the self-heal: if the pattern holds, the ranking snapshot taken at a 09-01 evening rebalance would read a $33.95 08-31 close, not a ghost. **That is a hope, not a guard.** The exposure is a rebalance that reads a same-day price on a night the ghost is live.

**+$28,811.01 from three tickers, against a net book gain of +$30,099.95 — 95.7%.** MU and STX are the book's two largest single-name positions at **$295,773 (3.81%)** and **$294,085 (3.78%)** of held value; WDC is sixth at $152,218 (1.96%).

The catalyst is dated, specific and a carry-over. **SanDisk's 08-13 Investor Day** — an FY2028–FY2030 framework of mid-to-high-teens revenue growth, ~80% non-GAAP gross margins and ~50% adjusted FCF margins, plus a jointly-unveiled ninth-generation 2-terabit QLC 3D NAND part with Kioxia — extended into a second session, with **SNDK continuing its 14% rally in Friday pre-market and MU/WDC moving higher on stronger memory and storage demand expectations** ([TipRanks, 2026-08-14](https://www.tipranks.com/news/why-are-memory-chip-stocks-sndk-mu-and-wdc-rising-in-pre-market-today-august-14)). A second outlet places **STX advancing ~5% to $922 in the same rally** ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-13](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/13/memory-stocks-stay-strong-with-sandisk-sk-hynix-and-western-digital-leading-the-storage-stack/)).

**Two weeks of context, because the level matters more than the day.** STX has gone **$800.99 (08-10) → $973.44 (08-14), +21.5% in five sessions**. WDC has gone **$434.30 (08-07) → $508.80, +17.2% in five sessions**, having first fallen from $519.17 on 08-05. MU has gone **$861.00 (08-10) → $971.66, +12.9%**. **These are not drifting positions; they are a vertical move in the book's two largest holdings, and the book's day-to-day variance is now effectively a bet on NAND/HDD pricing.**

**3b. AMAT: BEAT, RAISED, FELL 5.12% — AND THE SEMICAP COMPLEX FELL WITH IT.**

AMAT closed **$534.54 → $507.18, −5.12%**, costing **−$7,068.75** across **56 sleeves** holding **$131,036 (1.69% of held value)**. This is the single largest dollar loser in the book today, and it lands exactly where this morning's entry said it would (−4.94% pre-market at $508.11; the close was $507.18).

The print itself was strong: **revenue $9.12B, +25% y/y, ahead of ~$8.99B consensus; non-GAAP EPS a record $3.50 vs $3.40 expected; FQ4 guidance ~$10.25B revenue and $4.02 adjusted EPS, both above consensus** ([Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-14](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/applied-materials-shares-fall-strong-102943769.html)). Three reasons are given for the fall, and they are consistent across sources: **elevated valuation after the YTD rally**, **China down to ~28% of sales from ~35% a year earlier**, and **"sell the news" profit-taking** ([Invezz, 2026-08-14](https://invezz.com/news/2026/08/14/applied-materials-beat-wall-street-and-raised-guidance-so-why-did-the-stock-fall-6/); [Proactive Investors, 2026-08-14](https://www.proactiveinvestors.com/companies/news/1097067/applied-materials-shares-drop-despite-earnings-beat-bullish-outlook-1097067.html)).

### 6. Strategic read

**6a. The ladder gradient inverted its own weekly/biweekly sign on the day, and the cumulative monthly slope has now flipped materially positive.**

| Cadence | Day slope (pp/wt) | r | Cumulative slope | r | Spread | Leader | Laggard |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Monthly | **+0.0183** | +0.950 | **+0.0239** | +0.471 | 5.37pp | w6040 (+9.26%) | w2575 (+3.88%) |
| Weekly | **+0.0186** | +0.937 | **−0.0254** | −0.580 | 4.92pp | w1585_wk (+6.33%) | w7030_wk (+1.42%) |
| Biweekly | **+0.0169** | +0.922 | **−0.0927** | −0.871 | 10.43pp | w0595_2wk (+8.59%) | w8020_2wk (−1.84%) |

**Read the day slopes as a concentration measurement, not a factor measurement.** All three cadences produce nearly identical slopes (+0.017 to +0.019) at r above +0.92 — the tightest three-way agreement recorded in this journal. That is not three independent experiments agreeing; **it is one fact: high-residual rungs hold more MU/STX/WDC, memory rose 2–6%, and every rung's day return is a linear function of its memory weight.** Record CW's standing warning applies — adjacent rungs share 74–94% of their names, and w05 vs w95 share 4 of ~47.

**The cumulative movement is the part worth watching.** Monthly's cumulative slope has gone **+0.0045 (yesterday) → +0.0239 (today)**, a 5× move in one session, and its r has climbed from +0.105 to +0.471. Weekly's has gone **−0.0446 → −0.0254**, nearly halved. **Two of three cadences now point in opposite directions on which end of the ladder leads, and the monthly cadence — the one with the fewest trading events and therefore the least turnover noise — has switched sides in under a week.** That is not a finding; it is evidence the gradient is not yet measuring anything stable. Biweekly's −0.0927 at r −0.871 remains the strongest signal in the set, and it is the cadence record CW identified as having a **22-day schedule gap** in July.

**6b. Do the current sleeves have structural edge? The 07-06 cohort still says no, but by less than yesterday.**

| Sleeve | Since 07-06 inception | vs SPY_0701 (+3.34%) | vs QQQ_0706 (+1.14%) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| residual_roa_6535_0701 | **+0.38%** | −2.96pp | −0.76pp |
| mom_roa_6535_0701 | −0.04% | −3.38pp | −1.18pp |
| mom_v1_0701 | −1.47% | −4.81pp | −2.61pp |
| mom_v2_0701 | −2.83% | −6.17pp | −3.97pp |
| sector_top4_full (ETF, May cohort) | **+8.14%** | vs SPY_paper +7.73% → **+0.41pp** | — |

**Four of four factor sleeves lose to both index controls over the cohort's entire clean live history.** Every one gained today (+0.64% to +1.56%) while both controls fell, so the gaps closed by 0.8–1.7pp in a single session — but the sign has not changed for any of them in six weeks. **The only systematic sleeve beating its own index control is the ETF one (`sector_top4_full_paper`, +0.41pp over SPY).**

**What today's data actually supports, stated carefully.** The four factor sleeves outperformed on a day when their common exposure — memory/storage semiconductors — rose hard and the index fell. That is a *beta to a theme*, not alpha. The honest decomposition is available and unflattering: **the book's three largest positive contributors are three tickers held in 60–66 of 76 sleeves.** When 60+ of 76 sleeves hold the same name, the "76-sleeve experiment" has far fewer independent observations than its count suggests — the same criticism record CW made of the 19 ladder rungs, one level up.

**6c. Is any new long-term-viable sleeve concept supported by today's data? Two candidates, one weak, one worth a prereg.**

**Candidate A — "beat-and-raise fade," WEAK, do not build.** Today produced a fourth, fifth and sixth instance of the week's pattern: **AMAT** (beat, raised, −5.12%), **CRMD** (beat, guide maintained, −7.37%), **EDRY** (114% EPS beat, −5.36%), against **AAOI** (beat, raised, **+15.53%**). Four data points inside one week, one of which goes hard the other way. **This is a week-long regime observation with n≈6 and an obvious confound — every one of these names had already run into its print.** It is also structurally hostile to this platform: it requires *event-timed* entries, and every sleeve here rebalances monthly-or-slower on close prices. **Do not build it. Record it and see whether it survives September.**

**Candidate B — a "one-signal-per-sleeve" concentration control, WORTH A PREREG.** Today's clearest structural fact is not about factors, it is about overlap: **three tickers produced 95.7% of the book's net P&L, and each is held by 60–66 of 76 sleeves.** The 07-06 cohort's four sleeves move together because they hold the same names, and the ladder's 19 rungs move together for the same reason. **The measurable question is whether a cap on cross-sleeve name overlap changes any conclusion the platform has drawn** — i.e. re-run the existing held-out windows with a constraint that no name may exceed X% of aggregate book weight, and see whether the residual/momentum ranking survives. This is a **backtest question, answerable on existing data, requiring no new sleeve and no new capital**, and it directly attacks the "76 sleeves, far fewer independent observations" problem that record CW raised and that today's P&L concentration reasserted. **Recommended as a research task, not a deployment.**

**No recommendation is made on either. Both are logged for the record.**

Friday's entry stated that after the record-DD rebuild "nothing in the system will ever raise it again." That claim is **wrong** and should not be repeated. Check (b2) is *never failed*, which is not the same as *never reported* — it is printed in the per-sleeve info line on every run. Parsing the 08-16 20:30 block:

```

```

**The cause is single and exact: TER.** 08-14 was marked on Saturday morning while TER still carried forward at **$410.52**; TER's real 08-14 close of **$418.79** arrived afterwards. Replicating `verify_run`'s own (b2) arithmetic against the live DB reproduces each figure to the cent — `residual_w5050_paper` holds **6.1504 TER shares**, and 6.1504 × ($418.79 − $410.52) = **+$50.86**. The 27 affected sleeves are exactly the 27 TER holders that the 08-14 anomaly scan listed as carry-forwards.

This is textbook record-CK.4 behaviour — `daily_price_refresh` revises a rolling 30-day window by design — and treating it as informational is defensible. **The correction is only to the claim that it disappears from view.** It does not.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**3a. Technology (25.53% of held value) — memory is in a third consecutive session of leadership, with a dated pricing catalyst on top of the 08-13 event.**

The 08-13 SanDisk Investor Day remains the anchor: an FY2028–FY2030 framework of mid-to-high-teens revenue growth, ~80% non-GAAP gross margins and ~50% adjusted FCF margins, plus a jointly-unveiled ninth-generation 2-terabit QLC 3D NAND part with Kioxia. **The Jackson Hole / rebalance adjacency deserves explicit statement.** A first-ever keynote from a chair who has publicly declined to be constrained by market pricing lands **one trading day before** the monthly rebalance recomputes 12-1 momentum across ~5,150 names. If 08-28 produces a sharp regime move, the 09-01 book will be selected on a one-day-old ranking that may already be stale. That is a structural feature of monthly rebalancing, not a bug — but it is a knowable, dated exposure.

**Data-integrity flags carried forward.**

### 6. Strategic insights

**6a. The ladder gradient — pre-market agrees across cadences, cumulative does not.**

Pre-market day moves, measured off a **repriced 08-14 base** so the TER drift documented in §0c cannot contaminate the fit:

```
monthly    slope +0.0029 pp/wt   r +0.813   spread 0.36pp   leader w90 +0.614%
weekly     slope +0.0023 pp/wt   r +0.620   spread 0.37pp   leader w50 +0.629%
biweekly   slope +0.0033 pp/wt   r +0.798   spread 0.43pp   leader w90 +0.682%
```

All three positive, all three tight. **This is a memory-concentration artefact, not a factor result** — the high-residual rungs hold more MU/STX/WDC, so on a memory-led morning they lead mechanically. Record CW's standing warning applies in full: the 19 rungs are **not 19 observations** (adjacent-rung Jaccard 0.74–0.94; w05 vs w95 shares 4 names of ~48), so **r must never be read as significance**.

Cumulative from inception, unchanged from Friday:

```
monthly    +0.0239 pp/wt   r +0.471   spread  5.37pp   leader w6040     +9.26%
weekly     -0.0254 pp/wt   r -0.580   spread  4.92pp   leader w1585_wk  +6.34%
biweekly   -0.0927 pp/wt   r -0.871   spread 10.43pp   leader w0595_2wk +8.60%
```

**Monthly slopes positive; weekly and biweekly slope negative.** Under record CW's decomposition — the entire cumulative gradient is 05-01 stock selection, and rebalancing contributed +2.20pp monthly / ~0 weekly / −0.71pp biweekly, all within one standard error of zero — **this disagreement is exactly what noise looks like**, not evidence that cadence interacts with weight. The honest statement is that after 15 weeks the three cadences remain statistically indistinguishable, and the ladder's only durable output is still a sizing number: **roughly 0.10–0.14pp of return per weight point per adverse month.**

**6b. The finding that matters most: the 07-06 cohort is 4-for-4 below both its own index controls, and has been for its entire clean live history.**

| Sleeve | Close | Pre-market | vs SPY control | vs QQQ control |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `spy_benchmark_0701_paper` | +3.34% | +3.45% | — | — |
| `qqq_benchmark_0706_paper` | +1.14% | +1.55% | — | — |
| `residual_roa_6535_0701_paper` | +0.38% | +0.95% | **−2.96pp** | **−0.76pp** |
| `mom_roa_6535_0701_paper` | −0.02% | +0.62% | **−3.36pp** | **−1.16pp** |
| `mom_v1_0701_paper` | −1.46% | −1.14% | **−4.80pp** | **−2.60pp** |
| `mom_v2_0701_paper` | −2.83% | −2.24% | **−6.17pp** | **−3.97pp** |

**Thirty marked sessions, four systematic sleeves, two index controls, zero wins.** This holds on the close and on pre-market. The 07-06 cohort exists precisely because it is the cleanest forward test in the project — fresh $100k on audited data, no re-inception, no replay seeding, no KLAC contamination — and it is saying that on this sample the momentum and residual-momentum factors have delivered **negative alpha against a passive index**.

**What this does and does not establish.** It does **not** invalidate the strategies: 30 sessions is a tiny sample, the held-out backtests that justified deployment covered 2.4 years, and July's factor drawdown (`spy_benchmark_paper` +0.03% while `mom_v1/v2/mom_roa_6535` lost ~23.5%) is a single adverse regime that any momentum book would suffer. It **does** establish that the cohort's entire live history to date is a losing one against the honest benchmark, and that the continuous May family tells the same story: **`residual_roa_6535_paper` +5.78% against `spy_benchmark_paper` +7.73% and `qqq_benchmark_paper` +8.44%** — the champion sleeve losing to both indices — while `mom_v1_paper` and `mom_v2_paper` sit at **−8.46% and −8.54%**.

**The one systematic sleeve that beats an index is the ETF one.** `sector_top4_full_paper` at **+8.14%** edges `spy_benchmark_paper` (+7.73%) and trails `qqq_benchmark_paper` (+8.44%). That is a real pattern worth naming: **the sleeve operating on 11 liquid sector ETFs is the only systematic construction in the book keeping pace with passive**, while every single-stock momentum variant is behind. Its held-out backtest CAGR (+17.59%) was the *lowest* of the five strategies, and it is the only one delivering.

**6c. Does any of today's data support a new long-term-viable sleeve concept? A qualified no, with one observation worth pre-registering.**

The honest answer is that **today's data supports no new sleeve**, and saying otherwise would be fitting a concept to one morning's tape. Three candidate readings and why each fails the bar:

- **"Memory/storage momentum is a sleeve."** It is not — it is the current expression of the momentum factor the book already runs. MU, STX and WDC are in the book *because* the existing factors selected them. A dedicated memory sleeve would be a single-industry concentration bet dressed as a strategy, and the project has already closed the universe-restriction family (record: top-500/1000 by market cap, survivorship-biased and in-sample losers).
- **"Fade the beat-and-sell."** The week produced five beat-and-raise sell-offs (Cisco, Coherent, SanDisk's initial move, AMAT, CRMD). This is a real, repeated, dated observation. But it is **five events in one week inside one earnings season**, it is a post-earnings-announcement-drift variant, and **PEAD is already on the ruled-out list** (record: "Factor combos / sleeves (dilution/correlation) — quality, low-vol, XBRL, **PEAD**, accruals"). Re-testing it would need a pre-registered hypothesis and a proper in-sample/held-out split, not a week of anecdotes.
- **"The ETF sleeve is the one that works — do more of it."** This is the observation with actual support, and it is **the only one worth pre-registering**. `sector_top4_full_paper` is the sole systematic sleeve matching passive, it has the lowest held-out backtest CAGR of the five, and it carries the smallest maximum drawdown (−16.2% held-out, vs −30.4% to −34.8% for the single-stock variants). The mechanism is plausible and testable: **ETF-level momentum averages away the idiosyncratic blow-ups that dominate single-stock momentum's drawdowns**, at the cost of upside tail. If that is true, it should show up as a *lower* live return dispersion and a *higher* live Sharpe, not merely a higher NAV.

**The falsifiable version, stated now so it cannot be fitted later:** if ETF-level momentum's live edge is the drawdown-averaging mechanism rather than luck, then over the next 60 trading sessions `sector_top4_full_paper` should show a **lower daily return standard deviation** than `residual_roa_6535_paper` while maintaining a **NAV within ±2pp of `spy_benchmark_paper`**. It currently satisfies the second condition (+8.14% vs +7.73%, a +0.41pp gap). The first is measurable from `paper_nav` today and requires no new code. **If the volatility condition fails, the ETF sleeve's lead is concentration luck and should be reported as such.**

**6d. What today's data most changes: the LLM stock overlay's failure mode is now specific enough to test.**

Section 4a established that the veto has been wrong on all six names it acted on this cycle. What is new today is that the *rationales* are now checkable against outcomes, and they share a signature: **every veto cited recent price weakness relative to moving averages** — MU "below 5/20/50 EMAs", VICR "price 213 vs 50DMA 283", BE "below 50DMA", XLK "below 50DMA, RSI43 fading". Every one of those names then mean-reverted upward.

**That converts a vague "the overlay is losing" into a testable claim: the overlay is functioning as a short-horizon trend filter, and short-horizon trend filters on monthly-rebalanced momentum are already on this project's ruled-out list** (record: "Timing/regime gating — SPY 200-DMA filter"; and record BU closed the entire preemptive-overlay family, trend-200DMA "worse than nothing"). If that identification is right, the overlay's failure is not bad luck on four names — it is the rediscovery of a known-dead effect through a different mechanism.

**This is a hypothesis, not a conclusion, on n=6 decisions.** It is recorded here so the kill-switch review at 30 picks can test it directly rather than re-deriving it: **tag each logged decision by whether its rationale cited a moving-average or RSI condition, and check whether that subset underperforms the rest.** The data to do so already exists in `llm_overlay_log.rationale` and `sector_overlay_log.rationale`.

**This is worth stating plainly because it is a new shape.** Every prior entry in this journal has been able to say "all 76 sleeves are marked" or "none are." **0c. Only six held tickers lacked an 08-17 close, and the ladder rebalance traded through two of them.**

The 08-17 anomaly scan, `var/anomaly_report.log`:

```
=== 2026-08-17 17:17 | anomaly scan  close=2026-08-17  prior=2026-08-14  held=201 cache_new=4143 ===
  NOCLOSE TWST  ·  NOCLOSE TXG  ·  NOCLOSE TYRA  ·  NOCLOSE V  ·  NOCLOSE VECO  ·  NOCLOSE VLO
ANOMALIES: 6 flagged.
```

Zero price-move anomalies — **no CFNB, no ghost of any kind.** All six no-closes are alphabetically contiguous (TWST → VLO), the tail-of-alphabet publication lag this journal has logged repeatedly.

The consequential part is the interaction with the 20:30 ladder. Because the rebalance ran while those six were still unpublished, **positions in V and VLO were sold at carried-forward 08-14 prices**:

```
2026-08-17 20:31:39,992 INFO paper_rebalance:   SELL  V  qty=3.21  fill=$363.97  pnl=$-6.05
```

V's stored 08-14 close is **$364.1500**; $364.15 less the 5 bp sell-side half-spread is **$363.968** — the fill is exactly the carried-forward price, not an 08-17 price. Counting across the run: **10 sleeves sold VLO and 8 sold V on stale marks**, 18 sells in total. Every other sell and all 263 buys priced off a real 08-17 close.

This is **not a bug and not a fabrication** — the simulator did what it is specified to do with the data it had. It is a *cadence-vs-coverage collision*: an 8:30pm rebalance on a day whose cache is only ~80% published will always trade some names on yesterday's price. It is worth recording as a dated, quantified instance because the same collision at a **monthly** rebalance would move far more capital than 18 sells.

Confirmed directly against `price_cache`: **zero rows exist for OBNK between 2026-06-03 and 2026-07-07.** Its surrounding history is present (2026-05-20 $1.2585, 2026-05-28 $1.1221, 2026-06-01 $1.1422).

**Why this matters:** this is the defect class that produced the largest data disaster in the project's record. On 2026-06-13 roughly 815 tickers were found to have multi-year holes, causing 12-1 momentum to be measured against a stale bar and phantom-ranking names into ~half of every momentum sleeve. A 23-day hole is far smaller than a multi-year one and lands well inside the 12-1 lookback rather than at its anchor, so the distortion is bounded — but the mechanism is identical.

**The exposure is bounded and dated:** OBNK is held by **zero sleeves**, so live P&L impact is **$0.00**. It became newly rankable when the audit window rolled forward one day. The risk is entirely forward: **the 09-01 monthly rebalance ranks the full universe**, and a ticker whose trailing-year series is 75% complete can rank on a distorted score. This is a *report*, not a repair — per the standing rule, data that looks wrong gets recorded and the fix is Evan's call.

### 2. Overnight and pre-market moves

**Method and its limits.** 25 quotes were fetched individually from stockanalysis.com between **07:27 and 08:14 ET on 2026-08-18**. Every one was reconciled by adding back the quoted dollar change: **all 25 recover the stored 2026-08-17 close exactly, to 0.00 bp.** These are pre-market indications on thin volume, not fills, and the market has not opened — there is no intraday data for 2026-08-18.

**One methodological caveat, new today.** The separately-displayed "Previous Close" *label* on stockanalysis.com was **one session stale** on all 25 pages, showing the 08-14 close rather than 08-17 (MU $971.66, STX $973.44, WDC $508.80, AMAT $507.18, LRCX $332.36, KLAC $203.49, TER $418.79, VICR $234.74, FIX $1,774.06, AAPL $305.93, SPY $776.34). The **dollar-change base was correct at 08-17 in every case.** Reading the label instead of the change would have produced badly wrong percentages — for MU, −0.40% instead of −4.34%. Recorded so a future run does not trust the wrong field.

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**3a. The memory reversal has a stated cause, and it is not memory.**

Micron gained **4.1%** Monday, SanDisk **8.9%**, SK Hynix ADRs **~3%**, capping a run in which SanDisk had risen roughly **35% over the five sessions through Friday**. Tuesday pre-market reversed it: **Micron indicated ~6% lower, SanDisk −5.3%, SK Hynix ADRs −5.1%.**

Invezz is explicit that no fundamental news drove it: the retreat "came without an obvious overnight deterioration in memory demand," and the attribution is to **Nasdaq-100 futures −1.2%** and the **30-year Treasury yield at ~5.33%, its highest in nearly two decades**, creating "a tougher backdrop for richly valued technology stocks" — described as "simple profit-taking, not bad news" ([Invezz, 2026-08-18](https://invezz.com/sg/news/2026/08/18/micron-down-6percent-sk-hynix-and-sandisk-5percent-why-is-memory-trade-crashing/)).

**This journal should treat that attribution as provisional.** Eight searches produced no dated ticker-specific catalyst — no downgrade, no guidance cut, no supply announcement timestamped 2026-08-17 or 2026-08-18. Several search results that *appeared* to describe today were verified and rejected on date: a Yahoo Finance piece describing "Micron dropped 5.1% in premarket to $929" carries a publication date of **2026-07-13**, and the Michael Burry put position it cites was established **2026-07-01**. Those are July facts and are **not** today's driver. **Reported as missing rather than filled in.**

The one genuinely dated sell-side data point running against memory is older than today and already known: Citigroup's **Atif Malik cut his MU target to $1,150 from $1,400 on 2026-08-10** while maintaining Buy, arguing memory pricing momentum slows over the next year with prices peaking in Q2 of next year, and naming rising Chinese memory capacity as the biggest long-term risk ([Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-10](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/micron-memory-boom-heading-peak-100028273.html)). Running the other way, Deutsche Bank's Melissa Weathers expects DRAM supply tight **through 2027 and into 2028** on AI-driven HBM demand.

Context for the level: MU's Monday close of **$1,011.75** is a **+240% year-to-date** gain, and the stock carries **41 buy ratings and 0 sells**, with Q3 EPS of **$25.11 against a $20.20 estimate (+24.31%)** ([stockanalysis.com MU](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/mu/); [Yahoo Finance MU](https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/MU/)). **A 4% overnight drawdown on a name up 240% YTD is noise inside the position, not a thesis break — but the book holds it across 60 sleeves and it is the single largest line.**

**3b. Storage: the SanDisk investor-day catalyst is intact and the pricing news still runs positive.**

The dated fundamentals behind last week's move have not reversed. **SanDisk announced a 10% NAND price hike and Micron has paused NAND and DRAM quotes**, signaling sharper increases; **spot DDR4 1Gx8 3200MT/s rose 3.31% in a week, $4.896 → $5.058**. SanDisk has signed **five multi-year supply agreements, three with minimum revenue commitments totalling $42 billion**, at a floor of roughly **$0.29/GB**, broadly in line with Q2-2026 average selling prices.

WDC's own positioning is unchanged: trading about **49% above its 200-day SMA of $349.72** and **7.8% above its 100-day SMA of $483.28**, with Seagate and Western Digital operating as "a tight duopoly in the high-capacity HDD market" ([Benzinga, 2026-08-17](https://www.benzinga.com/trading-ideas/movers/26/08/61245397/western-digital-stock-is-gaining-monday-whats-going-on-2)).

**The honest read: the fundamental story is unchanged and the price is 5% lower. That is what profit-taking looks like, and it is also what the first leg of a de-rating looks like. There is no way to tell them apart today, and this journal should not pretend otherwise.**

**3c. Healthcare — 24.61% of the book — is quietly holding.**

The book's second-largest sector is doing what the rotation would predict. **JNJ +0.90% pre-market** and **XLV +0.61%** are among the seven green lines. On Monday's close the healthcare complex was broadly firm: **NHC +2.06%, EXEL +2.11%, PTCT +1.65%, TGTX +1.11%, KRYS +1.04%, INDV +0.18%**, against **AUPH −1.16%**. Pre-market PTCT is **−0.92%**; KRYS and EXEL have no indication.

Healthcare is 63 distinct names and **no single one exceeds 1.25% of the book**, so this sector behaves as a diversified block rather than a concentrated bet — the structural opposite of the technology weight. **On a rates-up day that distinction is the main reason the book's uncovered 61% is very likely doing better than its covered 39%.**

**3d. The consumer read arrived this morning and it is a beat with a bad sentence in it.**

Home Depot's Q2 FY2026: **net income $4.77B ($4.79/share)** vs $4.55B ($4.58) a year earlier, **adjusted EPS $4.92**, **sales $47.9B, +5.7%**, full-year guidance reaffirmed, and the stock **+1% pre-bell** ([CNBC, 2026-08-18](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/home-depot-hd-q2-2026-earnings.html); [StockTitan](https://www.stocktitan.net/news/HD/the-home-depot-announces-second-quarter-fiscal-2026-results-w7n9jy4uowii.html)).

The commentary is the part that matters. CFO **Richard McPhail** said the company continues to operate in **"frozen housing market conditions."** CEO **Ted Decker** was blunt that the expected second-half pickup is **"solely driven by a return to normal storm activity,"** not a rebound in underlying demand. Separately, the company confirmed on **2026-08-12** that Decker had begun a **temporary medical leave**, with day-to-day oversight handed to a two-executive interim arrangement.

**Direct portfolio relevance:** the book holds no HD, but it holds **$586,118.60 of Industrials (7.47%)** and **$379,735.68 of Consumer Cyclical (4.84%)**, and **FIX (Comfort Systems, $82,558.82, 39 sleeves)** is a mechanical/HVAC contractor levered to construction activity. FIX rose **+6.04%** Monday and is **−2.98%** pre-market. A "frozen housing market" read from the country's largest home-improvement retailer is a **negative datapoint for that whole block**, and it lands the same morning housing starts print.

**3e. Macro: three things moved at once, and all three point the same way.**

**Rates.** The 30-year Treasury **closed 5.31% on 2026-08-17 — its first close above 5.30% since June 2007** — and the 10-year rose from **4.695% to 4.725%** ([Eurasia Business News, 2026-08-18](https://eurasiabusinessnews.com/2026/08/18/stock-market-today-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-fall-oil-price-above-88/)). Tuesday morning the 30Y is quoted at **5.31%** and the 10Y at **4.72%** ([Yahoo Finance live, 2026-08-18](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-august-18-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-080822735.html)); CNBC separately reports the 10Y at **4.73%**, up on US–Iran tension and year-ahead inflation expectations **above 4% for a fifth consecutive month** ([CNBC, 2026-08-18](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/treasury-yields-.html)).

**Oil and geopolitics.** The 60-day US–Iran memorandum signed in June **expired Monday 2026-08-17**, and **Trump rejected extending it** absent a broader peace agreement ([Bloomberg, 2026-08-18](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-18/us-stock-index-futures-drop-as-bond-yields-oil-prices-rise)). Oil rose **~3% on Monday's session** to WTI above **$83** and Brent above **$88**; Tuesday morning **Brent is $91 and WTI $84–85** after Trump said he intends to inflict more economic pain on Iran. Compounding it: **renewed fighting in Lebanon, attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, and shipping activity through the Strait slowing significantly over the weekend**; Iranian Foreign Minister **Abbas Araqchi** said Tehran has not decided whether to resume talks ([TradingEconomics Brent](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil)).

**The Fed.** The **07-28/29 FOMC held 3.50–3.75% on a 9–3 vote**, with **Beth Hammack (Cleveland), Neel Kashkari (Minneapolis) and Lorie Logan (Dallas) all dissenting in favor of a HIKE — the most dissents since September 2016** ([CNBC Fed recap, 2026-07-29](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html)). BMO Capital Markets read it as "a Committee with vocal hawks, but the majority is siding with Warsh to keep rates stable until at least September." **The minutes release is Wednesday 2026-08-19** ([Federal Reserve August 2026 calendar](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/2026-august.htm); [InteractiveCrypto](https://www.interactivecrypto.com/fomc-minutes-on-august-19-set-to-clarify-fed-s-rate-path-amid-mixed-economic-signals-aug-2026)).

**Monday's tape.** Dow **53,459.78 (−0.5%)**, S&P 500 **7,745.06 (−0.5%)**, Nasdaq Composite **26,644.91 (−0.3%)**. Industrials led sector gainers; Communication Services and Utilities lagged. Gold rose **0.80% to $4,472.90** on the futures; spot gold near **$4,388.62**, silver around **$65.19** ([Motley Fool, 2026-08-17](https://www.fool.com/coverage/stock-market-today/2026/08/17/stock-market-today-aug-17-markets-inch-lower-and-treasury-yields-rise-as-investors-wait-for-retail-earnings/); [Washington Post, 2026-08-17](https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/2026/08/17/wall-street-stocks-dow-nasdaq/226262fa-9a7c-11f1-9cc4-2dc9b46e2d5c_story.html)).

**Tuesday's futures at ~07:01 CDT:** S&P 500 **−0.4%**, Dow **flat**, Nasdaq-100 **−1.1%**. Benzinga's prediction-market contract on "S&P 500 up or down on August 18" showed a **27% chance of a higher open** ([Benzinga, 2026-08-18](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/prediction-markets/26/08/61265010/stock-market-will-sp-500-open-up-or-down-today-18)).

**Today's data calendar** ([XTB macro calendar, 2026-08-18](https://www.xtb.com/en/market-analysis/macro-calendar-us-housing-market-in-the-spotlight-of-investors-18-08-2026); [forex.tradingcharts economic calendar, 2026-08-18](https://forex.tradingcharts.com/economic_calendar/2026-08-18.html?code=USD)):

**The three forces stack rather than offset.** Higher long rates compress the multiple on long-duration growth; higher oil raises the inflation path that keeps rates high; and a Committee with three hawkish dissenters removes the cushion that would normally soften both. **Every one of those pushes against a 25.21% technology weight and toward the 6.29% energy weight.** The pre-market table in §2 is that stack expressed in dollars.

**Monday was the first session since 2026-08-03 on which the control finished ahead of the cash treatment.** MU's close at $1,011.75 lifted the control to +0.79% against the treatment's flat $100,000 — a 3.20pp deficit on Friday erased entirely in two sessions. Pre-market it reversed again: the treatment leads by **3.58pp**.

**The veto has flipped sign twice inside 24 hours, and that is the finding.** It is the clearest demonstration yet that at n=1 name and 11 trading days, this experiment is measuring a single stock's volatility, not the LLM's judgment. The pre-registered comparison — the treatment against MU alone — remains the honest scoreboard, and on that basis the treatment is **behind by 16.67%** this cycle on pre-market and was **behind 21.97%** at Monday's close.

That earnings event passed nearly two weeks ago; the name's round trip back below the veto price is a consequence of today's macro tape, not evidence the reasoning worked. **Recorded as a data point, not a vindication.**

**The XLK veto's cumulative cost narrowed for the first time.** XLK closed **$178.04** on the day it was vetoed (2026-08-03) and reached **$190.32** Monday — **+6.90% against the veto**. Pre-market at **$187.21** that gap is **+5.15%**, a **1.75pp** narrowing in one overnight session. It remains a large, clearly-losing call: the LLM's rationale cited "rotation OUT of tech into cyclicals" and "hawkish Fed (~63% Sept-hike odds)" pressuring long-duration growth. **Today is the first session where that stated reasoning has actually been paid.** One session does not redeem eleven of being wrong, but it is the first evidence the mechanism is real rather than post-hoc.

### 6. Strategic insights — structural edge

**6a. The ladder gradient inverted overnight, and that is the most informative thing in this entry.**

The residual ladder holds 19 weight rungs (5/95 through 95/05, residual-momentum vs ROA) at three cadences. Pre-market slope, measured off the 08-17 basis:

| Cadence | Slope (pp per weight point) | r | n |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Monthly | **+0.0005** | +0.092 | 19 |
| Weekly | **+0.0033** | +0.457 | 19 |
| Biweekly | **+0.0027** | +0.412 | 19 |

All three are **positive** — higher residual-momentum weight is being hurt *less* pre-market — and on the monthly rungs the relationship is essentially zero. Compare Monday's realized session on the marked ladder sleeves, where the gradient was strongly positive and the dispersion was large: the weekly/biweekly rungs ran from **w0595 −0.52%** to **w6040 +1.81%**, a **2.33pp spread across the weight axis in one session**.

**The interpretation is not "residual momentum works."** It is that the ladder's weight axis is currently acting as a proxy for semiconductor exposure — the high-residual rungs hold more of the memory complex, so they won big on 08-17 and would be expected to lose big on 08-18. That the pre-market slope is *positive* rather than negative therefore cuts against the simple story and suggests the high-residual rungs' overnight losses are being offset elsewhere in their books. **Either way, a factor axis whose sign is set by one sector's two-day round trip is not measuring the factor.**

Cumulatively the three cadences still disagree, and the disagreement has persisted for weeks:

| Cadence | Slope | r | Spread | Leader |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Monthly (08-14 mark) | **+0.0239** | +0.471 | 5.37pp | w6040 **+9.26%** |
| Weekly (08-17 mark) | **−0.0122** | −0.292 | 4.35pp | w5050 **+7.06%** |
| Biweekly (08-17 mark) | **−0.0787** | −0.788 | 8.72pp | w0595 **+8.04%** |

The weekly slope moved from **−0.0254 (r −0.580)** on Friday to **−0.0122 (r −0.292)** after last night's rebalance — a halving of both slope and correlation in a single rebalance. **The monthly cadence says more residual momentum is better; the biweekly says the opposite at r −0.788.** Two of three point one way. After roughly ten weeks of live data across 57 ladder sleeves, **the honest conclusion is that the weight axis is not yet separable from cadence and sector noise**, and no rung should be promoted on this evidence.

**6b. The 07-06 cohort: still 0-for-4 against SPY, but a sleeve cleared QQQ for the first time.**

On the 08-17 indicative basis, all six from a common $100,000 inception:

| Sleeve | 08-17 indicative | vs $100k | Pre-market | vs $100k |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `mom_roa_6535_0701` | $102,364.44 | **+2.36%** | $101,526.45 | **+1.53%** |
| `residual_roa_6535_0701` | $101,893.87 | **+1.89%** | $100,937.39 | +0.94% |
| `mom_v1_0701` | $100,104.39 | +0.10% | $99,689.20 | −0.31% |
| `mom_v2_0701` | $99,181.78 | −0.82% | $98,528.07 | −1.47% |
| `spy_benchmark_0701` | $102,847.13 | **+2.85%** | $102,395.91 | **+2.40%** |
| `qqq_benchmark_0706` | $100,975.34 | +0.98% | $99,806.31 | −0.19% |

**`mom_roa_6535_0701` at +2.36% has passed `qqq_benchmark_0706` at +0.98% — the first time any 07-06 cohort sleeve has cleared either of its own controls since inception.** On pre-market, **two of four** (mom_roa and residual_roa) sit above QQQ.

Against SPY the record is unbroken: **0-for-4 across 31 marked sessions**, on both the close and pre-market. The gap narrowed materially — `mom_roa_6535_0701` is now **0.49pp** behind SPY where it was 3.36pp behind on Friday — but narrowing is not clearing.

**What this is and is not evidence of.** Thirty-one sessions is not a validation window. Every one of Monday's gains and today's losses traces to the same eight semiconductor names, which means the cohort's recent trajectory measures one sector's two-day round trip, not the factor. **The structural claim this journal has repeated for weeks — that the cohort has not demonstrated edge over its own passive controls — remains true, and one sleeve clearing the weaker of two controls on a single favorable session does not change it.** The correct posture is to keep marking and keep reporting.

**6c. Does today's data support any new long-term-viable sleeve concept?**

Three observations from today are structurally interesting. None is a recommendation, and none is close to deployable.

**(i) The book has an unmeasured, unintended factor: rate duration.** Today's pre-market is a near-perfect sort on duration — semiconductors −4 to −6%, tobacco/pharma/energy/payments +0.4 to +1.1% — driven by a 30-year yield at a 19-year high rather than by anything company-specific. The book's exposure to that sort is large (25.21% technology) and entirely incidental: no sleeve in the roster measures or targets rate sensitivity. **A duration diagnostic — regressing each sleeve's daily return on the daily change in the 10Y or 30Y and reporting the beta — would be a measurement, not a strategy, and it is cheap.** It would answer whether the residual-momentum construction is systematically long duration or whether today is coincidence. That is a legitimate research question with a clean falsifiable answer.

**Against it:** the project has already closed the entire risk-overlay family (record BU, 2026-07-14 — preemptive trend and vol-target overlays both failed on clean data against both champions). A duration overlay is the same shape of idea and should be expected to fail the same way. **The distinction worth preserving is measurement versus overlay: measuring the exposure is honest bookkeeping; hedging it is a new overlay, and the prior says it will not survive held-out validation.**

**(ii) The overlay experiment's signal-to-noise problem is now quantified and it is bad.** The single-name arm's lead flipped sign twice in 24 hours on n=1 name. Over the 08-03 cycle the vetoed basket has read +7.22% (Friday), +10.59% (Monday), +8.01% (today) — a 3.4pp range in three sessions on a decision made fifteen days ago. **At this sample size the experiment cannot distinguish LLM judgment from single-stock variance, and it will not be able to for many more cycles.** The pre-registered kill switch (12 months / 30 picks) was set correctly, and the right action is to run it to that threshold without reading anything into the interim. **Today's honest addition to the record is the measurement of how noisy the interim readings are** — itself useful evidence about how much weight future entries should give them.

**(iii) The cadence-vs-coverage collision is a real, generalizable operational finding.** Last night, 18 of 276 sells priced off a carried-forward close because an 8:30pm rebalance ran against an ~80%-published cache. **The same collision at the 09-01 monthly rebalance would touch far more capital**, and the monthly rebalance runs at ~6:03pm — even earlier in the publication cycle. That is not a strategy idea; it is a specification question worth answering before 09-01: *should a rebalance refuse to trade a name whose current-day close has not published, or is trading on a one-day-stale price acceptable?* `paper_rebalance` already carries a universe-size guard against catastrophic liquidation; a coverage guard would be the same category of protection. **This journal's role is to report the instance, not to design the fix.**

**6d. What today does not support.**

It does not support any conclusion about memory as a theme. The 08-17 rally and the 08-18 reversal have the same names, comparable magnitudes and opposite signs, with **no dated ticker-specific catalyst on either side** — Monday's move was attributed to SanDisk's investor-day read-through, today's to profit-taking and a bond shock. **Two sessions of ±5% on the book's largest concentration, with no fundamental news in either direction, is the definition of noise, and the correct response is to keep the marking honest and change nothing.**

**Read plainly: M3.5's self-heal is now demonstrably two-deep.** The design assumption stated in HANDOFF is that `TradingMorningMTM` "heals a day left pending at 5:15pm." Today it did not — the day needed the *next* evening's `mtm_catchup` to close it. That still worked, and `verify_run` never reported a gap because a below-floor day is PENDING rather than missing. **But the healing latency for a PENDING day is now empirically up to ~24 hours, not ~14.** Nothing is broken; the documented expectation is just narrower than reality.

**0d. THE MAJOR FINDING — DMAA AND UYSC ARE SPACs, AND THIS RETRACTS SIXTEEN SESSIONS OF THIS JOURNAL'S OWN REPORTING.**

Since 2026-08-01 this journal has carried DMAA as an unexplained defect. The language escalated: "no longer plausibly a live mark" (08-14), "an unexplained feed shape" (08-17). **Every one of those statements was wrong about the cause.**

DMAA's stored series, read directly:

```
07-24 10.70 | 07-27 10.70 | 07-28..08-06 10.71 (8 sessions) | 08-07 10.705
08-10..08-14 10.71 (5 sessions) | 08-17 10.72 | 08-18 10.72
```

**DMAA is Drugs Made In America Acquisition Corp., a blank-check (SPAC) company incorporated in 2024, based in Fort Lauderdale, which priced a 20,000,000-unit IPO at $10.00 per unit on 2025-01-27** ([Nasdaq listing](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/dmaa); [SEC Form 8-K, CIK 0002028614](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2028614/000121390025008377/ea022913501ex99-1_drugs.htm)). A pre-deal SPAC's common shares trade at the redemption value of the trust account plus a small premium; the trust accretes at short-rate interest. **A monotonic $0.00–$0.01/day grind just above $10.00 is the correct price of that instrument, not a stale feed.** The 08-17 ladder rebalance exited DMAA, so it is now held by **zero sleeves** and the item is closed — but not for the reason previously given.

**And the ranker replaced it.** Tonight's `check_anomalies` flags exactly one name:

```
2026-08-18 17:17 | anomaly scan  close=2026-08-18  prior=2026-08-17  held=209 cache_new=4345
  NOCLOSE UYSC     no close on 2026-08-18  [HELD residual_w5050_wk_paper, ... 20 sleeves ]
ANOMALIES: 1 flagged for 2026-08-18.
```

**UYSC is UY Scuti Acquisition Corp., a Cayman Islands blank-check company incorporated in 2024, based in New York, which IPO'd 2025-03-31** ([stockanalysis.com](https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/uysc/); [Nasdaq listing](https://www.nasdaq.com/market-activity/stocks/uysc)). It was **bought on 2026-08-17 at $10.845420 into 20 weekly and biweekly ladder sleeves — 4,299 shares, $46,601.16 at the 08-17 close of $10.84.**

Its stored series since 2026-06-15 is 44 sessions long and contains **7 distinct prices**, spanning **$10.67 to $10.85 — a 1.7% total range over two months**:

```
06-15..06-16 10.69 | 06-17..(...) 10.70 | ... | 07-31..08-13 10.78 (10 sessions) | 08-14 10.85 | 08-17 10.84
```

A book-wide scan of every held name's 61-session daily-return standard deviation, threshold 0.30%:

```
UYSC   sd=0.1306%  n_sess=61  range $10.67-$10.85   20 sleeves  $46,601.16
TOTAL flagged $46,601.16
```

**UYSC is the only held name in the entire 209-name book that trips it.** DMAA would have been the second before it was sold.

**Why this matters, stated as a mechanism rather than an alarm.** Residual (idiosyncratic) momentum ranks on the *risk-adjusted* residual of a return regression. A security whose price rises monotonically with near-zero residual variance produces an enormous score by construction — the numerator is small but the denominator is smaller. **A pre-deal SPAC accreting at the risk-free rate is the purest possible instance of that shape.** This is not a bad price; it is a correct price for an instrument that should never have entered a stock universe.

**No existing filter catches it.** `MAX_PRICE_USD = 5000` passes $10.84. `MAX_HIST_RATIO = 100` measures the wrong direction entirely — it screens for *explosive* history, not flat history. `NON_STOCK_TICKERS` (added 2026-06-09) is a hand-maintained exclusion list for warmed ETFs and indices; no SPAC is on it. **This is a SELECTION defect of the same class as the 2026-06-09 ETF contamination, and it is live in 20 sleeves right now.** The economic damage so far is nil — a 1.7% two-month drift is not a loss — but the capital is dead, and the **09-01 rebalance will re-rank on the same signal against the same unfiltered universe.**

This is a finding, not a fix. **Per the standing rule, it is reported, not repaired** — the universe filter is Evan's call.
