OBNK is held by no sleeve, so live P&L impact is zero, but it is rankable and **the 09-01 rebalance is the exposure.**

CFNB's stored series reads **$33.95 on 08-17** and every session 08-10 through 08-17; it has **no 08-18 row yet**, consistent with the 4,345-row partial. The 08-15, 08-16, 08-17 and 08-18 anomaly scans all returned **zero CFNB flags**. Four clean sessions after two ghosts and two silent reversions. The recurrence remains real and unexplained; **both universe filters would still pass a $1,425 print, and 09-01 is still the exposure.**

### 3. Key position analysis

**3a. The semiconductor complex was 81.3% of the net loss on 18.25% of the book.**

Twenty-nine semiconductor, semicap and semi-adjacent names in the held book carried **$1,408,387.41 = 18.25% of held value** and produced **−$108,779.51** against a total net book change of **−$133,816.15**. Against the gross loss of −$181,780.28 they are **59.8%**.

The names: AAOI, AEHR, AMAT, AMD, AMKR, CIEN, COHU, FORM, ICHR, INTC, KLAC, KLIC, LRCX, LSCC, MRVL, MTRN, MU, MXL, NVEC, ONTO, SITM, STX, TER, TTMI, UCTT, VECO, VIAV, VICR, WDC.

**The catalyst is dated and has two legs.**

**Leg one — the WSJ off-balance-sheet analysis, published 2026-08-18.** A Wall Street Journal analysis found that **nine top technology companies carry roughly $3 trillion of off-balance-sheet commitments, mostly AI-related** — approximately **$1.2 trillion in leases for facilities not yet in service** and **$1.9 trillion in purchase commitments for chips, energy and equipment** — against about **$600 billion of trailing capex**. Alphabet disclosed **$811 billion** of purchase and contractual obligations; Meta reported **$347 billion** of future lease commitments, roughly three times its reported debt. Under current accounting, leases that have not commenced are not balance-sheet liabilities, so reported leverage understates the commitment ([TipRanks, 2026-08-18](https://www.tipranks.com/news/big-tech-has-3-trillion-in-ai-commitments-hidden-off-the-balance-sheet); [Crypto Briefing, 2026-08-18](https://cryptobriefing.com/big-tech-3-trillion-off-balance-sheet-ai-commitments/); [Seeking Alpha, 2026-08-18](https://seekingalpha.com/news/4633674-big-tech-companies-have-3t-in-hidden-ai-expenditures--report)). On that report, **SanDisk fell 9.1%, Micron 7.3% and Western Digital 5.3%** ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-18](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/18/wsj-report-sends-memory-stocks-down-sandisk-down-9-micron-down-7-western-digital-down-5/)).

**Leg two — the long end of the curve.** The **30-year Treasury closed near 5.29%, within a basis point or two of a 19-year high, and the 10-year near 4.70%** ([Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-18](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-tuesday-august-18-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-080822735.html)). The mechanism is explicit in the trade press: higher yields raise the discount rate applied to distant earnings, which hits hardest the stocks whose valuations lean most on distant results, and separately raise the financing cost of the fabrication capacity Micron and Western Digital are building ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-18](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/18/micron-technology-falls-5-sandisk-sinks-6-western-digital-drops-7-as-higher-rates-test-the-memory-boom/)).

**Neither leg is a memory-demand event.** The same source notes the uniformity of the decline — Seagate and the Roundhill memory ETF each −6% — as confirming a macro rate reset rather than company-specific news, with **VIX at 14.25** and the S&P down only ~0.5%, i.e. a sector derating rather than systemic stress.

**Semicap equipment fell alongside for the same reason.** KLA was down 6% intraday to $193.46; the group's decline was driven by "investors questioning the AI capital spending cycle that has been powering the sector's year-to-date returns," after Applied Materials, Lam Research, KLA, Teradyne, MKS, Integ and Onto Innovation all roughly **doubled in 2026** ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-18](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/18/applied-materials-rockets-98-in-2026-how-does-amat-compare-to-lam-research-and-kla-as-ai-capex-powers-chip-gear-stocks/)).

**3c. Individual names with a dated, verified catalyst.**

**AEHR −15.36% to $123.25 (−$2,908.32, 6 sleeves)** — the book's worst percentage move. Aehr Test Systems fell on disclosed insider selling: company executives and directors offloaded **109,475 shares valued at $13.8 million** ([MoneyCheck, 2026-08-18](https://moneycheck.com/aehr-test-systems-aehr-stock-plummets-9-amid-13-8m-insider-selling-spree)). **A methodology note worth recording:** that article reports "down 9.1% to $132.37," which is an *intraday* snapshot. ### 6. Strategic insights — does any of this have structural edge?

**6a. Today produced the single cleanest quantitative result in this journal's live record, and it is not flattering: on 2026-08-18, semiconductor weight explained 91% of the cross-sectional variation in sleeve returns.**

Regressing each sleeve's day return on its semiconductor-and-semicap portfolio weight, computed from the position book:

```
All 76 sleeves:                     day% = +0.0011 - 0.09285 x semi_wt%    r = -0.884   R2 = 0.782
                                    (semi weight range 0.0% - 99.9%)

65 diversified sleeves (>=40 pos):  day% = ...     - 0.18365 x semi_wt%    r = -0.956   R2 = 0.914
                                    (semi weight range 10.2% - 45.0%)
```

**The second line is the one that matters**, because it excludes the single-name and ETF-only sleeves that would otherwise be leverage points. Across 65 genuinely diversified 44-to-50-name portfolios spanning a 35-point range of semiconductor weight, **a single sector exposure accounts for 91% of the day's dispersion**, at a slope of **−18 basis points of sleeve return per point of semiconductor weight**.

Measured per sleeve:

| Sleeve | Semi weight | Technology weight | Day % |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `mom_roa_6535_0701_paper` | **44.99%** | **57.43%** | **−6.290%** |
| `mom_roa_6535_paper` | 44.30% | 57.58% | −6.023% |
| `mom_v2_0701_paper` | 34.89% | 47.02% | −5.511% |
| `mom_v2_paper` | 35.30% | 46.75% | −5.229% |
| `mom_v1_0701_paper` | 28.59% | 45.56% | −4.727% |
| `mom_v1_paper` | 28.56% | 45.39% | −4.533% |
| `residual_roa_6535_0701_paper` | **22.34%** | **25.28%** | **−2.359%** |
| `residual_roa_6535_paper` | 22.21% | 25.10% | −2.264% |
| `residual_w9505_paper` | 16.81% | 14.06% | −1.862% |
| `residual_w0595_paper` | 12.26% | 28.07% | −0.376% |

**Say the uncomfortable thing plainly: `mom_roa_6535` is not a diversified quality-momentum portfolio. It is a 45%-semiconductor, 57%-technology sector bet that a factor screen happened to produce, and nothing in its construction stops that from happening.** A top-50 equal-weight book that ends up 45% in one industry has an effective breadth far below 50. **This is the structural explanation for the 07-06 cohort's 0-for-4 record against SPY across 32 sessions** — it is not that momentum stopped working, it is that four sleeves have been making the same undiversified bet and being marked against a diversified index.

**6b. The strongest genuinely positive finding tonight: residual momentum's live drawdown advantage is real, and it comes from exactly where the 2026-06-09 backtest said it would.**

`residual_roa_6535` lost **−2.36%** today; `mom_roa_6535` lost **−6.29%** — **3.93pp of outperformance in a single session**, on sleeves that share a universe, a rebalance cadence and a top-50 construction, and differ only in whether momentum is measured raw or residual to a market factor.

**The 2026-06-09 research entry deployed `residual_roa_6535` specifically on the claim that it "beats mom_v2 on BOTH windows on return+Sharpe+DD" with "much lower DD than champion mom_roa_6535 (−20% vs −30% held-out)."** Today is a live, out-of-sample instance of exactly that claimed property, and the mechanism is now visible and measured: **residualising the momentum signal halves the sector concentration (22.34% semi vs 44.99%), and the drawdown difference follows almost mechanically from that.** All four 07-06 cohort sleeves are still below SPY, so this is a relative claim among losers — but it is the first live confirmation of the specific reason the sleeve was deployed, and it is worth recording as such.

**6c. The ladder gradient is not measuring a factor. It is measuring semiconductor beta, and today proved it by inverting.**

| Cadence | Day slope (pp per weight pt) | r | Cumulative slope | r | Spread | Leader |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Monthly | **−0.0197** | −0.909 | +0.0167 | +0.354 | 5.43pp | `residual_w6040_paper` +8.91% |
| Weekly | **−0.0086** | −0.704 | −0.0211 | −0.484 | 4.79pp | `residual_w1585_wk_paper` +5.79% |
| Biweekly | **−0.0105** | −0.756 | −0.0890 | −0.837 | 9.64pp | `residual_w0595_2wk_paper` +7.72% |

Friday's day slopes were **+0.0183 / +0.0186 / +0.0169 at r +0.950 / +0.937 / +0.922**. Today's are **−0.0197 / −0.0086 / −0.0105 at r −0.909 / −0.704 / −0.756**. **Same 19 rungs, same construction, sign fully reversed in two sessions, with high |r| on both days.**

Record CW already established that the 19 rungs are not 19 independent observations (adjacent-rung Jaccard 0.74–0.94; w05 vs w95 share 4 names of ~48) and warned against quoting r as significance. **Today adds the mechanism: the rungs differ in semiconductor weight, so the "gradient" is a sector-beta gradient sampled once.** A high r on a day when semis move is not information about where the residual-momentum edge lives. **This should be treated as retiring the day-slope statistic entirely** — it can only ever restate the day's sector move.

**Cumulative, the three cadences still disagree in sign** (monthly +0.0167, weekly −0.0211, biweekly −0.0890), which is itself the useful finding: **if the weight gradient carried a real edge, three cadences sampling the same ladder would not point in opposite directions.**

**6d. A new sleeve-hygiene defect, and the first one of the *selection* class since 2026-06-09.**

The SPAC finding in §0d is not a market observation, it is a construction defect, and it belongs here. **The residual-momentum ranker preferentially selects instruments whose returns have near-zero idiosyncratic variance — and a pre-deal SPAC accreting toward trust value is the purest example of that shape available in a US equity universe.** DMAA was held for weeks; UYSC was bought into 20 sleeves on 2026-08-17 for $46,601.16 and is live now.

The damage is small and the mechanism is not: **a signal that rewards low residual variance will keep finding these**, and each one is dead capital occupying a top-50 slot. Three candidate filters, in the order of the project's simplicity ladder — **none implemented, all reported for Evan's decision**:

1. **Cheapest: extend `NON_STOCK_TICKERS`** with the currently-held offenders. Fixes today, fixes nothing structurally, and requires manual maintenance forever.
2. **A minimum-realized-volatility floor** in the universe filter — e.g. reject any ticker whose 60-session daily-return standard deviation is below some threshold. Tonight's scan at 0.30% catches UYSC (0.1306%) and nothing else in a 209-name held book, which suggests the threshold is separable. **This is a one-line universe filter and it is the natural sibling of the existing `MAX_PRICE_USD` and `MAX_HIST_RATIO` guards.**
3. **A SPAC name/metadata exclusion** (e.g. issuers whose name contains "Acquisition Corp"). More precise in intent, more fragile in practice, and requires a metadata source the pipeline does not currently have.

**The honest framing: option 2 is a universe-hygiene fix, not a strategy change, and it is the kind of thing that must be pre-registered and re-validated against the frozen tests before it goes anywhere near a live sleeve.** The next rebalance is **2026-09-01** and that is the deadline for a decision.

**6e. So: is there structural edge here, and does today support any new long-term-viable sleeve concept?**

**On the existing sleeves, today is evidence against three of the four families and neutral-to-positive on one.**

- **Plain momentum (`mom_v1`, `mom_v2`) — no live evidence of edge.** `mom_v1_paper` −11.10% and `mom_v2_paper` −11.57% since 2026-05-01 against `spy_benchmark_paper` +6.49%; their 07-06 twins −4.48% and −6.28% against `spy_benchmark_0701` +2.15%. **Four sleeves, two inception dates, 0-for-4.** The 2026-05-28 data audit already collapsed mom_v2's validation from "9yr + 2.4yr" to "2.4yr only"; the live forward record is now consistent with that collapse.
- **Momentum × ROA (`mom_roa_6535`) — the concentration problem is now measured, not suspected.** 44.99% in one industry. Its −7.97% since 05-01 and −4.07% since 07-06 are both dominated by that.
- **Residual momentum × ROA — the only family with a live, mechanistically-explained advantage**, and it is a *drawdown* advantage rather than a return advantage. `residual_roa_6535_paper` +4.87% since 05-01 is still 1.62pp behind `spy_benchmark_paper` (+6.49%) and 1.56pp behind QQQ (+6.43%). **Better risk, not better return, and only ~15 weeks of it.**
- **The sector-rotation sleeves are the best systematic performers in the book and get almost no attention in this journal.** `sector_top4_full_paper` is **+8.15% since 2026-05-01, third best of 76 sleeves and 1.66pp ahead of SPY**, and it fell only **−0.23%** today. It holds four sector ETFs. **A four-ETF rotation beating six single-stock factor sleeves over 15 weeks is a finding, even if the n is small and the mechanism is mostly "it was in XLE and XLV."**

**On new sleeve concepts, today supports one hypothesis and it is a construction constraint rather than a new signal.** The R²=0.914 result says the sleeves' dominant live risk is unhedged single-sector concentration produced by the ranker, not the factor itself. **A sector-capped variant — the same signal, the same top-50, with a hard cap on any one GICS sector — is the natural falsifiable test, and it is cheap: it reuses the existing backtest harness and changes one constraint.**

Two honest caveats before that becomes a plan:

1. **It is adjacent to territory the project has already closed.** Record BU (2026-07-14, pre-registered) killed the entire risk-overlay family — trend filters and vol-targeting — on clean data against both champions. **A sector cap is a portfolio-construction constraint applied at selection time, not a reactive or preemptive overlay applied to an existing book, so it is not literally inside BU's scope. But the family resemblance is close enough that it should be pre-registered with the same rigour and expected to fail.**
2. **The honest prior is that a sector cap costs return in a year where one sector led.** Semiconductors are why these sleeves were up before today; capping them would have removed the gains as well as the loss. **The testable claim is about Sharpe and drawdown, not about return, and it must be stated that way before any backtest is run or the result will be read to taste.**

**No recommendation is made here.** Today is one session. The R²=0.914 is a cross-sectional fact about one day, not a time-series fact about the strategy, and the correct next step — if there is one — is to measure how much of these sleeves' *entire live variance* since 2026-05-01 is explained by sector concentration, which is a different and much slower calculation than the one run tonight.

**6f. What today did NOT change.**

- **The 07-06 cohort is 0-for-4 against SPY across 32 sessions** and 3-of-4 behind QQQ. That record is unchanged in direction and worse in magnitude.
- **The LLM experiment remains undecided in both arms**, with the stock arm's sign flipping four times in three sessions on n=1 and the sector arm's control still ahead by ~4pp.
- **The ladder cadence question remains unresolvable in this data**, per record CW.
- **Every conclusion in this section rests on paper marks with a 5bps one-way transaction-cost assumption**, and on an indicative NAV built from a `price_cache` that is 4,345 of ~5,155 complete for today.

`verify_run --mode daily` returned **PASS (76/76 sleeves OK)** at 17:17:38, with the rebuilt record-DD check reading `ledger(12/12) drift($±0.00)` on essentially every sleeve. Four ladder rungs report a non-zero drift — `residual_w9010_2wk_paper` **$+0.65**, `residual_w9010_wk_paper` **$+0.63**, `residual_w9505_2wk_paper` **$+0.62**, `residual_w9505_wk_paper` **$+0.60** — and check (b2) is **reported, never failed** by construction, because it measures `daily_price_refresh`'s by-design nightly rewrite of a rolling 30-day window (record CK.4). Cadence check: `last_rebalance(2026-08-03/nostatus) settled_month(2026-08)`.

**Today's 07:45 `TradingMorningMTM` had not fired when this was compiled.** `var/last_morning_run.log` still ends at `2026-08-18 07:47:21` / `[OPS 2026-08-18] coverage=n/a verify=PASS`. Yesterday's morning heal *failed* on coverage (4,612 < 5,000) and the evening run did the work; 08-18 sits at **4,345** as of 17:17 last night and nothing has refreshed `price_cache` since, so that count is stale by construction and says nothing about what Yahoo has published overnight.

**0c. 3,214 open position rows, 209 distinct tickers, one without an 08-18 close.**

**0d. Two cache-gap items: one new and serious, one a retraction I owe this journal.**

*The new one — CFNB.* This ticker has appeared in these entries repeatedly as a recurring "ghost" and was declared quiet for three sessions on Monday. Pulling its actual stored history changes the picture:

```
2026-04-01   $24.60
2026-05-14   $1,578.50      <- first of 29 consecutive sessions in the $1,490-$1,697 band
2026-05-19   $1,490.00      <- low of that band
2026-06-25   $1,697.50      <- last of that band
2026-06-26   $33.95         <- and then 36 consecutive identical closes
2026-08-17   $33.95         <- most recent stored close
2026-08-18   (none)
```

Two separate defects sit on one ticker. The **29-session inflated window (2026-05-14 → 2026-06-25)** is still in `price_cache` and has not been cleaned. The **36 consecutive byte-identical $33.95 closes** (2026-06-26 → 2026-08-17) are the shape this journal spent sixteen sessions calling a "stale feed" on DMAA before that turned out to be a SPAC at trust value — but CFNB has **4,179 cached closes back to 2010-01-04** and traded at $19.01 a year ago, so the SPAC explanation is not available here.

**The important part is that neither universe filter can see the ghost.** `tradeable_universe` tests, per `trading_bot/factors/universe.py`:

- `px(as_of) >= MIN_PRICE_USD (5.0)` — $33.95 passes
- `px(as_of) <= MAX_PRICE_USD (5000.0)` — passes
- `i >= MIN_HISTORY_DAYS (252)` — 4,179 closes, passes
- `old_px = prices[i-252] >= MIN_PRICE_USD` — for a 2026-09-01 as-of that bar is **2025-08-14 at $19.01**, passes
- `px/stable <= MAX_HIST_RATIO (100)` **and** `old_px/stable <= MAX_HIST_RATIO` — stable is the 60-day median, which is $33.95; the two tested bars give ratios of **1.00** and **0.56**. Both pass.

**The test is on two endpoints. The corruption is interior.** `MAX_HIST_RATIO` was built for ARSC-class damage where the *old* endpoint is inflated, and `MAX_PRICE_USD` for BKGM-class damage where the *current* endpoint is inflated. A spike that opens and closes entirely inside the lookback is invisible to both — this is a filter-coverage gap, not a filter failure.

What consumes interior bars is `residual_momentum`, which per its own docstring takes *"daily returns over the 12-1 formation window (252 trading days ending `skip`=21 days before as_of)"*, with `LOOKBACK_TRADING_DAYS = 252` and `SKIP_TRADING_DAYS = 21`. For a 2026-09-01 as-of that window runs roughly 2025-08 → 2026-08 and **contains both the +4,700%-class bar into the ghost and the −98%-class bar out of it**. Fifty-seven of the 76 sleeves score on that factor.

**I did not run the ranker.** Ranking is a rebalance operation and this task is read-only, so whether CFNB actually lands in a top-50 is an open question, not a claim. What is established: the ghost is in the cache, the filters structurally cannot reject it, and the residual-momentum window structurally contains it. **The 09-01 rebalance is the exposure.**

*The retraction — OBNK.* Monday's and Tuesday's entries both wrote that OBNK is "unheld but rankable into 09-01." **That is wrong, and it was wrong when written.** OBNK holds **148 cached closes in total**, spanning 2025-11-03 to 2026-08-17, against `MIN_HISTORY_DAYS = 252`; and its most recent close is **$1.00** against `MIN_PRICE_USD = 5.0`. Either filter alone excludes it.

The error came from reading `check_cache_gaps`' output word as if it meant the same thing as the strategy universe. It does not — the script's own header defines it: *"rankable = tickers with a close on any of the last 3 calendar days."* That is a scan-scoping convenience, nothing more. The **23-day hole (2026-06-03..2026-07-07, window_coverage 75%) is real and still flagged**, and it remains the same defect class as the 2026-06-13 history-gap disaster; what is retracted is the claim that it can reach the portfolio.

Last night's audit, unchanged from the night before:

```
=== 2026-08-18 17:17 | cache-gap audit  window=2025-07-08..2026-08-18  trading_days=281
    rankable=5156  max_gap>5 ===
flagged: 2 of 5156 rankable tickers have an internal hole > 5 consecutive trading days.
  OBNK     worst_gap= 23d  2026-06-03..2026-07-07  window_coverage=75%
  BDPT     worst_gap=  8d  2026-03-27..2026-04-08  window_coverage=80%
```

### 3. Catalyst and macro review

**3a. Technology, 24.22% of the book — the overnight event was Korean and the US did not follow.**

South Korea's KOSPI **fell more than 6% and briefly halted trade on a sidecar** as program selling hit, with **SK Hynix −9% and Samsung Electronics −7%**, explicitly tied to the 30-year US Treasury yield hitting a 19-year high ([Seoul Economic Daily, 2026-08-19](https://en.sedaily.com/news/2026/08/19/samsung-sk-hynix-plunge-as-bond-yields-spike-kospi-drops-6); [Investing.com, 2026-08-19](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/south-koreas-kospi-briefly-halts-trade-after-5-slide-as-sk-hynix-samsung-tumble-4866353)). Korea's exposure is structural: crowded AI positioning plus the two chipmakers' index weight means a reversal in the semiconductor trade moves the whole benchmark.

US futures did not transmit it. Reads on the morning ranged from **S&P 500 futures −0.18% / Nasdaq 100 futures −0.37%** to "little changed," with the consistent detail being that **chipmakers continued to lag after Tuesday's rout** ([Benzinga, 2026-08-19](https://www.benzinga.com/markets/equities/26/08/61293924/stock-market-today-sp-500-nasdaq-100-futures-rise-as-trump-says-no-talks-are-happening-with-iran-keysight-technologies-mercury-systems-sk-hynix-in-focus)). The book's own quotes agree with the US read, not the Korean one: the worst US semi in the book is WDC at **−1.04%** against SK Hynix's −9%.

Yesterday's cause remains the operative one and it was never a demand event. The 08-18 selloff was attributed to **rising Treasury yields compressing valuations**, with **no company-specific news and no change to memory fundamentals** — the article's own framing is that higher yields *"raise the discount rate applied to future earnings, which hits hardest the stocks whose valuations lean most on distant results."* Named moves that session: **MU −5% to $962.85, SNDK −6% to $1,681.10, WDC −7% to $500.05, STX −6% to $931, SK Hynix −6%**, with the S&P 500 down 0.5% and **VIX at 14.25**. Year-to-date through 08-17: **SNDK +653%, Seagate +262%, Micron +255%, Western Digital +211%** ([24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-18](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/18/micron-technology-falls-5-sandisk-sinks-6-western-digital-drops-7-as-higher-rates-test-the-memory-boom/)).

The bear case named in coverage is worth recording plainly because it describes the book's two largest positions: gains of this magnitude embed substantial expectations, memory is cyclical and has historically given back large advances, and **higher financing costs genuinely matter for companies committing capital to new capacity** ([Invezz, 2026-08-18](https://invezz.com/news/2026/08/18/jim-cramer-says-its-not-too-late-to-invest-in-sndk-mu-stx-wdc/)).

**3e. Macro — rates, then oil, in that order of importance to this book.**

*Rates.* The **30-year Treasury topped 5.33% on 08-18, a new 19-year high**, on inflation and fiscal-spending concerns, before easing **more than 2bp to ~5.285%** ([CNBC, 2026-08-18](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/18/treasury-yields-.html)). The **10-year eased to 4.70%** on 08-19 ([Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/government-bond-yield)). This is the single macro variable that most directly prices the book: a 24.22% technology weight concentrated in names whose entire 2026 return is a multiple expansion on distant earnings.

*Fed.* **FOMC minutes for the 07-28/29 meeting release today, 2026-08-19 at 14:00 ET.** The Committee held at **3.50–3.75%** on a **9–3 vote**, with Logan, Hammack and Kashkari all dissenting in favour of a **25bp hike** — the most dissents since September 2016. The statement was little changed from June and offered **no explicit forward guidance**, consistent with Chair Warsh's aversion to signalling the path. Context going in: **July core PCE tracking ~0.2–0.3% m/m ahead of its 2026-08-26 release**, and a notably weak July payrolls report with sizeable downward revisions to prior months ([Newsquawk preview](https://www.newsquawk.com/headlines/preview-fomc-minutes-due-wednesday-19th-august-2026-at-1900bst1400edt); [CNBC, 2026-07-29](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)).

The asymmetry is worth stating: with the long end already at a 19-year high, minutes that read *more* hawkish than the statement extend exactly the move that cost the book 1.68% yesterday, while minutes that read dovish mostly confirm what is already priced. **This is a one-sided risk for a duration-heavy book.**

*Oil and Iran.* Brent climbed toward **$92 on a fourth consecutive up session**; **WTI +0.94% at $83.90**. Trump said there are **no ongoing negotiations** with Tehran and confirmed the naval blockade remains in effect; Iran said Tuesday that **the Strait of Hormuz will stay closed** until the US ends the war and meets its conditions — a hardening, not a softening, after the June 60-day memorandum expired Monday 2026-08-17. **Eight attacks on vessels transiting Hormuz, including ships linked to the UAE and Saudi Arabia, have been reported this month** ([Trading Economics, 2026-08-19](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil); [Al Jazeera, 2026-08-12](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/12/oil-prices-rise-as-attacks-dent-hopes-for-strait-of-hormuz-reopening); [CNBC, 2026-08-10](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/10/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-iran.html)).

### 6. Strategic insights

**6a. The ladder gradient collapsed to zero this morning, and that is the cleanest evidence yet for what it actually measures.**

Pre-market session slopes, all three cadences:

| Cadence | slope (pp per weight point) | r | spread |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Monthly | −0.0011 | −0.696 | 0.12pp |
| Weekly | −0.0009 | −0.609 | 0.12pp |
| Biweekly | −0.0010 | −0.638 | 0.12pp |

Compare the last three sessions of this same statistic: Friday **+0.0183 / +0.0186 / +0.0169** at r ≈ +0.93; Tuesday **−0.0197 / −0.0086 / −0.0105** at r ≈ −0.79; this morning **≈ −0.001 at 0.12pp of spread across nineteen rungs**.

Record CW established that the ladder gradient is 05-01 stock selection rather than trading, and Tuesday's entry proposed that the day-to-day gradient is semiconductor beta. **This morning tests that proposal directly and it survives.** Semis are flat overnight (the seven quoted names move −1.04% to +0.03%), and the gradient went flat with them — not weak, not noisy, but 0.12pp of dispersion across a nineteen-point weight range, an order of magnitude below either of the two prior sessions. The r-values stay meaningfully negative, which is what you would expect if the *ordering* is a stable property of the books and only the *amplitude* is the semi move.

That matters for how the ladder gets read at the 09-01 review. If the day-gradient is amplitude-modulated semiconductor exposure, then quoting a slope on any single session is quoting that session's chip tape. **The cumulative numbers are the only ones with content, and they still disagree across cadences** — monthly **+0.0155 pp/wt (r +0.333, spread 5.35pp, leader `residual_w6040_paper` +8.87%)**, weekly **−0.0221 (r −0.495, 4.85pp, leader `residual_w1585_wk_paper` +5.83%)**, biweekly **−0.0900 (r −0.836, 9.72pp, leader `residual_w0595_2wk_paper` +7.76%)**. Two of three point low-residual, one points mid-ladder, and record CW's standing caveat applies unchanged: **the 19 rungs are not 19 observations** (adjacent-rung Jaccard 0.74–0.94; w05 vs w95 shares 4 names of ~48), so no r from this structure is a significance statement.

**6b. The structural question is unchanged and the answer is still no.**

07-06 cohort, cumulative from $100,000 at pre-market prices, 33 sessions:

| Sleeve | pre-market NAV | cum. | vs SPY | vs QQQ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `spy_benchmark_0701_paper` | $102,188.26 | **+2.19%** | — | +3.02pp |
| `qqq_benchmark_0706_paper` | $99,174.07 | −0.83% | −3.02pp | — |
| `residual_roa_6535_0701_paper` | $99,463.27 | −0.54% | −2.73pp | **+0.29pp** |
| `mom_roa_6535_0701_paper` | $95,837.04 | −4.16% | −6.35pp | −3.33pp |
| `mom_v1_0701_paper` | $95,477.30 | −4.52% | −6.71pp | −3.69pp |
| `mom_v2_0701_paper` | $93,657.26 | −6.34% | −8.53pp | −5.51pp |

**Zero for four against SPY across 33 sessions.** One sleeve clears QQQ, by 0.29pp, and it is the same sleeve the 2026-06-13 revalidation named as the in-sample champion and the best held-out risk-adjusted performer (`residual_roa_6535`, held-out Sharpe 1.21, maxDD −20.1%, Calmar 1.60). That ordering has now held live for a month: **residual > mom_roa > mom_v1 > mom_v2**, which is exactly the held-out Calmar ordering, and it is the one genuinely encouraging structural signal in the cohort. It is also entirely compatible with all four sleeves simply being long a factor that is currently losing.

Two sessions this week make the dispersion problem concrete. On 08-18 `mom_roa_6535_0701` fell **−6.29%** against SPY's −0.68% because it is **44.99% semiconductors and 57.43% technology by weight**, measured from its position book. This morning the same sleeve is **−0.093%** against SPY's +0.035%. **A sleeve that is 45% one industry is not a momentum sleeve with a semiconductor tilt; it is a semiconductor sleeve with a momentum entry rule.** That is the honest characterisation of what unconstrained top-50 cross-sectional momentum produced in this regime, and no backtest in this project's history measured concentration as a risk variable — it measured return, Sharpe, drawdown and Calmar.

**6c. On new sleeve concepts, today's data supports exactly one line of thought, and it is a constraint rather than a strategy.**

The task asks whether today's data supports any long-term-viable new sleeve concept. **It mostly does not, and saying so is the useful answer.** But three things converged this morning that are worth logging as a hypothesis for later, not as a proposal:

First, **the book's healthcare weight is the only reason yesterday was −1.68% rather than −2.5%**, and that weight was not chosen — it is a residue of cross-sectional ranking. Healthcare returned +0.84% and added $16,281.69 on a day technology cost $110,158.46. This morning healthcare is again the offset. A book that arrives at a 26.58% defensive weight by accident cannot be said to be hedged; it can only be observed to have been lucky.

Second, **the concentration statistic is measurable, cheap, and already available**: `mom_roa_6535_0701`'s 44.99% single-industry weight was computed from the position book in a single query. Every sleeve in this project has one. **None of the historical validation work — not the 2026-06-13 revalidation, not the BU/BV weight sweeps, not the risk-overlay family closed on 2026-07-14 — ever measured it.**

Third, and this is the part that argues *against* acting: the risk-overlay family is already closed. Record BU established, pre-registered, that preemptive overlays (trend-200DMA, vol-target) fail on clean data against both champions, and the reactive family (stops, stop-and-reenter) died across thirteen attempts before it. **An industry-concentration cap is structurally the same species of idea** — a constraint bolted onto a working ranker to reduce a drawdown — and that species has a 0-for-many record in this project.

So the honest formulation is a **measurement question, not a sleeve**: *does the ex-ante industry Herfindahl of a top-50 momentum book predict its forward drawdown, in-sample and held-out?* That is answerable with the existing backtest harness, it is falsifiable, it costs no new data, and it produces a number whether or not anything is ever built on it. **If the answer is no, the concentration observation is retired permanently and this journal stops writing "44.99% semiconductors" as though it were a finding.** If the answer is yes, then the next question — whether a cap helps net of the momentum premium it destroys, which is exactly how the $1M ADV filter died in May (−92% of in-sample return) — is a separate and much harder one.

**No recommendation.** The 09-01 rebalance carries two live selection defects (CFNB, UYSC), and those are strictly higher priority than any new research line.

**0d. CFNB re-printed at $1,440.00 today. This morning's structural prediction was correct; its conclusion now needs revisiting.**

This morning's §0d laid out CFNB's stored history: $24.60 on 2026-04-01, then a **29-session band of $1,490.00–$1,697.50 from 2026-05-14 to 2026-06-25**, then **37 consecutive byte-identical $33.95 closes** through 2026-08-18 [corrected — see the note at the end of this entry]. Verified again tonight from `price_cache`, including the transition day:

```
2026-05-12   $31.57
2026-05-13   $31.57
2026-05-14   $1,578.50      <- first band print
2026-05-19   $1,490.00      <- band low
2026-06-25   $1,697.50      <- last band print
2026-06-26   $33.95         <- 36 identical closes begin
2026-08-17   $33.95
2026-08-18   $33.95         <- last of them (37 in total)
2026-08-19   $1,440.00      <- NEW
```

CFNB holds **4,181 cached closes** and is **held by zero sleeves**, so there is **no NAV or position impact whatsoever**.

What changed is the shape of the exposure. This morning's argument was that the corruption is *interior* to the lookback window and therefore invisible to `tradeable_universe`, whose two ratio tests (`MAX_HIST_RATIO = 100`) examine only the as-of close and the 252-day-back close against a 60-day median. **That reasoning was correct for a 09-01 as-of when the newest close was $33.95.** It is no longer the operative case. With $1,440.00 as the current endpoint, the as-of test compares $1,440 against a 60-day median still near $33.95, giving a ratio of roughly **42** — **under the threshold of 100, so it still passes**, and `MAX_PRICE_USD` (5,000) passes it too. The filter tightens and does not close.

**I did not run the ranker.** Ranking is a rebalance operation and this task is read-only. What is established tonight and what is not:

- **Established:** the ghost band is still in the cache, uncleaned; a new band-level print landed on 08-19; `check_anomalies` caught this one precisely because it is an endpoint move against yesterday, which is the class the interior band was not; and CFNB is held by nothing.
- **Not established:** whether CFNB clears `tradeable_universe` on a 2026-09-01 as-of, and whether `residual_momentum` — which regresses daily returns over the 252-day window ending 21 days before as-of, and which 57 of 76 sleeves score on — ranks it into a top-50. **The 09-01 rebalance remains the exposure and it is eight trading days away.**

One more thing worth stating plainly: this morning's entry was written before today's print and predicted the mechanism correctly. Tonight's print confirms the mechanism, not the specific conclusion. **The journal should not carry "invisible to both filters" forward as settled** — the endpoint case is different from the interior case, and only the interior case was analyzed.

Deutsche Bank read the surprise buyback boost as unease at the Treasury over long-end yields — "soft financial repression" in their phrase — rather than a routine operation.

**Sector dispersion was extreme, and both tails are directly in this book.** Healthcare was the best S&P sector and set a record high; chip equipment was the worst pocket in the market.

**The named cause is AI-capex repricing and the evidence for it is the yield move.** 24/7 Wall St. states it directly: equipment stocks selling into a falling-yield tailwind "points to AI capex repricing rather than a rates problem." Two dated inputs:

1. **Anthropic told investors its annualized run rate reached $65 billion at end-July** — up from $47B in May and $9B at end-2025 — with **2028 projected revenue of $190–200 billion**, which the article says landed **below some investor projections** ([CNBC, 2026-08-17](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/17/anthropic-says-annualized-revenue-climbed-to-65-billion-in-july.html); [Axios, 2026-08-17](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/17/anthropic-revenue-run-rate-ipo-openai)). OpenAI's run rate is cited at ~$40B.
2. **The WSJ ~$3 trillion off-balance-sheet AI-commitment analysis** across nine tech companies, which was 08-18's catalyst and remained the frame today.

Cited intraday levels versus the book's stored closes, which differ because the article was written midday:

**STX is the book's single largest loss and the largest position in the semi complex by sleeve count (66).** TradingKey reports STX **−6.52% on 08-19** attributing it to "profit-taking and insider selling disclosures," against the book's stored **−7.87%** ([TradingKey, 2026-08-19](https://www.tradingkey.com/news/market-movers/262118741-market-movers-stx-20260819)); the discrepancy is a different price base, not a contradiction of direction. STX's fundamentals are not in question — fiscal Q4/2026 revenue **+48.5% y/y to $3.63B** and adjusted EPS **$5.71** — which is exactly the pattern the wires describe across AI hardware: names beating estimates and selling anyway.

**On the semiconductor index itself, the equipment move did not show up cleanly.** SOXX traded at $522.49 and was **+77% YTD through Tuesday's close**; the article's own explanation is that SOXX blends designers, manufacturers and equipment suppliers, which dilutes equipment-specific moves. **The book has no such dilution — it is long the equipment tail directly.**

**3b. Healthcare, and the Moderna print the book almost entirely missed.**

**Moderna closed $174.38, +176.97% from $62.96** — verified in `price_cache`, and verified as a real event, not a split artifact or a stale-feed ghost. It did not trip `check_anomalies` because the held-name threshold is >300%.

Two dated catalysts, both 2026-08-19:

1. **The Phase 3 melanoma-recurrence trial with Merck met its primary endpoint** — the personalized mRNA cancer therapy cut the risk of recurrence and spread in high-risk melanoma patients. Moderna described it as **the first positive Phase 3 results for an mRNA-based cancer therapy**, which is the reason the move is a platform revaluation and not a single-product event.
2. **The FDA cleared mFLUSIVA**, Moderna's flu vaccine for adults 50+, its fifth global product and fourth FDA-approved therapy, with a US launch targeted at the 2026–27 season.

Volume was **185.1M shares, roughly 1,819% above the three-month average of 9.6M**; market cap went from **$25B to $69B**. **Merck +11.2%** was the largest positive contributor to the Dow; **BioNTech +21%**, **Novavax +6%** ([Motley Fool via Yahoo Finance, 2026-08-19](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/stock-market-today-aug-19-212102683.html); [StockStory](https://stockstory.org/us/stocks/nasdaq/mrna/news/why-up-down/why-is-moderna-mrna-stock-rocketing-higher-today-4); [Schaeffer's, 2026-08-19](https://www.schaeffersresearch.com/content/news/2026/08/19/moderna-stock-eyes-best-day-ever-after-cancer-vaccine-breakthrough); [24/7 Wall St., 2026-08-19](https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/08/19/moderna-rockets-93-merck-jumps-7-as-melanoma-therapy-meets-primary-goal-in-phase-3-trial/)).

**What the book got out of it: $3,288.92.** MRNA is held by **two sleeves only — `mom_v1_paper` and `mom_v1_0701_paper`** — at a combined **$5,147.38, which is 0.07% of held value**. Both are the top-100 sleeve, whose whole design premise is breadth; on a 100-name equal-weight book a name that nearly triples adds about **1pp** to that sleeve, and `mom_v1_paper` in fact returned **−0.206%** on the day because its semiconductor names took more away. **This is worth recording as a structural observation and not a complaint: a top-50 sleeve would have missed it entirely, and a top-100 sleeve captured 1% of its portfolio nearly tripling and still finished down.** Single-name tail events do not rescue a book that is short the wrong sector.

**3e. Macro: oil is up a fifth straight session and energy went nowhere.**

**Brent gained 1% to $91.91 and WTI rose 1.1% to $84.99 early on 08-19.** Trump reiterated there are **no ongoing negotiations with Tehran** and confirmed the **US naval blockade remains in effect**; **eight attacks on vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz — including ships linked to the UAE and Saudi Arabia — have been reported this month** ([Al Jazeera, 2026-08-12](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/12/oil-prices-rise-as-attacks-dent-hopes-for-strait-of-hormuz-reopening); [Trading Economics](https://tradingeconomics.com/commodity/brent-crude-oil); [CNBC, 2026-08-10](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/10/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-iran.html)).

**The book's energy sleeve did not respond.** Energy is **6.46% of held value** and returned **−0.03%, −$149.21**; **XLE fell −0.16% to $63.58**. That breaks a two-session pattern in which XLE was the book's best ETF read — a fifth straight up session in crude produced nothing at the equity level, which is worth noting because the pre-market entry leaned on XLE both yesterday and today.

**The FOMC minutes were the scheduled event and were hawkish.** From the July 28–29 record: **many participants assessed that higher rates would likely be necessary if inflation did not fall**; price pressures were characterised as broad-based; **nominal Treasury yields rose 25–30bp over the intermeeting period, driven by real rates**, while short-term inflation compensation declined on indexation-lag technicals. The meeting held at **3.50–3.75%** with **three dissents for a 25bp hike** (Logan, Hammack, Kashkari) ([Federal Reserve minutes, July 28–29 2026](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/fomcminutes20260729.htm); [InvestingLive, 2026-08-19](https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fomc-minutes-many-participants-assessed-higher-rates-would-likely-be-necessary-if-inflation-did-not-fall/); [CNBC, 2026-07-29](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-meeting-today-live-updates.html)).

**The market ignored it, and that is the read that matters.** A hawkish minutes release landed at 14:00 ET and yields *fell* 5–9bp anyway, because the Treasury's buyback announcement dominated. **For a book that is 23.60% long-duration technology, the supply-side intervention outweighed the policy signal today.** Whether that holds through Jackson Hole (2026-08-27–29, Warsh's first keynote 08-28) is the open question, and it lands one trading day before the 09-01 rebalance.

**Ranking today: cash (0.000%) > cascade (−0.039%) > control (−6.639%).** The cash treatment leads for the first time since 08-11 — and to be precise about what this is and is not: **the cascade has closed below par on 12 prior days** (07-15, 07-16, 07-17, 07-20, 07-24, 07-29 among them, low **$87,545.11 on 07-29**, most recently 08-11), so today is the **13th**, not the first. **This arm has crossed above and below the cash treatment repeatedly over 33 sessions on a single name. It has no signal in it yet and this journal should stop narrating each crossing as an event.**

### 6. Ladder gradient and structural read

**6a. The day-gradient is the tightest negative reading this journal has recorded, and the monthly cumulative slope flipped sign.**

Least-squares fit of day return (pp) against residual-momentum weight (5 → 95), 19 rungs per cadence:

| Cadence | Day slope (pp/wt) | r | Cumulative slope | r | Spread | Leader |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Monthly | **−0.0326** | **−0.969** | **−0.0177** | −0.366 | 4.98pp | `residual_w6040_paper` +8.23% |
| Weekly | **−0.0259** | **−0.987** | **−0.0480** | −0.775 | 6.33pp | `residual_w1585_wk_paper` +6.70% |
| Biweekly | **−0.0258** | **−0.989** | **−0.1155** | −0.887 | 11.76pp | `residual_w0595_2wk_paper` +8.84% |

Four sessions of day-slopes, alongside the semiconductor complex:

| Session | Monthly | Weekly | Biweekly | Semi complex |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| 08-14 (Fri) | +0.0183 | +0.0186 | +0.0169 | up |
| 08-18 (Tue) | −0.0197 | −0.0086 | −0.0105 | down hard |
| 08-19 pre-mkt | ~−0.001 | ~−0.001 | ~−0.001 | flat |
| **08-19 (close)** | **−0.0326** | **−0.0259** | **−0.0258** | **down hard** |

**The sign has matched the semiconductor complex in all four readings, and today's r-values (−0.969 / −0.987 / −0.989) leave essentially no residual variance to attribute to anything else.** This is now the strongest single piece of evidence for the position this journal reached on 08-18: **the ladder's day-gradient measures semiconductor beta, not a factor.** High-residual-weight rungs hold more semis, so they swing with them symmetrically in both directions.

**The monthly cumulative slope flipped from +0.0167 to −0.0177 in one session.** All three cadences are now negatively sloped since inception. **This is not a finding and should not be reported as one**, for the reasons record CW established and which today illustrates cleanly:

- **A single session moved a cumulative slope across zero.** The monthly cumulative slope changed by −0.0344 today, which is arithmetically the day slope. If one session can flip the sign of a 15-week cumulative measure, the cumulative measure carries almost no information.
- **The 19 rungs are not 19 observations.** Adjacent-rung Jaccard overlap is 0.74–0.94; w05 vs w95 share 4 names of ~48. It is a dose-response curve between two near-disjoint portfolios sampled once. **The r-values above must never be read as significance.**
- The window is still replay-seeded (05-01 → 07-16 deterministic, not live fills); live forward began 07-01 monthly / 07-13 weekly / 07-06 biweekly.

### 7. Strategic read

**7a. What today's data says about structural edge — and it is not encouraging, for a specific reason.**

The 07-06 cohort now trails **both** benchmarks on all four systematic sleeves after 33 sessions. That is a short window and forward-OOS by construction, so it is not a verdict. But today added a mechanism, and mechanisms matter more than 33 days of return:

**The book's sector concentration is not a chosen exposure — it is an artifact of when the ranker last ran.** All four systematic sleeves and all 57 ladder sleeves last rebalanced 2026-08-03. Momentum measured on 12-1 formation windows ending late July selected the semiconductor and memory complex, because that complex was the best-performing group in the market at the time. **Sixteen days later the same complex is being repriced by an AI-capex narrative, and the portfolio has no mechanism to respond until 09-01.** Today it cost 266% of the net loss.

That is the structural criticism of monthly momentum stated in its most concrete form available: **the factor's holding period is 21 trading days and the regime's turn took two.** The BU/BV work already closed the reactive-and-preemptive risk-overlay family as a fix (trend-200DMA worse than nothing, vol-target a no-op), so the answer is not an overlay. What today's data supports is narrower and more useful: **the loss is arriving through sector concentration, not through individual name selection.** Breadth was 92 up / 112 down — close to even — and the book still lost, because the down names were clustered and heavy.

**7b. Is there a long-term-viable sleeve concept in today's data? One is suggested and one is contradicted.**

**Suggested — sector-neutralised residual momentum.** The ladder decomposition (record CW) already established the whole gradient is 05-01 stock selection rather than trading, and today shows what that selection actually is: a semiconductor bet with a factor label. A sleeve that ranks on the same residual-momentum/ROA blend but caps per-sector weight — say at index weight plus a fixed band — would test whether the residual-momentum signal has content independent of the sector it happens to be pointing at. **This is a real hypothesis with a clean falsification: if sector-capped residual momentum performs the same as uncapped, the signal is genuinely stock-level; if it performs materially better or worse, the sleeve was a sector timer all along.** It also has a pre-registrable in-sample/held-out design and requires no new data. **I am not recommending building it** — the roadmap's open item is M6's live `slippage_log` write, which is Evan's, and adding a sleeve while 76 are running is a scope decision, not a data decision.

**Contradicted — anything relying on single-name tail capture.** Moderna nearly tripled today. Two sleeves held it, at 0.07% of the book, and the sleeve that held it still finished down. **The top-100 breadth premise was maximally rewarded today and produced −0.206%.** Any concept whose thesis is "wide enough to catch the outlier" now has a dated counterexample in this book's own record: catching the outlier is not sufficient when the concentrated loss is 3x larger than the outlier's contribution. The LLM stock arm makes the same point from the opposite end — **33 sessions, n=1 name, and the treatment has crossed the control's line so many times that no reading of it is stable.**

**7c. What would change the read.**

Three dated events in the next seven trading days, all before the 09-01 rebalance:

1. **NVDA earnings, 2026-08-26 after the close**, same day as July core PCE. The book is 23.60% technology and 16.45% semis. This is the single largest scheduled risk to the current book.
2. **Jackson Hole, 2026-08-27–29, Warsh's first keynote 08-28.** Today demonstrated that a supply-side Treasury intervention can override a hawkish Fed signal; Jackson Hole tests whether that holds.
3. **The 09-01 rebalance itself**, which is the first opportunity for the ranker to see the memory/semicap drawdown and act on it — and which carries the unresolved CFNB question from §0d.
